Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.

Majjhimanikāyo

The Middle-Length Discourses

Mūlapaṇṇāsapāḷi

The Root Fifty

1. Mūlapariyāyavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Root Exposition

1. Mūlapariyāyasuttaṃ

1. The Root Exposition

1. Evaṃ [M 1.0001][V 1.0001][P 1.0001][T 1.0001] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā ukkaṭṭhāyaṃ viharati subhagavane sālarājamūle. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “sabbadhammamūlapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

1. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Ukkaṭṭhā in the Subhaga Grove at the foot of a majestic sāla tree. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the exposition that is the root of all things. Listen and pay close attention, I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

2. “Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido [V 1.0002] ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – pathaviṃ paṭhaviṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pathavito sañjānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito saññatvā pathaviṃ maññati, pathaviyā maññati, pathavito maññati, pathaviṃ meti maññati[T 1.0002], pathaviṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

2. “Here, bhikkhus, an uninstructed ordinary person—who has not seen the noble ones, is unskilled in the noble Dhamma, and untrained in the noble Dhamma; who has not seen true individuals, is unskilled in the Dhamma of true individuals, and untrained in the Dhamma of true individuals—perceives earth as earth. Having perceived earth as earth, he conceives earth, he conceives in regard to earth, he conceives in relation to earth, he conceives, ‘Earth is mine,’ and he delights in earth. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Āpaṃ āpato sañjānāti; āpaṃ āpato saññatvā āpaṃ maññati, āpasmiṃ maññati, āpato maññati, āpaṃ meti maññati, āpaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives water as water. Having perceived water as water, he conceives water, he conceives in regard to water, he conceives in relation to water, he conceives, ‘Water is mine,’ and he delights in water. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Tejaṃ [M 1.0002] tejato sañjānāti; tejaṃ tejato saññatvā tejaṃ maññati, tejasmiṃ maññati, tejato maññati, tejaṃ meti maññati, tejaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives fire as fire. Having perceived fire as fire, he conceives fire, he conceives in regard to fire, he conceives in relation to fire, he conceives, ‘Fire is mine,’ and he delights in fire. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Vāyaṃ vāyato sañjānāti; vāyaṃ vāyato saññatvā vāyaṃ maññati, vāyasmiṃ maññati, vāyato maññati, vāyaṃ meti maññati, vāyaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti [P 1.0002] vadāmi.

“He perceives air as air. Having perceived air as air, he conceives air, he conceives in regard to air, he conceives in relation to air, he conceives, ‘Air is mine,’ and he delights in air. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

3. “Bhūte bhūtato sañjānāti; bhūte bhūtato saññatvā bhūte maññati, bhūtesu maññati, bhūtato maññati, bhūte meti maññati, bhūte abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

3. “He perceives beings as beings. Having perceived beings as beings, he conceives beings, he conceives in regard to beings, he conceives in relation to beings, he conceives, ‘Beings are mine,’ and he delights in beings. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Deve devato sañjānāti; deve devato saññatvā deve maññati, devesu maññati, devato maññati, deve meti maññati, deve abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives gods as gods. Having perceived gods as gods, he conceives gods, he conceives in regard to gods, he conceives in relation to gods, he conceives, ‘Gods are mine,’ and he delights in gods. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Pajāpatiṃ pajāpatito sañjānāti; pajāpatiṃ pajāpatito saññatvā pajāpatiṃ maññati, pajāpatismiṃ maññati, pajāpatito maññati, pajāpatiṃ meti maññati, pajāpatiṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives Pajāpati as Pajāpati. Having perceived Pajāpati as Pajāpati, he conceives Pajāpati, he conceives in regard to Pajāpati, he conceives in relation to Pajāpati, he conceives, ‘Pajāpati is mine,’ and he delights in Pajāpati. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Brahmaṃ [V 1.0003] brahmato sañjānāti; brahmaṃ brahmato saññatvā brahmaṃ maññati[T 1.0003], brahmasmiṃ maññati, brahmato maññati, brahmaṃ meti maññati, brahmaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives Brahmā as Brahmā. Having perceived Brahmā as Brahmā, he conceives Brahmā, he conceives in regard to Brahmā, he conceives in relation to Brahmā, he conceives, ‘Brahmā is mine,’ and he delights in Brahmā. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Ābhassare ābhassarato sañjānāti; ābhassare ābhassarato saññatvā ābhassare maññati, ābhassaresu maññati, ābhassarato maññati, ābhassare meti maññati, ābhassare abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the Radiant Gods as the Radiant Gods. Having perceived the Radiant Gods as the Radiant Gods, he conceives the Radiant Gods, he conceives in regard to the Radiant Gods, he conceives in relation to the Radiant Gods, he conceives, ‘The Radiant Gods are mine,’ and he delights in the Radiant Gods. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Subhakiṇhe subhakiṇhato sañjānāti; subhakiṇhe subhakiṇhato saññatvā subhakiṇhe maññati, subhakiṇhesu maññati, subhakiṇhato maññati, subhakiṇhe meti maññati, subhakiṇhe abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the Gods of Refulgent Glory as the Gods of Refulgent Glory. Having perceived the Gods of Refulgent Glory as the Gods of Refulgent Glory, he conceives the Gods of Refulgent Glory, he conceives in regard to the Gods of Refulgent Glory, he conceives in relation to the Gods of Refulgent Glory, he conceives, ‘The Gods of Refulgent Glory are mine,’ and he delights in the Gods of Refulgent Glory. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Vehapphale [M 1.0003] vehapphalato sañjānāti; vehapphale vehapphalato saññatvā vehapphale maññati, vehapphalesu maññati, vehapphalato maññati, vehapphale meti maññati, vehapphale abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the Gods of Great Reward as the Gods of Great Reward. Having perceived the Gods of Great Reward as the Gods of Great Reward, he conceives the Gods of Great Reward, he conceives in regard to the Gods of Great Reward, he conceives in relation to the Gods of Great Reward, he conceives, ‘The Gods of Great Reward are mine,’ and he delights in the Gods of Great Reward. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Abhibhuṃ abhibhūto sañjānāti; abhibhuṃ abhibhūto saññatvā abhibhuṃ maññati, abhibhusmiṃ maññati, abhibhūto maññati, abhibhuṃ meti maññati, abhibhuṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the Conqueror as the Conqueror. Having perceived the Conqueror as the Conqueror, he conceives the Conqueror, he conceives in regard to the Conqueror, he conceives in relation to the Conqueror, he conceives, ‘The Conqueror is mine,’ and he delights in the Conqueror. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

4. “Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanato sañjānāti; ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanato saññatvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanasmiṃ maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanato maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ meti maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ [T 1.0004] kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

4. “He perceives the base of infinite space as the base of infinite space. Having perceived the base of infinite space as the base of infinite space, he conceives the base of infinite space, he conceives in regard to the base of infinite space, he conceives in relation to the base of infinite space, he conceives, ‘The base of infinite space is mine,’ and he delights in the base of infinite space. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanato sañjānāti; viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanato saññatvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ [P 1.0003] maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanasmiṃ maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanato [V 1.0004] maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ meti maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the base of infinite consciousness as the base of infinite consciousness. Having perceived the base of infinite consciousness as the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives in regard to the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives in relation to the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives, ‘The base of infinite consciousness is mine,’ and he delights in the base of infinite consciousness. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.

“Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanato sañjānāti; ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanato saññatvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanasmiṃ maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanato maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ meti maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

“He perceives the base of nothingness as the base of nothingness. Having perceived the base of nothingness as the base of nothingness, he conceives the base of nothingness, he conceives in regard to the base of nothingness, he conceives in relation to the base of nothingness, he conceives, ‘The base of nothingness is mine,’ and he delights in the base of nothingness. For what reason? Because it is not fully comprehended by him, I say.”

“Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato sañjānāti; nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato saññatvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasmiṃ maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ meti maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; having perceived the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives from the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives ‘the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is mine,’ and he delights in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

5. “Diṭṭhaṃ [M 1.0004] diṭṭhato sañjānāti; diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhato saññatvā diṭṭhaṃ maññati, diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati, diṭṭhato maññati, diṭṭhaṃ meti maññati, diṭṭhaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

5. He perceives the seen as the seen; having perceived the seen as the seen, he conceives the seen, he conceives in the seen, he conceives from the seen, he conceives ‘the seen is mine,’ and he delights in the seen. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Sutaṃ sutato sañjānāti; sutaṃ sutato saññatvā sutaṃ [T 1.0005] maññati, sutasmiṃ maññati, sutato maññati, sutaṃ meti maññati, sutaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives the heard as the heard; having perceived the heard as the heard, he conceives the heard, he conceives in the heard, he conceives from the heard, he conceives ‘the heard is mine,’ and he delights in the heard. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Mutaṃ mutato sañjānāti; mutaṃ mutato saññatvā mutaṃ maññati, mutasmiṃ maññati, mutato maññati, mutaṃ meti maññati, mutaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives the sensed as the sensed; having perceived the sensed as the sensed, he conceives the sensed, he conceives in the sensed, he conceives from the sensed, he conceives ‘the sensed is mine,’ and he delights in the sensed. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Viññātaṃ viññātato sañjānāti; viññātaṃ viññātato saññatvā viññātaṃ maññati, viññātasmiṃ maññati, viññātato maññati, viññātaṃ meti maññati, viññātaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives the cognized as the cognized; having perceived the cognized as the cognized, he conceives the cognized, he conceives in the cognized, he conceives from the cognized, he conceives ‘the cognized is mine,’ and he delights in the cognized. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

6. “Ekattaṃ [V 1.0005] ekattato sañjānāti; ekattaṃ ekattato saññatvā ekattaṃ maññati, ekattasmiṃ maññati, ekattato maññati, ekattaṃ meti maññati, ekattaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

6. He perceives oneness as oneness; having perceived oneness as oneness, he conceives oneness, he conceives in oneness, he conceives from oneness, he conceives ‘oneness is mine,’ and he delights in oneness. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Nānattaṃ nānattato sañjānāti; nānattaṃ nānattato saññatvā nānattaṃ maññati, nānattasmiṃ maññati, nānattato maññati, nānattaṃ meti maññati, nānattaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives diversity as diversity; having perceived diversity as diversity, he conceives diversity, he conceives in diversity, he conceives from diversity, he conceives ‘diversity is mine,’ and he delights in diversity. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Sabbaṃ sabbato sañjānāti; sabbaṃ sabbato saññatvā sabbaṃ maññati, sabbasmiṃ [P 1.0004] maññati, sabbato maññati, sabbaṃ meti maññati, sabbaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives all as all; having perceived all as all, he conceives all, he conceives in all, he conceives from all, he conceives ‘all is mine,’ and he delights in all. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

“Nibbānaṃ nibbānato sañjānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato saññatvā nibbānaṃ maññati, nibbānasmiṃ maññati[T 1.0006], nibbānato maññati, nibbānaṃ meti maññati, nibbānaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

He perceives Nibbāna as Nibbāna; having perceived Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he conceives Nibbāna, he conceives in Nibbāna, he conceives from Nibbāna, he conceives ‘Nibbāna is mine,’ and he delights in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.

Puthujjanavasena paṭhamanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the ground of the first method, concerning the ordinary person, is concluded.

7. “Yopi [M 1.0005] so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkho sekho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) appattamānaso anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamāno viharati, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya abhiññatvā (ka.) pathaviṃ mā maññi vā maññati, pathaviyā mā maññi, pathavito mā maññi, pathaviṃ meti mā maññi, pathaviṃ mābhinandi vā abhinandati (sī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññeyyaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

7. Bhikkhus, whatever monk is a learner, who has not yet reached his goal, and dwells aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage, he too directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, let him not conceive earth, let him not conceive in earth, let him not conceive from earth, let him not conceive ‘earth is mine,’ and let him not delight in earth. For what reason? Because it should be fully understood by him, I say.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya [V 1.0006] nibbānaṃ mā maññi, nibbānasmiṃ mā maññi, nibbānato mā maññi, nibbānaṃ meti mā maññi, nibbānaṃ mābhinandi. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññeyyaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Radiant Ones... the Gods of Refulgent Glory... the Gods of Great Fruit... the Overlord... the base of infinite space... the base of infinite consciousness... the base of nothingness... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... oneness... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, let him not conceive Nibbāna, let him not conceive in Nibbāna, let him not conceive from Nibbāna, let him not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and let him not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because it should be fully understood by him, I say.

Sekkhavasena satthāravasena (sī.), satthuvasena (syā. ka.) dutiyanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the ground of the second method, concerning the learner, is concluded.

8. “Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito [T 1.0007] abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

8. Bhikkhus, whatever monk is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of being, and is liberated through perfect knowledge—he too directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because it has been fully understood by him, I say.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Radiant Ones... the Gods of Refulgent Glory... the Gods of Great Fruit... the Overlord... the base of infinite space... the base of infinite consciousness... the base of nothingness... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... oneness... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because it has been fully understood by him, I say.

Khīṇāsavavasena tatiyanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the ground of the third method, concerning one whose taints are destroyed, is concluded.

9. “Yopi [M 1.0006] so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito [P 1.0005] abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā rāgassa, vītarāgattā.

9. O monks, that monk who is an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what was to be done, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are completely destroyed, and who is liberated through right understanding—he too directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because of the destruction of lust, because of being without lust.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ [V 1.0007]… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ [T 1.0008]… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā rāgassa, vītarāgattā.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Ābhassara gods... the Subhakiṇha gods... the Vehapphala gods... the Abhibhū... the dimension of infinite space... the dimension of infinite consciousness... the dimension of nothingness... the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... unity... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive of Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because of the destruction of lust, because of being without lust.

Khīṇāsavavasena catutthanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the fourth methodical ground, by way of the one whose taints are destroyed, is concluded.

10. “Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā dosassa, vītadosattā.

10. O monks, that monk who is an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what was to be done, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are completely destroyed, and who is liberated through right understanding—he too directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because of the destruction of aversion, because of being without aversion.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā dosassa, vītadosattā.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Ābhassara gods... the Subhakiṇha gods... the Vehapphala gods... the Abhibhū... the dimension of infinite space... the dimension of infinite consciousness... the dimension of nothingness... the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... unity... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive of Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because of the destruction of aversion, because of being without aversion.

Khīṇāsavavasena pañcamanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the fifth methodical ground, by way of the one whose taints are destroyed, is concluded.

11. “Yopi [T 1.0009][M 1.0007] so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā mohassa, vītamohattā.

11. O monks, that monk who is an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what was to be done, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are completely destroyed, and who is liberated through right understanding—he too directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because of the destruction of delusion, because of being without delusion.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ [V 1.0008]… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā mohassa, vītamohattā.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Ābhassara gods... the Subhakiṇha gods... the Vehapphala gods... the Abhibhū... the dimension of infinite space... the dimension of infinite consciousness... the dimension of nothingness... the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... unity... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive of Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because of the destruction of delusion, because of being without delusion.

Khīṇāsavavasena chaṭṭhanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the sixth methodical ground, by way of the one whose taints are destroyed, is concluded.

12. “Tathāgatopi, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati[P 1.0006]. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātantaṃ tathāgatassā’ti vadāmi.

12. O monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, also directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because, I say, that has been fully comprehended by the Tathāgata.

“Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ [T 1.0010]… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātantaṃ tathāgatassā’ti vadāmi.

Water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Ābhassara gods... the Subhakiṇha gods... the Vehapphala gods... the Abhibhū... the dimension of infinite space... the dimension of infinite consciousness... the dimension of nothingness... the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... unity... diversity... all... Nibbāna—he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive of Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' and he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because, I say, that has been fully comprehended by the Tathāgata.

Tathāgatavasena sattamanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The section on the seventh methodical ground, by way of the Tathāgata, is concluded.

13. “Tathāgatopi[M 1.0008], bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Nandī nandi (sī. syā.) dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā ‘bhavā jāti bhūtassa jarāmaraṇa’nti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘tathāgato sabbaso taṇhānaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti vadāmi.

13. O monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, also directly knows earth as earth. Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. For what reason? Because of knowing, 'Delight is the root of suffering,' and 'From existence comes birth; for a being that has come to be, there is aging and death.' Therefore, O monks, I declare that the Tathāgata, through the utter destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishment of all cravings, is fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

“Āpaṃ [V 1.0009] …pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ [T 1.0011] kissa hetu? ‘Nandī dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā ‘bhavā jāti bhūtassa jarāmaraṇa’nti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘tathāgato sabbaso taṇhānaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti vadāmī”ti.

He directly knows water... fire... air... beings... gods... Pajāpati... Brahmā... the Ābhassara gods... the Subhakiṇha gods... the Vehapphala gods... the Abhibhū... the dimension of infinite space... the dimension of infinite consciousness... the dimension of nothingness... the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception... the seen... the heard... the sensed... the cognized... oneness... diversity... all... Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive 'Nibbāna is mine,' he does not delight in Nibbāna. For what reason? Because he has understood: 'Delight is the root of suffering,' and 'For a being that has come to be from becoming, there is aging and death.' Therefore, monks, I say that through the utter destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishment of all cravings, the Tathāgata is fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Tathāgatavasena aṭṭhamanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

The eighth section on the grounds of the method in terms of the Tathāgata is concluded.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Na te bhikkhū na attamanā tebhikkhū (syā.), te bhikkhū (pī. ka.) bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Those monks did not rejoice in the Blessed One's words.

Mūlapariyāyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first discourse, the Root of All Things, is concluded.

2. Sabbāsavasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on All Taints

14. Evaṃ [T 1.0012][V 1.0010] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “sabbāsavasaṃvarapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha[M 1.0009][P 1.0007], sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

14. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks.' 'Venerable sir,' those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: 'Monks, I will teach you the method for the restraint of all taints. Listen to it, pay close attention, and I will speak.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

15. “Jānato ahaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato. Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiñca passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi? Yoniso ca manasikāraṃ ayoniso ca manasikāraṃ. Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppannā ceva āsavā uppajjanti, uppannā ca āsavā pavaḍḍhanti; yoniso ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppannā ceva āsavā na uppajjanti, uppannā ca āsavā pahīyanti.

15. Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see. And what, monks, does one know and see for the destruction of the taints? Proper attention and improper attention. For one who attends improperly, monks, unarisen taints arise, and arisen taints increase. But for one who attends properly, monks, unarisen taints do not arise, and arisen taints are abandoned.

16. “Atthi, bhikkhave, āsavā dassanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā.

16. Monks, there are taints to be abandoned by seeing, there are taints to be abandoned by restraint, there are taints to be abandoned by using, there are taints to be abandoned by enduring, there are taints to be abandoned by avoiding, there are taints to be abandoned by dispelling, and there are taints to be abandoned by developing.

Dassanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Seeing

17. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā dassanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave[T 1.0013], assutavā puthujjano – ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – manasikaraṇīye dhamme nappajānāti, amanasikaraṇīye dhamme nappajānāti. So manasikaraṇīye dhamme appajānanto amanasikaraṇīye dhamme appajānanto, ye dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā, te dhamme manasi karoti, ye dhammā manasikaraṇīyā te dhamme na manasi karoti.

17. And what, monks, are the taints to be abandoned by seeing? Here, monks, an uninstructed ordinary person—who has not seen the noble ones, is unskilled in the Dhamma of the noble ones, and is undisciplined in the Dhamma of the noble ones; who has not seen the good persons, is unskilled in the Dhamma of the good persons, and is undisciplined in the Dhamma of the good persons—does not know the things that should be attended to and does not know the things that should not be attended to. Not knowing the things that should be attended to and not knowing the things that should not be attended to, he attends to those things that should not be attended to, and he does not attend to those things that should be attended to.

“Katame [V 1.0011] ca, bhikkhave, dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme manasi karoti? Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pavaḍḍhati; anuppanno vā bhavāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā bhavāsavo pavaḍḍhati; anuppanno vā avijjāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā avijjāsavo pavaḍḍhati – ime dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme manasi karoti.

And what, monks, are those things that should not be attended to, which he attends to? Monks, when he attends to certain things, the unarisen taint of sensual desire arises in him, and the arisen taint of sensual desire increases; the unarisen taint of becoming arises, and the arisen taint of becoming increases; the unarisen taint of ignorance arises, and the arisen taint of ignorance increases. These are the things that should not be attended to, which he attends to.

“Katame [M 1.0010] ca, bhikkhave, dhammā manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme na manasi karoti? Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pahīyati; anuppanno vā bhavāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā bhavāsavo pahīyati; anuppanno vā avijjāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā avijjāsavo pahīyati – ime dhammā manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme na manasi karoti.

And what, monks, are those things that should be attended to, which he does not attend to? Monks, when he attends to certain things, the unarisen taint of sensual desire does not arise in him, and the arisen taint of sensual desire is abandoned; the unarisen taint of becoming does not arise, and the arisen taint of becoming is abandoned; the unarisen taint of ignorance does not arise, and the arisen taint of ignorance is abandoned. These are the things that should be attended to, which he does not attend to.

“Tassa amanasikaraṇīyānaṃ [P 1.0008] dhammānaṃ manasikārā manasikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ amanasikārā anuppannā ceva āsavā uppajjanti uppannā ca āsavā [T 1.0014] pavaḍḍhanti.

For him, through attending to things that should not be attended to and through not attending to things that should be attended to, unarisen taints arise, and arisen taints increase.

18. “So evaṃ ayoniso manasi karoti – ‘ahosiṃ nu kho ahaṃ atītamaddhānaṃ? Na nu kho ahosiṃ atītamaddhānaṃ? Kiṃ nu kho ahosiṃ atītamaddhānaṃ? Kathaṃ nu kho ahosiṃ atītamaddhānaṃ? Kiṃ hutvā kiṃ ahosiṃ nu kho ahaṃ atītamaddhānaṃ? Bhavissāmi nu kho ahaṃ anāgatamaddhānaṃ? Na nu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṃ? Kiṃ nu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṃ? Kathaṃ nu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṃ? Kiṃ hutvā kiṃ bhavissāmi nu kho ahaṃ anāgatamaddhāna’nti? Etarahi vā paccuppannamaddhānaṃ paccuppannamaddhānaṃ ārabbha (syā.) ajjhattaṃ kathaṃkathī hoti – ‘ahaṃ nu khosmi? No nu khosmi? Kiṃ nu khosmi? Kathaṃ nu khosmi? Ayaṃ nu kho satto kuto āgato? So kuhiṃ gāmī bhavissatī’ti?

18. He attends unwisely in this way: ‘Did I exist in the past? Did I not exist in the past? What was I in the past? How was I in the past? Having been what, what did I become in the past?’ ‘Will I exist in the future? Will I not exist in the future? What will I be in the future? How will I be in the future? Having been what, what will I become in the future?’ Or now, concerning the present time, he is inwardly perplexed: ‘Am I? Am I not? What am I? How am I? From where has this being come? Where will it go?’

19. “Tassa evaṃ ayoniso manasikaroto channaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ aññatarā diṭṭhi uppajjati. ‘Atthi me attā’ti vā assa vāssa (sī. syā. pī.) saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati; ‘natthi me attā’ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati; ‘attanāva attānaṃ sañjānāmī’ti vā assa saccato thetato [V 1.0012] diṭṭhi uppajjati; ‘attanāva anattānaṃ sañjānāmī’ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati; ‘anattanāva attānaṃ sañjānāmī’ti vā assa saccato thetato diṭṭhi uppajjati; atha vā panassa evaṃ diṭṭhi hoti – ‘yo me ayaṃ attā vado vedeyyo tatra tatra kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti so kho pana me ayaṃ attā nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo [M 1.0011] sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassatī’ti. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[T 1.0015], diṭṭhigataṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāraṃ diṭṭhivisūkaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ. Diṭṭhisaṃyojanasaṃyutto, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano na parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi; ‘na parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.

19. When he attends unwisely in this way, one of six views arises in him. The view, ‘I have a self,’ arises in him as true and established; or the view, ‘I have no self,’ arises in him as true and established; or the view, ‘It is by means of the self that I perceive the self,’ arises in him as true and established; or the view, ‘It is by means of the self that I perceive not-self,’ arises in him as true and established; or the view, ‘It is by means of not-self that I perceive the self,’ arises in him as true and established. Or else he has a view such as this: ‘This self of mine is the one who speaks, who feels, who experiences here and there the result of good and bad actions. This self of mine is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, and will remain the same as what is eternal.’ This, monks, is called a wrong view, a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a thorn of views, a contortion of views, a fetter of views. Bound by the fetter of views, monks, the uninstructed ordinary person is not freed from birth, aging, and death, from sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs; he is not freed from suffering, I say.

20. “Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako – ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto – manasikaraṇīye dhamme pajānāti amanasikaraṇīye dhamme pajānāti. So manasikaraṇīye dhamme pajānanto amanasikaraṇīye dhamme pajānanto ye dhammā na [P 1.0009] manasikaraṇīyā te dhamme na manasi karoti, ye dhammā manasikaraṇīyā te dhamme manasi karoti.

20. But, monks, the instructed noble disciple—who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the Dhamma of the noble ones, and is well-disciplined in the Dhamma of the noble ones; who has seen the good persons, is skilled in the Dhamma of the good persons, and is well-disciplined in the Dhamma of the good persons—discerns the states that should be attended to and discerns the states that should not be attended to. Discerning the states that should be attended to and discerning the states that should not be attended to, he does not attend to those states that should not be attended to, and he attends to those states that should be attended to.

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme na manasi karoti? Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pavaḍḍhati; anuppanno vā bhavāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā bhavāsavo pavaḍḍhati; anuppanno vā avijjāsavo uppajjati, uppanno vā avijjāsavo pavaḍḍhati – ime dhammā na manasikaraṇīyā, ye dhamme na manasi karoti.

And what, monks, are those states that should not be attended to, which he does not attend to? Monks, they are those states whereby for one attending to them, the unarisen taint of sensual desire arises, and the arisen taint of sensual desire increases; the unarisen taint of becoming arises, and the arisen taint of becoming increases; the unarisen taint of ignorance arises, and the arisen taint of ignorance increases. These are the states that should not be attended to, which he does not attend to.

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme manasi karoti? Yassa, bhikkhave, dhamme manasikaroto anuppanno vā kāmāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā kāmāsavo pahīyati; anuppanno vā bhavāsavo na uppajjati[T 1.0016], uppanno vā bhavāsavo pahīyati; anuppanno vā avijjāsavo na uppajjati, uppanno vā avijjāsavo pahīyati – ime dhammā manasikaraṇīyā ye dhamme manasi karoti.

And what, monks, are the states that should be attended to, which he attends to? Monks, they are those states whereby for one attending to them, the unarisen taint of sensual desire does not arise, and the arisen taint of sensual desire is abandoned; the unarisen taint of becoming does not arise, and the arisen taint of becoming is abandoned; the unarisen taint of ignorance does not arise, and the arisen taint of ignorance is abandoned. These are the states that should be attended to, which he attends to.

“Tassa amanasikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ amanasikārā manasikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ manasikārā anuppannā ceva āsavā na uppajjanti, uppannā ca āsavā pahīyanti.

For him, by not attending to states that should not be attended to and by attending to states that should be attended to, unarisen taints do not arise, and arisen taints are abandoned.

21. “So [V 1.0013] ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yoniso manasi karoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yoniso manasi karoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yoniso [M 1.0012] manasi karoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yoniso manasi karoti. Tassa evaṃ yoniso manasikaroto tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā dassanā pahātabbā.

21. He wisely attends, ‘This is suffering’; he wisely attends, ‘This is the origin of suffering’; he wisely attends, ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; he wisely attends, ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ For him, thus wisely attending, three fetters are abandoned: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and rituals. These, monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by seeing.

Saṃvarā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Restraint

22. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati. Yañhissa, bhikkhave, cakkhundriyasaṃvaraṃ asaṃvutassa viharato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, cakkhundriyasaṃvaraṃ saṃvutassa viharato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso sotindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati…pe… ghānindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati…pe… jivhindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati…pe… kāyindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati…pe… manindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati. Yañhissa, bhikkhave[T 1.0017], manindriyasaṃvaraṃ asaṃvutassa viharato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, manindriyasaṃvaraṃ saṃvutassa viharato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.

22. And what, monks, are the taints to be abandoned by restraint? Here, monks, a monk, reflecting wisely, dwells restrained with the restraint of the eye faculty. For, monks, if he were to dwell unrestrained with the restraint of the eye faculty, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise; but when he dwells restrained with the restraint of the eye faculty, those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise. Reflecting wisely, he dwells restrained with the restraint of the ear faculty… he dwells restrained with the restraint of the nose faculty… he dwells restrained with the restraint of the tongue faculty… he dwells restrained with the restraint of the body faculty… he dwells restrained with the restraint of the mind faculty. For, monks, if he were to dwell unrestrained with the restraint of the mind faculty, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise; but when he dwells restrained with the restraint of the mind faculty, those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise.

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave, saṃvaraṃ asaṃvutassa viharato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā[P 1.0010], saṃvaraṃ saṃvutassa viharato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā.

For, monks, if one were to dwell unrestrained by this restraint, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise; but when one dwells restrained by this restraint, those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise. These, monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by restraint.

Paṭisevanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Using

23. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvaraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapa- siriṃsapa (sī. syā. pī.) samphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva hirikopīnappaṭicchādanatthaṃ’.

23. And what, monks, are the taints to be abandoned by using? Here, monks, a monk, reflecting wisely, uses the robe only for warding off cold, for warding off heat, for warding off the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, and only for the purpose of covering his private parts.

“Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso piṇḍapātaṃ paṭisevati – ‘neva davāya, na madāya, na maṇḍanāya, na [V 1.0014] vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṃsūparatiyā, brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi navañca [M 1.0013] vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro ca’ cāti (sī.).

Having reflected wisely, he uses almsfood: ‘Not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but only for the endurance and sustenance of this body, for the cessation of discomfort, and for the support of the holy life. Thus, I shall ward off old feeling and not give rise to new feeling. And for me, there will be sustenance, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

“Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso senāsanaṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva utuparissayavinodanapaṭisallānārāmatthaṃ’.

Having reflected wisely, he uses a lodging: ‘Only for warding off cold, for warding off heat, for warding off the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, and only for dispelling the dangers of the climate and for delighting in seclusion.’

“Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva uppannānaṃ veyyābādhikānaṃ vedanānaṃ paṭighātāya, abyābajjhaparamatāya’ abyāpajjhaparamatāya (sī. syā. pī.), abyāpajjaparamatāya (ka.).

Having reflected wisely, he uses medicinal requisites for the sick: ‘Only for warding off arisen, afflicting, painful feelings, and for the supreme state of being without affliction.’

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave, appaṭisevato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā [T 1.0018] vighātapariḷāhā, paṭisevato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā.

For him, O monks, for whom by not using them taints, vexation, and fever would arise, for him, by using them, those taints, vexation, and fever do not arise. These, O monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by using.

Adhivāsanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Enduring

24. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa, jighacchāya pipāsāya. Ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ, duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ tippānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.

24. And what, O monks, are the taints to be abandoned by enduring? Here, O monks, a monk, having reflected wisely, is patient with cold and heat, with hunger and thirst, with the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, with ill-spoken, unwelcome words, and he is of a nature to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave, anadhivāsayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, adhivāsayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā.

For him, O monks, for whom by not enduring them taints, vexation, and fever would arise, for him, by enduring them, those taints, vexation, and fever do not arise. These, O monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by enduring.

Parivajjanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Avoidance

25. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [V 1.0015] paṭisaṅkhā yoniso caṇḍaṃ hatthiṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ assaṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ goṇaṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ kukkuraṃ parivajjeti, ahiṃ khāṇuṃ kaṇṭakaṭṭhānaṃ [P 1.0011] sobbhaṃ papātaṃ candanikaṃ oḷigallaṃ. Yathārūpe anāsane nisinnaṃ [M 1.0014] yathārūpe agocare carantaṃ yathārūpe pāpake mitte bhajantaṃ viññū sabrahmacārī pāpakesu ṭhānesu okappeyyuṃ, so tañca anāsanaṃ tañca agocaraṃ te ca [T 1.0019] pāpake mitte paṭisaṅkhā yoniso parivajjeti.

25. And what, O monks, are the taints to be abandoned by avoidance? Here, O monks, a monk, reflecting wisely, avoids a fierce elephant, a fierce horse, a fierce bull, a fierce dog, a snake, a stump, a thorny place, a pit, a precipice, a cesspool, and a sewer. In a case where wise companions in the holy life might suspect him of being in evil states for sitting in a certain kind of unsuitable seat, for frequenting a certain kind of unsuitable resort, or for associating with certain kinds of evil friends—that monk, reflecting wisely, avoids that unsuitable seat, that unsuitable resort, and those evil friends.

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave, aparivajjayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, parivajjayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā.

For him who does not avoid these, O monks, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise. For him who does avoid them, in this way those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise. These, O monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by avoidance.

Vinodanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Dispelling

26. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ gameti, uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ gameti.

26. And what, O monks, are the taints to be abandoned by dispelling? Here, O monks, a monk, reflecting wisely, does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire; he abandons it, dispels it, brings it to an end, and causes it to go to non-existence. He does not tolerate an arisen thought of ill will... an arisen thought of cruelty... He does not tolerate any arisen evil, unwholesome states; he abandons them, dispels them, brings them to an end, and causes them to go to non-existence.

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave, avinodayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, vinodayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā.

For him who does not dispel them, O monks, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise. For him who does dispel them, in this way those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise. These, O monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by dispelling.

Bhāvanā pahātabbāsavā

Taints to be Abandoned by Development

27. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ; paṭisaṅkhā yoniso dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… [V 1.0016] passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.

27. And what, O monks, are the taints to be abandoned by development? Here, O monks, a monk, reflecting wisely, develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. He develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena... the enlightenment factor of energy... the enlightenment factor of rapture... the enlightenment factor of tranquility... the enlightenment factor of concentration... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment.

“Yañhissa, bhikkhave[T 1.0020], abhāvayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, bhāvayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā.

For him who does not develop these, O monks, taints, vexations, and fevers would arise. For him who does develop them, in this way those taints, vexations, and fevers do not arise. These, O monks, are called the taints to be abandoned by development.

28. “Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ye āsavā dassanā pahātabbā te dassanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā [M 1.0015] te saṃvarā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā te paṭisevanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā te adhivāsanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā [P 1.0012] te parivajjanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā te vinodanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā te bhāvanā pahīnā honti; ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave – ‘bhikkhu sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati, acchecchi acchejji (ka.) taṇhaṃ, vivattayi vāvattayi (sī. pī.) saṃyojanaṃ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’”ti.

28. When, O monks, a monk's taints that are to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, his taints that are to be abandoned by restraint have been abandoned by restraint, his taints that are to be abandoned by use have been abandoned by use, his taints that are to be abandoned by endurance have been abandoned by endurance, his taints that are to be abandoned by avoidance have been abandoned by avoidance, his taints that are to be abandoned by dispelling have been abandoned by dispelling, and his taints that are to be abandoned by development have been abandoned by development—this monk, O monks, is called: ‘one who dwells restrained with the restraint of all taints, who has cut off craving, turned away from the fetters, and, through the right and full understanding of conceit, has made an end of suffering.’”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One spoke this. Delighted, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One’s speech.

Sabbāsavasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Sabbāsava Sutta, the second, is concluded.

3. Dhammadāyādasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Heirs in the Dhamma

29. [T 1.0021][V 1.0017] Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

29. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’ti. Tumhe ca me, bhikkhave, āmisadāyādā bhaveyyātha no dhammadāyādā, tumhepi tena ādiyā ādissā (sī. syā. pī.) bhaveyyātha – ‘āmisadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no dhammadāyādā’ti; ahampi tena ādiyo bhaveyyaṃ – ‘āmisadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no dhammadāyādā’ti. Tumhe ca me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhaveyyātha, no āmisadāyādā, tumhepi tena na ādiyā bhaveyyātha – ‘dhammadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no āmisadāyādā’ti; ahampi tena na ādiyo bhaveyyaṃ – ‘dhammadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no āmisadāyādā’ti. Tasmātiha me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me [M 1.0016] tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’ti.

“Be my heirs in the Dhamma, bhikkhus, not my heirs in material things. I have compassion for you: ‘How might my disciples be heirs in the Dhamma and not heirs in material things?’ If you, bhikkhus, should be my heirs in material things and not in the Dhamma, you would on that account be censured: ‘The Teacher’s disciples dwell as heirs in material things, not as heirs in the Dhamma.’ And I too would on that account be censured: ‘The Teacher’s disciples dwell as heirs in material things, not as heirs in the Dhamma.’ But if you, bhikkhus, should be my heirs in the Dhamma and not in material things, you would not on that account be censured: ‘The Teacher’s disciples dwell as heirs in the Dhamma, not as heirs in material things.’ And I too would not on that account be censured: ‘The Teacher’s disciples dwell as heirs in the Dhamma, not as heirs in material things.’ Therefore, bhikkhus, be my heirs in the Dhamma, not my heirs in material things. I have compassion for you: ‘How might my disciples be heirs in the Dhamma and not heirs in material things?’”

30. “Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bhuttāvī assaṃ pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito [T 1.0022] suhito yāvadattho; siyā ca me piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo chaḍḍiyadhammo (sī. syā. pī.). Atha dve bhikkhū āgaccheyyuṃ jighacchādubbalya- jighacchādubballa (sī. pī.) paretā[P 1.0013]. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadeyyaṃ – ‘ahaṃ khomhi, bhikkhave, bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi ca me ayaṃ piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace ākaṅkhatha, bhuñjatha, no ce tumhe bhuñjissatha sace tumhe na bhuñjissatha (sī. syā. pī.), idānāhaṃ appaharite vā chaḍḍessāmi, appāṇake vā udake opilāpessāmī’ti. Tatrekassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘bhagavā kho bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi cāyaṃ bhagavato piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace mayaṃ na bhuñjissāma, idāni bhagavā appaharite vā chaḍḍessati, appāṇake vā udake opilāpessati’[V 1.0018]. Vuttaṃ kho panetaṃ bhagavatā – ‘dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā’ti. Āmisaññataraṃ kho panetaṃ, yadidaṃ piṇḍapāto. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ abhuñjitvā imināva jighacchādubbalyena evaṃ imaṃ rattindivaṃ rattidivaṃ (ka.) vītināmeyya”nti. So taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ abhuñjitvā teneva jighacchādubbalyena evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya. Atha dutiyassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘bhagavā kho bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi cāyaṃ bhagavato piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace mayaṃ na bhuñjissāma, idāni bhagavā appaharite vā chaḍḍessati, appāṇake [T 1.0023] vā udake opilāpessati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā paṭivinetvā (sī. syā. pī.) evaṃ imaṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya’nti. So taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya. Kiñcāpi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya, atha kho asuyeva me purimo bhikkhu pujjataro ca pāsaṃsataro ca. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tañhi tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dīgharattaṃ [M 1.0017] appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā sallekhāya subharatāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattissati. Tasmātiha me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’”ti.

30. “Suppose, bhikkhus, I have eaten, have refused more, am full, have finished my meal, am satisfied, and have eaten to my heart’s content; and there is some of my almsfood left over that is to be discarded. Then two bhikkhus might arrive, overcome by hunger and weakness. I would say to them: ‘I, bhikkhus, have eaten and have eaten to my heart’s content. This almsfood of mine is left over and is to be discarded. If you wish, eat. If you do not eat, I will now discard it where there is little greenery or cast it into water that is free of living beings.’ It might occur to one of the bhikkhus: ‘The Blessed One has eaten and has eaten to his heart’s content. This almsfood of the Blessed One is left over and is to be discarded. If we do not eat it, the Blessed One will now discard it. But the Blessed One has said: “Be my heirs in the Dhamma, bhikkhus, not my heirs in material things.” This almsfood is a kind of material thing. What if I, without eating this almsfood, were to pass this day and night just so, with this hunger and weakness?’ And so, without eating that almsfood, he would pass that day and night just so, with that same hunger and weakness. Then it might occur to the second bhikkhu: ‘The Blessed One has eaten and has eaten to his heart’s content. This almsfood of the Blessed One is left over and is to be discarded. If we do not eat it, the Blessed One will now discard it. What if I, having eaten this almsfood and dispelled this hunger and weakness, were to pass this day and night just so?’ And so, having eaten that almsfood and dispelled that hunger and weakness, he would pass that day and night just so. Although, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, by eating the almsfood and dispelling his hunger and weakness, would pass that day and night just so, the first bhikkhu is more to be venerated by me and more to be praised. For what reason? Because that, bhikkhus, will lead for a long time to that bhikkhu’s fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, ease of support, and arousal of energy. Therefore, bhikkhus, be my heirs in the Dhamma, not my heirs in material things. I have compassion for you: ‘How might my disciples be heirs in the Dhamma and not heirs in material things?’”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata rose from his seat and entered the dwelling.

31. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto acirapakkantassa bhagavato bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te [P 1.0014] bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

31. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti, kittāvatā ca pana satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhantī”ti? “Dūratopi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āgacchāma [T 1.0024] āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṃ. Sādhu vatāyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho; āyasmato sāriputtassa sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Tena [V 1.0019] hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

“Friends, to what extent do the disciples of a Teacher who dwells in seclusion not follow the training in seclusion, and to what extent do they follow the training in seclusion?” “Friend, we would come even from afar to the presence of the Venerable Sāriputta to understand the meaning of this statement. It would be good if the meaning of this statement would become clear to the Venerable Sāriputta himself. Having heard it from the Venerable Sāriputta, the bhikkhus will remember it.” “In that case, friends, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti? Idhāvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti, yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha, te ca dhamme nappajahanti, bāhulikā bāhullikā (syā.) ca honti, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā. Tatrāvuso, therā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme nappajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena [M 1.0018] ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Bāhulikā ca, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. Therā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. Tatrāvuso, majjhimā bhikkhū…pe… navā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato [T 1.0025] sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme nappajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Bāhulikā ca honti, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. Navā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti.

To what extent, venerable sirs, when the Teacher dwells in seclusion, do the disciples not train in imitation of seclusion? Here, venerable sirs, when the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples do not train in imitation of seclusion; they do not abandon those states that the Teacher has said should be abandoned; and they are materialistic and lax, foremost in backsliding, and have laid down the burden in seclusion. In this regard, venerable sirs, the elder monks are blameworthy on three grounds. ‘When the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples do not train in imitation of seclusion’—on this first ground the elder monks are blameworthy. ‘They do not abandon those states that the Teacher has said should be abandoned’—on this second ground the elder monks are blameworthy. ‘They are materialistic and lax, foremost in backsliding, and have laid down the burden in seclusion’—on this third ground the elder monks are blameworthy. Elder monks, venerable sirs, are blameworthy on these three grounds. In this regard, venerable sirs, the middle monks… the new monks are blameworthy on three grounds. ‘When the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples do not train in imitation of seclusion’—on this first ground the new monks are blameworthy. ‘They do not abandon those states that the Teacher has said should be abandoned’—on this second ground the new monks are blameworthy. ‘They are materialistic and lax, foremost in backsliding, and have laid down the burden in seclusion’—on this third ground the new monks are blameworthy. New monks, venerable sirs, are blameworthy on these three grounds. It is to this extent, venerable sirs, that when the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples do not train in imitation of seclusion.

32. “Kittāvatā ca, panāvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhanti[P 1.0015]? Idhāvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhanti – yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme pajahanti; na ca bāhulikā honti, na sāthalikā okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā. Tatrāvuso, therā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃsā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme pajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā [V 1.0020] bhavanti. ‘Na ca bāhulikā, na sāthalikā okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā bhavanti. Therā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃsā bhavanti[T 1.0026]. Tatrāvuso, majjhimā bhikkhū…pe… navā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃsā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme pajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā bhavanti. ‘Na ca bāhulikā, na sāthalikā okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū pāsaṃsā bhavanti. Navā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi [M 1.0019] tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃsā bhavanti. Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhanti.

32. And to what extent, venerable sirs, do the disciples train in imitation of seclusion when the Teacher dwells in seclusion? Here, venerable sirs, when the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples train in imitation of seclusion: they abandon those states which the Teacher has said should be abandoned; they are not materialistic or lax; they have laid down the burden in backsliding and are foremost in seclusion. In this regard, venerable sirs, the elder monks are praiseworthy on three grounds. ‘When the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples train in imitation of seclusion’—on this first ground the elder monks are praiseworthy. ‘They abandon those states which the Teacher has said should be abandoned’—on this second ground the elder monks are praiseworthy. ‘They are not materialistic or lax; they have laid down the burden in backsliding and are foremost in seclusion’—on this third ground the elder monks are praiseworthy. The elder monks, venerable sirs, are praiseworthy on these three grounds. In this regard, venerable sirs, the middle monks… the new monks are praiseworthy on three grounds. ‘When the Teacher dwells in seclusion, the disciples train in imitation of seclusion’—on this first ground the new monks are praiseworthy. ‘They abandon those states which the Teacher has said should be abandoned’—on this second ground the new monks are praiseworthy. ‘They are not materialistic or lax; they have laid down the burden in backsliding and are foremost in seclusion’—on this third ground the new monks are praiseworthy. The new monks, venerable sirs, are praiseworthy on these three grounds. It is to this extent, venerable sirs, that the disciples train in imitation of seclusion when the Teacher dwells in seclusion.

33. “Tatrāvuso, lobho ca pāpako doso ca pāpako. Lobhassa ca pahānāya dosassa ca pahānāya atthi majjhimā paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamā ca sā, āvuso, majjhimā paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ seyyathīdaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho sā, āvuso, majjhimā paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

33. Therein, venerable sirs, greed is evil and hatred is evil. For the abandoning of greed and for the abandoning of hatred, there is a middle way that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna. And what, venerable sirs, is that middle way that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, venerable sirs, is that middle way that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna.

“Tatrāvuso, kodho ca pāpako upanāho ca [T 1.0027] pāpako…pe… makkho ca pāpako paḷāso ca pāpako, issā ca pāpikā maccherañca pāpakaṃ, māyā ca pāpikā sāṭheyyañca pāpakaṃ, thambho ca pāpako sārambho [P 1.0016] ca pāpako, māno ca pāpako atimāno ca pāpako, mado ca pāpako pamādo ca pāpako. Madassa ca pahānāya pamādassa ca pahānāya atthi majjhimā paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamā ca sā, āvuso, majjhimā paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho sā, āvuso, majjhimā [V 1.0021] paṭipadā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattatī”ti.

Friends, therein, anger is evil and hostility is evil; contempt is evil and rivalry is evil; envy is evil and stinginess is evil; deceit is evil and fraud is evil; stubbornness is evil and contention is evil; conceit is evil and arrogance is evil; intoxication is evil and heedlessness is evil. For the abandoning of intoxication and for the abandoning of heedlessness, there is a middle path that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to calming, to higher knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna. And what, friends, is that middle path that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to calming, to higher knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friends, is that middle path that produces vision and produces knowledge, which leads to calming, to higher knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna.

Idamavocāyasmā sāriputto. Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Thus spoke the Venerable Sāriputta. Those monks, being delighted, rejoiced in the words of the Venerable Sāriputta.

Dhammadāyādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Discourse on the Heirs of the Dhamma, the third, is concluded.

4. Bhayabheravasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Fear and Terror

34. Evaṃ [M 1.0020][V 1.0022][T 1.0028] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ sārāṇīyaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yeme, bho gotama, kulaputtā bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, bhavaṃ tesaṃ gotamo pubbaṅgamo, bhavaṃ tesaṃ gotamo bahukāro, bhavaṃ tesaṃ gotamo samādapetā samādāpetā (?); bhoto ca pana gotamassa sā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjatī”ti. “Evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa, evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa! Ye te, brāhmaṇa, kulaputtā mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, ahaṃ tesaṃ pubbaṅgamo, ahaṃ tesaṃ bahukāro, ahaṃ tesaṃ samādapetā; mama ca pana sā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjatī”ti. “Durabhisambhavāni hi kho, bho gotama, araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni, dukkaraṃ pavivekaṃ, durabhiramaṃ ekatte, haranti maññe mano vanāni samādhiṃ alabhamānassa bhikkhuno”ti[P 1.0017]. “Evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa, evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa! Durabhisambhavāni hi kho, brāhmaṇa, araññavanapatthāni pantāni [T 1.0029] senāsanāni, dukkaraṃ pavivekaṃ, durabhiramaṃ ekatte, haranti maññe mano vanāni samādhiṃ alabhamānassa bhikkhuno”ti.

34. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, for those clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, with the venerable Gotama in mind, the venerable Gotama is their forerunner, the venerable Gotama is of great service to them, the venerable Gotama is the one who establishes them. And that populace follows the seen example of the venerable Gotama.' 'So it is, brahmin, so it is! For those clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, with me in mind, I am their forerunner, I am of great service to them, I am the one who establishes them. And that populace follows my seen example.' 'But, venerable Gotama, forest and wilderness dwellings, which are remote resting places, are hard to endure. Seclusion is difficult, and it is hard to delight in being alone. The forests, it seems, carry away the mind of a monk who has not attained concentration.' 'So it is, brahmin, so it is! Forest and wilderness dwellings, which are remote resting places, are hard to endure. Seclusion is difficult, and it is hard to delight in being alone. The forests, it seems, carry away the mind of a monk who has not attained concentration.'

35. “Mayhampi kho, brāhmaṇa, pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘durabhisambhavāni hi kho araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni, dukkaraṃ pavivekaṃ, durabhiramaṃ ekatte, haranti maññe mano vanāni samādhiṃ alabhamānassa bhikkhuno’ti.
