“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘lābhī assaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘May I be a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘yesāhaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsana gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paribhuñjāmi tesaṃ te kārā mahapphalā assu [M 1.0040] mahānisaṃsā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish, ‘Of those from whom I make use of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick, may their deeds be of great fruit and great benefit,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya [T 1.0059] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘ye maṃ ye me (sī. syā.) ñātī sālohitā petā kālaṅkatā kālakatā (sī. syā. pī.) pasannacittā anussaranti tesaṃ taṃ mahapphalaṃ assa mahānisaṃsa’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘Those of my relatives and kinsmen who are deceased, departed, who remember me with a confident mind—may that remembrance of theirs be of great fruit and great benefit,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of empty abodes.”

66. “Ākaṅkheyya [V 1.0042] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘aratiratisaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ arati saheyya, uppannaṃ aratiṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

66. “If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘May I be one who withstands discontent and content; may discontent not overcome me; and may I dwell having repeatedly overcome any discontent that has arisen,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues… and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘bhayabheravasaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ bhayabheravaṃ saheyya, uppannaṃ bhayabheravaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘May I be one who withstands fear and dread; may fear and dread not overcome me; and may I dwell having repeatedly overcome fear and dread whenever it arises,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues… and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī assaṃ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘May I be an obtainer at will, without difficulty, without trouble, of the four jhānas which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant abidings in this very life,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues… and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā, te kāyena phusitvā vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘Those peaceful liberations which are formless, transcending forms—may I dwell having touched them with the body,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues… and is a developer of empty abodes.”

67. “Ākaṅkheyya [P 1.0034] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno assaṃ avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

67. “If, monks, a monk should wish: ‘Through the destruction of the three fetters, may I be a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, fixed, with enlightenment as my destination,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues… and is a developer of empty abodes.”

“Ākaṅkheyya [T 1.0060] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī assaṃ sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ kareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'By the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, may I be a once-returner, who, having come to this world only once, would make an end of suffering!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya [M 1.0041] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko assaṃ tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… [V 1.0043] brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'By the destruction of the five lower fetters, may I be one who arises spontaneously, attaining Parinibbāna there, not having the nature of returning from that world!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

68. “Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhaveyyaṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā assaṃ, bahudhāpi hutvā eko assaṃ; āvibhāvaṃ tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ kareyyaṃ, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kameyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmaseyyaṃ parimajjeyyaṃ; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

68. If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'May I experience the various kinds of psychic power: having been one, may I become many; having been many, may I become one; may I appear and vanish; may I go unhindered through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; may I perform emergence and submergence in the earth as if in water; may I go on unbroken water as if on earth; may I travel cross-legged in the sky like a winged bird; may I touch and stroke with my hand these moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; may I exercise mastery with the body even up to the Brahma world!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya [T 1.0061] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇeyyaṃ – dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'With the divine ear element, which is purified and surpasses the human, may I hear both kinds of sounds—divine and human, whether far or near!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajāneyyaṃ – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ vītadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ samohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ vītamohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ vikkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ mahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ amahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ sauttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ anuttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ samāhitaṃ [P 1.0035] cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ asamāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti [V 1.0044] pajāneyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'Having encompassed with my own mind the minds of other beings, other persons, may I know them discriminately: a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"; a mind without lust as "a mind without lust"; a mind with hatred as "a mind with hatred"; a mind without hatred as "a mind without hatred"; a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion"; a mind without delusion as "a mind without delusion"; a constricted mind as "a constricted mind"; a distracted mind as "a distracted mind"; a superior mind as "a superior mind"; a non-superior mind as "a non-superior mind"; a surpassable mind as "a surpassable mind"; an unsurpassable mind as "an unsurpassable mind"; a concentrated mind as "a concentrated mind"; an unconcentrated mind as "an unconcentrated mind"; a liberated mind as "a liberated mind"; an unliberated mind as "an unliberated mind"!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya [T 1.0062][M 1.0042] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jāti satasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapannoti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'May I recollect my manifold past existences, that is: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of cosmic contraction, many aeons of cosmic expansion, many aeons of cosmic contraction and expansion—"In that existence, I had such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my lifespan. Passing away from there, I arose in another existence. There too, I had such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my lifespan. Passing away from there, I have arisen here." Thus, with their aspects and details, may I recollect my manifold past existences!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ – ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto [T 1.0063] sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannāti, iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

If, O monks, a monk should wish: 'With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, may I see beings passing away and reappearing—lowly and eminent, of good appearance and bad appearance, in good destinations and bad destinations; may I know discriminately how beings fare according to their kamma: "Indeed, these honorable beings were endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind, were revilers of the noble ones, held wrong view, and undertook actions based on wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. Or indeed, these honorable beings were endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, were not revilers of the noble ones, held right view, and undertook actions based on right view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have reappeared in a good destination, in a heavenly world." Thus, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, may I see beings passing away and reappearing—lowly and eminent, of good appearance and bad appearance, in good destinations and bad destinations; may I know discriminately how beings fare according to their kamma!' he should be one who fulfills the precepts, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, possesses non-neglected absorption, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of meditation in secluded dwellings.

69. “Ākaṅkheyya [V 1.0045] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā [P 1.0036] upasampajja [M 1.0043] vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

69. “Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘Through the destruction of the taints, may I, in this very life, realize for myself with direct knowledge, attain, and dwell in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a cultivator of empty dwellings.

“Sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharatha sampannapātimokkhā; pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino; samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesū”ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti.

“‘Bhikkhus, dwell endowed with virtue, endowed with the Pātimokkha. Dwell restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, endowed with proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults. Having undertaken them, train in the training rules.’ That which was spoken was spoken in reference to this.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One spoke this. Those bhikkhus, with delighted minds, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s speech.

Ākaṅkheyyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Ākaṅkheyya Sutta, the sixth, is concluded.

7. Vatthasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Cloth

70. Evaṃ [T 1.0064][V 1.0046] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

70. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Bhikkhus.’ ‘Venerable sir,’ those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One spoke this:

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitaṃ; tamenaṃ rajako yasmiṃ yasmiṃ raṅgajāte upasaṃhareyya – yadi nīlakāya yadi pītakāya yadi lohitakāya yadi mañjiṭṭhakāya mañjeṭṭhakāya (sī. pī.), mañjeṭṭhikāya (syā.) durattavaṇṇamevassa aparisuddhavaṇṇamevassa. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aparisuddhattā, bhikkhave, vatthassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, citte saṃkiliṭṭhe, duggati pāṭikaṅkhā. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ; tamenaṃ rajako yasmiṃ yasmiṃ raṅgajāte upasaṃhareyya – yadi nīlakāya yadi pītakāya yadi lohitakāya yadi mañjiṭṭhakāya – surattavaṇṇamevassa parisuddhavaṇṇamevassa. Taṃ kissa hetu? Parisuddhattā, bhikkhave, vatthassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, citte asaṃkiliṭṭhe, sugati pāṭikaṅkhā.

“Bhikkhus, just as a cloth that is stained and soiled, if a dyer were to dip it into any kind of dye—whether blue, yellow, red, or crimson—it would be badly dyed and impure in color. For what reason? Bhikkhus, because of the impurity of the cloth. In the same way, bhikkhus, when the mind is defiled, an unfortunate destination is to be expected. Bhikkhus, just as a cloth that is pure and bright, if a dyer were to dip it into any kind of dye—whether blue, yellow, red, or crimson—it would be well-dyed and pure in color. For what reason? Bhikkhus, because of the purity of the cloth. In the same way, bhikkhus, when the mind is undefiled, a fortunate destination is to be expected.”

71. “Katame ca, bhikkhave, cittassa upakkilesā? Abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso, byāpādo cittassa upakkileso, kodho cittassa upakkileso, upanāho cittassa upakkileso, makkho [M 1.0044] cittassa upakkileso, paḷāso cittassa upakkileso, issā [T 1.0065] cittassa upakkileso, macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso, māyā cittassa upakkileso, sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso, thambho cittassa upakkileso, sārambho cittassa upakkileso, māno cittassa upakkileso, atimāno cittassa upakkileso, mado cittassa [P 1.0037] upakkileso, pamādo cittassa upakkileso.

71. “And what, bhikkhus, are the defilements of the mind? Covetousness and unrighteous greed is a defilement of the mind; ill will is a defilement of the mind; anger is a defilement of the mind; hostility is a defilement of the mind; contempt is a defilement of the mind; rivalry is a defilement of the mind; envy is a defilement of the mind; avarice is a defilement of the mind; deceit is a defilement of the mind; fraud is a defilement of the mind; stubbornness is a defilement of the mind; presumption is a defilement of the mind; conceit is a defilement of the mind; arrogance is a defilement of the mind; intoxication is a defilement of the mind; heedlessness is a defilement of the mind.”

72. “Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā byāpādaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati[V 1.0047]; ‘kodho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā kodhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘upanāho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā upanāhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘makkho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā makkhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘paḷāso cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā paḷāsaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘issā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā issaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘māyā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘thambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thambhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘sārambho cittassa upakkileso’ti [T 1.0066] – iti viditvā sārambhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘māno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā mānaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘atimāno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atimānaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘mado cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā madaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘pamādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā pamādaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati.

72. “Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, having known thus: ‘Covetousness and unrighteous greed is a defilement of the mind,’ abandons covetousness and unrighteous greed, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Ill will is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons ill will, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Anger is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons anger, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Hostility is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons hostility, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Contempt is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons contempt, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Rivalry is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons rivalry, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Envy is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons envy, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Avarice is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons avarice, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Deceit is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons deceit, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Fraud is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons fraud, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Stubbornness is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons stubbornness, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Presumption is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons presumption, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Conceit is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons conceit, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Arrogance is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons arrogance, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Intoxication is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons intoxication, a defilement of the mind. Having known thus: ‘Heedlessness is a defilement of the mind,’ he abandons heedlessness, a defilement of the mind.”

73. “Yato kho yato ca kho (sī. syā.), bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso [M 1.0045] pahīno hoti, ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā byāpādo cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘kodho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā kodho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘upanāho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā upanāho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘makkho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā makkho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘paḷāso cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā paḷāso cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘issā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā issā cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘māyā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māyā cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti [T 1.0067] – iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘thambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thambho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘sārambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sārambho cittassa upakkileso pahīno [V 1.0048] hoti; ‘māno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māno cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘atimāno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atimāno cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘mado cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā mado cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘pamādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā pamādo cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.

73. “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu understands that ‘covetousness and unrighteous greed is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, covetousness and unrighteous greed, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘ill will is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, ill will, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘anger is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, anger, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘hostility is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, hostility, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘denigration is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, denigration, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘rivalry is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, rivalry, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘envy is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, envy, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘stinginess is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, stinginess, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘deceit is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, deceit, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘fraud is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, fraud, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘obstinacy is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, obstinacy, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘contention is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, contention, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘conceit is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, conceit, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘arrogance is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, arrogance, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘vanity is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, vanity, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned; when he understands that ‘heedlessness is a defilement of the mind’—having known this, heedlessness, that defilement of the mind, is abandoned.”

74. “So buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti; dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti; saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno [M 1.0046] bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni, aṭṭha purisapuggalā. Esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo[T 1.0068], anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti.

74. “He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the true way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight individuals. This Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’”

75. “Yathodhi yatodhi (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ) kho panassa cattaṃ hoti vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, so ‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati; ‘dhamme…pe… saṅghe [P 1.0038] aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ; pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. ‘Yathodhi kho pana me cattaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭha’nti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ; pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati.

75. “And to the extent that defilements have been given up, disgorged, released, abandoned, and relinquished by him, he, reflecting, ‘I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha,’ gains inspiration from the meaning, gains inspiration from the Dhamma, and gains the joy connected with the Dhamma. When he is joyful, rapture arises. For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil. One with a tranquil body experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. Reflecting, ‘I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha,’ he gains inspiration from the meaning, gains inspiration from the Dhamma, and gains the joy connected with the Dhamma. When he is joyful, rapture arises. For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil. One with a tranquil body experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. Reflecting, ‘To the extent that defilements have been given up, disgorged, released, abandoned, and relinquished by me,’ he gains inspiration from the meaning, gains inspiration from the Dhamma, and gains the joy connected with the Dhamma. When he is joyful, rapture arises. For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil. One with a tranquil body experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated.”

76. “Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃsīlo evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño sālīnaṃ cepi piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati vicitakāḷakaṃ anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ, nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitaṃ acchodakaṃ āgamma parisuddhaṃ hoti pariyodātaṃ[V 1.0049], ukkāmukhaṃ vā panāgamma jātarūpaṃ parisuddhaṃ hoti pariyodātaṃ, evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃsīlo evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño sālīnaṃ cepi piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati vicitakāḷakaṃ anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ[T 1.0069], nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya.

76. “Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with such virtue, such a state of mind, and such wisdom, even if he eats alms-food of fine rice with dark grains removed, with many soups and many curries, it is no obstacle for him. Just as, bhikkhus, a cloth that is stained and soiled becomes clean and pure on encountering clear water, or just as gold becomes clean and pure on encountering a crucible, even so, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu endowed with such virtue, such a state of mind, and such wisdom, even if he eats alms-food of fine rice with dark grains removed, with many soups and many curries, it is no obstacle for him.”

77. “So mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ catutthiṃ (sī. pī.). Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena [M 1.0047] cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

77. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion… with appreciative joy… with equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will.

78. “So ‘atthi idaṃ, atthi hīnaṃ, atthi paṇītaṃ, atthi imassa saññāgatassa uttariṃ nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti[P 1.0039]. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave – ‘bhikkhu sināto antarena sinānenā’”ti.

78. He distinctly knows: ‘There is this, there is the inferior, there is the sublime, and there is a further escape from this state of perception.’ When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, from the taint of becoming, and from the taint of ignorance. When liberated, there is the knowledge: ‘Liberated.’ He distinctly knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ This, monks, is called a bhikkhu who has bathed with the inner bathing.

79. Tena kho pana samayena sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti. Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo [T 1.0070] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhukaṃ nadiṃ sināyitu”nti? “Kiṃ, brāhmaṇa, bāhukāya nadiyā? Kiṃ bāhukā nadī karissatī”ti? “Lokkhasammatā lokhyasammatā (sī.), mokkhasammatā (pī.) hi, bho gotama, bāhukā nadī bahujanassa, puññasammatā hi, bho gotama, bāhukā nadī bahujanassa, bāhukāya pana nadiyā bahujano pāpakammaṃ kataṃ pavāhetī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sundarikabhāradvājaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

79. Now at that time, the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja was sitting not far from the Blessed One. Then the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: “Does the venerable Gotama go to the Bāhukā river to bathe?” “What, brahmin, of the Bāhukā river? What can the Bāhukā river do?” “Venerable Gotama, the Bāhukā river is considered by many people to be a means of purification; Venerable Gotama, the Bāhukā river is considered meritorious by many people. In the Bāhukā river, many people wash away the evil kamma they have done.” Then the Blessed One addressed the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja in verse:

“Bāhukaṃ adhikakkañca, gayaṃ sundarikaṃ mapi sundarikāmapi (sī. syā. pī.), sundarikaṃ mahiṃ (itipi);

Sarassatiṃ payāgañca, atho bāhumatiṃ nadiṃ;

Niccampi bālo pakkhando pakkhanno (sī. syā. pī.), kaṇhakammo na sujjhati.

“To the Bāhukā, the Adhikakka, the Gayā, and the Sundarikā, to the Sarassatī, the Payāga, and the Bāhumatī river; though a fool with dark kamma may always plunge, he is not purified.

“Kiṃ [V 1.0050] sundarikā karissati, kiṃ payāgā payāgo (sī. syā. pī.) kiṃ bāhukā nadī;

Veriṃ katakibbisaṃ naraṃ, na hi naṃ sodhaye pāpakamminaṃ.

“What can the Sundarikā do? What the Payāga, what the Bāhukā river? They cannot purify that evil-doing man who is hostile and has committed cruel deeds.

“Suddhassa [M 1.0048] ve sadā phaggu, suddhassuposatho sadā;

Suddhassa sucikammassa, sadā sampajjate vataṃ;

Idheva sināhi brāhmaṇa, sabbabhūtesu karohi khemataṃ.

“For the pure one, it is always the Phaggu festival; for the pure one, it is always the Uposatha. For the pure one of pure deeds, his observance always succeeds. Bathe right here, brahmin; be a sanctuary for all beings.

“Sace musā na bhaṇasi, sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi;

Sace adinnaṃ nādiyasi, saddahāno amaccharī;

Kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayā”ti.

“If you do not speak falsely, if you do not harm a living being, if you do not take what is not given, having faith and being without avarice; what will you do by going to Gayā? Any well is Gayā for you.”

80. Evaṃ [T 1.0071] vutte, sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. Alattha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno [P 1.0040] kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosīti.

80. When this was said, the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, venerable Gotama! Magnificent, venerable Gotama! Just as, venerable Gotama, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the path to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—in the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the venerable Gotama in many ways. I go for refuge to the venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May I receive the going forth in the presence of the venerable Gotama, and may I receive the full admission.” And the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja received the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, and he received the full admission. Not long after his full admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Bhāradvāja, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, entered and dwelled in that unsurpassed goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He knew directly: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.” And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.

Vatthasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Vattha Sutta, the seventh, is concluded.

8. Sallekhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Effacement

81. Evaṃ [V 1.0051][T 1.0072] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā mahācundo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho [M 1.0049] āyasmā mahācundo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yā imā, bhante, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – attavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā lokavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā – ādimeva nu kho, bhante, bhikkhuno manasikaroto evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hotī”ti?

81. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Mahācunda, having emerged from seclusion, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Mahācunda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, regarding these various kinds of views that arise in the world—connected with theories of self or connected with theories of the world—for a bhikkhu who attends from the very beginning, is there thus the abandoning of these views, is there thus the relinquishing of these views?”

82. “Yā imā, cunda, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – attavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā lokavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā – yattha cetā diṭṭhiyo uppajjanti yattha ca anusenti yattha ca samudācaranti taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na me so attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññā passato evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hoti.

82. “Cunda, regarding these various kinds of views that arise in the world—connected with theories of self or connected with theories of the world—for one who sees that wherein they arise, lie latent, and come into play, as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self,’ for him there is the abandoning of these views, for him there is the relinquishing of these views.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu vivicceva [T 1.0073] kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete [P 1.0041] ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, having secluded himself from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, might enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called pleasant dwellings in the here-and-now in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, might enter and dwell in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called pleasant dwellings in the here-and-now in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ [V 1.0052] kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihareyya, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeyya, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā [T 1.0074] vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, with the fading away of rapture, might dwell equanimously, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experience happiness with the body; he might enter and dwell in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, he dwells happily.’ He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called pleasant dwellings in the here-and-now in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasuṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ [M 1.0050] catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow, might enter and dwell in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called pleasant dwellings in the here-and-now in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā, paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā, nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā, ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and through non-attention to perceptions of diversity, perceiving ‘Space is infinite,’ might enter and dwell in the base of infinite space. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called peaceful dwellings in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, perceiving ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ might enter and dwell in the base of infinite consciousness. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called peaceful dwellings in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā [T 1.0075] vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, perceiving ‘There is nothing,’ might enter and dwell in the base of nothingness. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called peaceful dwellings in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti[V 1.0053]. Na [P 1.0042] kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

“It is possible, Cunda, that a certain bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, might enter and dwell in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. He might think: ‘I am dwelling by effacement.’ But these, Cunda, are not called effacements in the Noble One’s Discipline. These are called peaceful dwellings in the Noble One’s Discipline.

83. “Idha kho pana vo, cunda, sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pāṇātipātī bhavissanti, mayamettha pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare adinnādāyī bhavissanti, mayamettha adinnādānā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare [M 1.0051] abrahmacārī bhavissanti, mayamettha brahmacārī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare musāvādī bhavissanti, mayamettha musāvādā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pisuṇavācā pisuṇā vācā (sī. pī.) bhavissanti, mayamettha pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pharusavācā pharusā vācā (sī. pī.) bhavissanti, mayamettha pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare samphappalāpī bhavissanti, mayamettha samphappalāpā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare abhijjhālū bhavissanti, mayamettha anabhijjhālū bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare byāpannacittā bhavissanti, mayamettha abyāpannacittā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchādiṭṭhī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammādiṭṭhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsaṅkappā [T 1.0076] bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsaṅkappā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvācā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvācā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchākammantā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammākammantā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāājīvā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāājīvā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvāyāmā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvāyāmā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsatī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsatī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsamādhi bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsamādhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāñāṇī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāñāṇī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvimuttī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvimuttī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo.

83. Here, Cunda, effacement should be practiced by you. ‘Others will be harmful, but here we shall be harmless’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will take life, but here we shall abstain from taking life’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will take what is not given, but here we shall abstain from taking what is not given’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be unchaste, but here we shall be chaste’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will speak falsely, but here we shall abstain from false speech’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will use slanderous speech, but here we shall abstain from slanderous speech’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will use harsh speech, but here we shall abstain from harsh speech’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will engage in frivolous chatter, but here we shall abstain from frivolous chatter’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be covetous, but here we shall be without covetousness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have minds of ill will, but here we shall have minds free from ill will’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will hold wrong view, but here we shall hold right view’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong resolve, but here we shall have right resolve’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong speech, but here we shall have right speech’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong action, but here we shall have right action’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong livelihood, but here we shall have right livelihood’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong effort, but here we shall have right effort’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong mindfulness, but here we shall have right mindfulness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong concentration, but here we shall have right concentration’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong knowledge, but here we shall have right knowledge’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have wrong liberation, but here we shall have right liberation’—thus effacement should be practiced.

“‘Pare thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā bhavissanti, mayamettha vigatathīnamiddhā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo[V 1.0054]. ‘Pare uddhatā bhavissanti, mayamettha anuddhatā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare vicikicchī vecikicchī (sī. pī. ka.) bhavissanti, mayamettha tiṇṇavicikicchā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare kodhanā bhavissanti, mayamettha akkodhanā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare upanāhī bhavissanti, mayamettha anupanāhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare [P 1.0043] makkhī bhavissanti[M 1.0052], mayamettha amakkhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare [T 1.0077] paḷāsī bhavissanti, mayamettha apaḷāsī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare issukī bhavissanti, mayamettha anissukī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare maccharī bhavissanti, mayamettha amaccharī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare saṭhā bhavissanti, mayamettha asaṭhā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare māyāvī bhavissanti, mayamettha amāyāvī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare thaddhā bhavissanti, mayamettha atthaddhā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare atimānī bhavissanti, mayamettha anatimānī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare dubbacā bhavissanti, mayamettha suvacā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pāpamittā bhavissanti, mayamettha kalyāṇamittā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pamattā bhavissanti, mayamettha appamattā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare assaddhā bhavissanti, mayamettha saddhā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare ahirikā bhavissanti, mayamettha hirimanā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare anottāpī anottappī (ka.) bhavissanti, mayamettha ottāpī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare appassutā bhavissanti, mayamettha bahussutā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare kusītā bhavissanti, mayamettha āraddhavīriyā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare muṭṭhassatī bhavissanti, mayamettha upaṭṭhitassatī bhavissāmā’ti [T 1.0078] sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare duppaññā bhavissanti, mayamettha paññāsampannā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī bhavissanti, mayamettha asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo.

‘Others will be overcome by sloth and torpor, but here we shall be free from sloth and torpor’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be restless, but here we shall be without restlessness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be doubtful, but here we shall have overcome doubt’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be angry, but here we shall be without anger’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be resentful, but here we shall be without resentment’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be denigrating, but here we shall be without denigration’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be competitive, but here we shall be without competitiveness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be envious, but here we shall be without envy’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be stingy, but here we shall be without stinginess’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be fraudulent, but here we shall be without fraudulence’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be deceitful, but here we shall be without deceit’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be stubborn, but here we shall be without stubbornness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be arrogant, but here we shall be without arrogance’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be difficult to correct, but here we shall be easy to correct’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will have bad friends, but here we shall have good friends’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be heedless, but here we shall be heedful’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be faithless, but here we shall be faithful’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be shameless, but here we shall have a sense of shame’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be without fear of wrongdoing, but here we shall be fearful of wrongdoing’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be of little learning, but here we shall be of great learning’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be lazy, but here we shall be energetic’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be of lapsed mindfulness, but here we shall be of established mindfulness’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will be unwise, but here we shall be endowed with wisdom’—thus effacement should be practiced. ‘Others will cling to their own views, grasping them tenaciously and abandoning them with difficulty, but here we shall not cling to our own views, not grasp them tenaciously, and shall abandon them with ease’—thus effacement should be practiced.

84. “Cittuppādampi kho ahaṃ, cunda, kusalesu dhammesu bahukāraṃ bahūpakāraṃ (ka.) vadāmi, ko pana vādo kāyena vācāya anuvidhīyanāsu! Tasmātiha, cunda, ‘pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ. ‘Pare pāṇātipātī bhavissanti, mayamettha pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā [M 1.0053] bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ…‘pare sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī [V 1.0055] ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī bhavissanti, mayamettha asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

84. Cunda, I say that even the arising of a thought is of great help in regard to wholesome states; what then of acting in accordance with it by body and speech? Therefore, Cunda, the thought should be aroused thus: ‘Others will be harmful, but we here shall be harmless.’ The thought should be aroused: ‘Others will be destroyers of life, but we here shall abstain from destroying life.’… The thought should be aroused: ‘Others will be those who misapprehend their own views, hold on to them tenaciously, and relinquish them with difficulty, but we here shall be those who do not misapprehend our own views, do not hold on to them tenaciously, and relinquish them with ease.’”

85. “Seyyathāpi, cunda, visamo maggo assa, tassa maggo tassāssa (sī. syā. pī.) añño samo maggo parikkamanāya; seyyathā vā pana, cunda, visamaṃ titthaṃ assa, tassa aññaṃ samaṃ titthaṃ parikkamanāya; evameva [P 1.0044] kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti parikkamanāya, pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, adinnādāyissa purisapuggalassa adinnādānā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, abrahmacārissa purisapuggalassa abrahmacariyā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya[T 1.0079], musāvādissa purisapuggalassa musāvādā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, pisuṇavācassa purisapuggalassa pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, pharusavācassa purisapuggalassa pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, samphappalāpissa purisapuggalassa samphappalāpā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, abhijjhālussa purisapuggalassa anabhijjhā hoti parikkamanāya, byāpannacittassa purisapuggalassa abyāpādo hoti parikkamanāya, micchādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa sammādiṭṭhi hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsaṅkappassa purisapuggalassa sammāsaṅkappo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvācassa purisapuggalassa sammāvācā hoti parikkamanāya, micchākammantassa purisapuggalassa sammākammanto hoti parikkamanāya, micchāājīvassa purisapuggalassa sammāājīvo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvāyāmassa purisapuggalassa sammāvāyāmo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsatissa purisapuggalassa sammāsati hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsamādhissa purisapuggalassa sammāsamādhi hoti parikkamanāya, micchāñāṇissa purisapuggalassa sammāñāṇaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvimuttissa purisapuggalassa sammāvimutti hoti parikkamanāya.

85. Just as, Cunda, there might be a rough path, and another, smooth path for bypassing it; or just as there might be a rough ford, and another, smooth ford for bypassing it—so too, Cunda, for a harmful person, non-harming is for bypassing; for a person who destroys life, abstention from destroying life is for bypassing; for a person who takes what is not given, abstention from taking what is not given is for bypassing; for a person who is not celibate, abstention from unchastity is for bypassing; for a person who speaks falsely, abstention from false speech is for bypassing; for a person who speaks divisively, abstention from divisive speech is for bypassing; for a person who speaks harshly, abstention from harsh speech is for bypassing; for a person who engages in idle chatter, abstention from idle chatter is for bypassing; for a covetous person, non-covetousness is for bypassing; for a person with a mind of ill will, non-ill will is for bypassing; for a person of wrong view, right view is for bypassing; for a person of wrong thought, right thought is for bypassing; for a person of wrong speech, right speech is for bypassing; for a person of wrong action, right action is for bypassing; for a person of wrong livelihood, right livelihood is for bypassing; for a person of wrong effort, right effort is for bypassing; for a person of wrong mindfulness, right mindfulness is for bypassing; for a person of wrong concentration, right concentration is for bypassing; for a person of wrong knowledge, right knowledge is for bypassing; for a person of wrong liberation, right liberation is for bypassing.

“Thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhitassa purisapuggalassa vigatathinamiddhatā hoti parikkamanāya, uddhatassa purisapuggalassa anuddhaccaṃ [T 1.0080] hoti parikkamanāya, vicikicchissa purisapuggalassa tiṇṇavicikicchatā hoti parikkamanāya, kodhanassa purisapuggalassa [M 1.0054] akkodho hoti parikkamanāya, upanāhissa purisapuggalassa anupanāho hoti parikkamanāya, makkhissa purisapuggalassa amakkho hoti parikkamanāya, paḷāsissa purisapuggalassa apaḷāso hoti parikkamanāya[V 1.0056], issukissa purisapuggalassa anissukitā hoti parikkamanāya, maccharissa purisapuggalassa amacchariyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, saṭhassa purisapuggalassa asāṭheyyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, māyāvissa purisapuggalassa amāyā amāyāvitā (ka.) hoti parikkamanāya, thaddhassa purisapuggalassa atthaddhiyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, atimānissa purisapuggalassa anatimāno hoti parikkamanāya, dubbacassa purisapuggalassa sovacassatā hoti parikkamanāya, pāpamittassa purisapuggalassa kalyāṇamittatā hoti parikkamanāya, pamattassa purisapuggalassa appamādo hoti parikkamanāya, assaddhassa purisapuggalassa saddhā hoti parikkamanāya, ahirikassa purisapuggalassa hirī hoti parikkamanāya, anottāpissa purisapuggalassa ottappaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, appassutassa purisapuggalassa bāhusaccaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, kusītassa purisapuggalassa vīriyārambho hoti parikkamanāya, muṭṭhassatissa purisapuggalassa upaṭṭhitassatitā hoti parikkamanāya, duppaññassa purisapuggalassa paññāsampadā hoti parikkamanāya[T 1.0081], sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsianādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti parikkamanāya.

For a person overcome by sloth and torpor, freedom from sloth and torpor is for bypassing. For a restless person, non-restlessness is for bypassing. For a person who is doubtful, the state of having overcome doubt is for bypassing. For an angry person, non-anger is for bypassing. For a hostile person, non-hostility is for bypassing. For a denigrating person, non-denigration is for bypassing. For a rivalrous person, non-rivalry is for bypassing. For a jealous person, non-jealousy is for bypassing. For a stingy person, non-stinginess is for bypassing. For a deceitful person, non-deceitfulness is for bypassing. For a fraudulent person, non-fraudulence is for bypassing. For an obstinate person, non-obstinacy is for bypassing. For an arrogant person, non-arrogance is for bypassing. For a person who is difficult to admonish, amenability to admonishment is for bypassing. For a person with bad friends, good friendship is for bypassing. For a heedless person, heedfulness is for bypassing. For a faithless person, faith is for bypassing. For a shameless person, moral shame is for bypassing. For a person with no moral dread, moral dread is for bypassing. For a person of little learning, great learning is for bypassing. For a lazy person, the arousal of energy is for bypassing. For a person of lapsed mindfulness, the state of established mindfulness is for bypassing. For an unwise person, accomplishment in wisdom is for bypassing. For a person who misapprehends their own views, holds on to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty, the state of not misapprehending one's own views, not holding on to them tenaciously, and relinquishing them with ease is for bypassing.

86. “Seyyathāpi, cunda, ye keci akusalā dhammā sabbe te adhobhāgaṅgamanīyā adhobhāvaṅgamanīyā (sī. syā. pī.), ye keci kusalā dhammā sabbe te uparibhāgaṅgamanīyā uparibhāvaṅgamanīyā (sī. syā. pī.), evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti uparibhāgāya uparibhāvāya (sī. syā. ka.), pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti uparibhāgāya…pe… sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa [P 1.0045] purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-anādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti uparibhāgāya.

86. Just as, Cunda, whatever unwholesome states there are, all of them lead to the lower realm; and whatever wholesome states there are, all of them lead to the upper realm. So too, Cunda, for a harmful person, non-harming is for the sake of the upper realm; for a person who destroys life, abstention from destroying life is for the sake of the upper realm… for a person who misapprehends their own views, holds on to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty, the state of not misapprehending one's own views, not holding on to them tenaciously, and relinquishing them with ease is for the sake of the upper realm.

87. “So vata, cunda, attanā palipapalipanno paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vata, cunda, attanā apalipapalipanno paraṃ [M 1.0055] palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. So vata, cunda, attanā adanto avinīto aparinibbuto paraṃ damessati vinessati parinibbāpessatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vata[V 1.0057], cunda, attanā danto vinīto parinibbuto paraṃ damessati vinessati parinibbāpessatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti parinibbānāya, pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Adinnādāyissa purisapuggalassa adinnādānā veramaṇī [T 1.0082] hoti parinibbānāya. Abrahmacārissa purisapuggalassa abrahmacariyā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Musāvādissa purisapuggalassa musāvādā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Pisuṇavācassa purisapuggalassa pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Pharusavācassa purisapuggalassa pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Samphappalāpissa purisapuggalassa samphappalāpā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Abhijjhālussa purisapuggalassa anabhijjhā hoti parinibbānāya. Byāpannacittassa purisapuggalassa abyāpādo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa sammādiṭṭhi hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsaṅkappassa purisapuggalassa sammāsaṅkappo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvācassa purisapuggalassa sammāvācā hoti parinibbānāya. Micchākammantassa purisapuggalassa sammākammanto hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāājīvassa purisapuggalassa sammāājīvo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvāyāmassa purisapuggalassa sammāvāyāmo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsatissa purisapuggalassa sammāsati hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsamādhissa purisapuggalassa sammāsamādhi hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāñāṇissa purisapuggalassa sammāñāṇaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvimuttissa purisapuggalassa sammāvimutti hoti parinibbānāya.

87. Indeed, Cunda, that a person who is himself sunk in the mire will pull out another who is sunk in the mire—this is not possible. Indeed, Cunda, that a person who is himself not sunk in the mire will pull out another who is sunk in the mire—this is possible. Indeed, Cunda, that a person who is himself untamed, undisciplined, and unextinguished will tame, discipline, and extinguish another—this is not possible. Indeed, Cunda, that a person who is himself tamed, disciplined, and extinguished will tame, discipline, and extinguish another—this is possible. In this very way, Cunda, for a harmful person, non-harmfulness is for final extinguishment. For a person who destroys life, abstinence from destroying life is for final extinguishment. For a person who takes what is not given, abstinence from taking what is not given is for final extinguishment. For a person who is unchaste, abstinence from unchastity is for final extinguishment. For a person who speaks falsely, abstinence from false speech is for final extinguishment. For a person who speaks divisively, abstinence from divisive speech is for final extinguishment. For a person who speaks harshly, abstinence from harsh speech is for final extinguishment. For a person who engages in frivolous chatter, abstinence from frivolous chatter is for final extinguishment. For a covetous person, non-covetousness is for final extinguishment. For a person with a mind of ill will, non-ill will is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong view, right view is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong thought, right thought is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong speech, right speech is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong action, right action is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong livelihood, right livelihood is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong effort, right effort is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong mindfulness, right mindfulness is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong concentration, right concentration is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong knowledge, right knowledge is for final extinguishment. For a person with wrong liberation, right liberation is for final extinguishment.

“Thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhitassa [T 1.0083] purisapuggalassa vigatathinamiddhatā hoti parinibbānāya. Uddhatassa purisapuggalassa anuddhaccaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Vicikicchissa purisapuggalassa tiṇṇavicikicchatā hoti parinibbānāya. Kodhanassa purisapuggalassa akkodho hoti parinibbānāya. Upanāhissa purisapuggalassa anupanāho hoti parinibbānāya. Makkhissa purisapuggalassa amakkho hoti parinibbānāya. Paḷāsissa purisapuggalassa apaḷāso [M 1.0056] hoti parinibbānāya. Issukissa purisapuggalassa anissukitā hoti parinibbānāya. Maccharissa purisapuggalassa amacchariyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Saṭhassa purisapuggalassa asāṭheyyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Māyāvissa purisapuggalassa amāyā hoti parinibbānāya. Thaddhassa purisapuggalassa atthaddhiyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Atimānissa purisapuggalassa anatimāno hoti parinibbānāya. Dubbacassa purisapuggalassa sovacassatā hoti parinibbānāya. Pāpamittassa purisapuggalassa kalyāṇamittatā hoti parinibbānāya. Pamattassa purisapuggalassa appamādo [V 1.0058] hoti parinibbānāya. Assaddhassa purisapuggalassa saddhā hoti parinibbānāya. Ahirikassa purisapuggalassa hirī hoti parinibbānāya. Anottāpissa purisapuggalassa ottappaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Appassutassa purisapuggalassa bāhusaccaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Kusītassa purisapuggalassa vīriyārambho hoti parinibbānāya. Muṭṭhassatissa purisapuggalassa [T 1.0084] upaṭṭhitassatitā hoti parinibbānāya. Duppaññassa purisapuggalassa [P 1.0046] paññāsampadā hoti parinibbānāya. Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-anādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti parinibbānāya.

For a person oppressed by sloth and torpor, the state of being without sloth and torpor is for final extinguishment. For a restless person, non-restlessness is for final extinguishment. For a person with doubt, the state of having crossed over doubt is for final extinguishment. For a person prone to anger, non-anger is for final extinguishment. For a person who bears grudges, non-animosity is for final extinguishment. For a person who is contemptuous, non-contempt is for final extinguishment. For a person prone to rivalry, non-rivalry is for final extinguishment. For a person who is envious, the state of being non-envious is for final extinguishment. For a person who is stingy, non-stinginess is for final extinguishment. For a person who is deceitful, non-deceitfulness is for final extinguishment. For a fraudulent person, non-fraudulence is for final extinguishment. For a person who is stubborn, non-stubbornness is for final extinguishment. For a person with excessive conceit, non-excessive conceit is for final extinguishment. For a person who is difficult to correct, the state of being easy to correct is for final extinguishment. For a person with bad friends, the state of having good friends is for final extinguishment. For a person who is heedless, heedfulness is for final extinguishment. For a person without faith, faith is for final extinguishment. For a person without moral shame, moral shame is for final extinguishment. For a person without moral dread, moral dread is for final extinguishment. For a person of little learning, the state of being of great learning is for final extinguishment. For a person who is lazy, the undertaking of energy is for final extinguishment. For a person of lapsed mindfulness, the state of having established mindfulness is for final extinguishment. For a person of little wisdom, accomplishment in wisdom is for final extinguishment. For a person who clings to their own views, holds to them firmly, and relinquishes them with difficulty, the state of not clinging to one's own views, not holding to them firmly, and relinquishing them with ease is for final extinguishment.

88. “Iti kho, cunda, desito mayā sallekhapariyāyo, desito cittuppādapariyāyo, desito parikkamanapariyāyo, desito uparibhāgapariyāyo, desito parinibbānapariyāyo. Yaṃ kho, cunda, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. ‘Etāni, cunda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni, jhāyatha, cunda, mā pamādattha, mā pacchāvippaṭisārino ahuvattha’ – ayaṃ kho amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti.

88. Thus, Cunda, the discourse on effacement has been taught by me, the discourse on the arising of thought has been taught, the discourse on abandoning has been taught, the discourse on the higher stage has been taught, and the discourse on final extinguishment has been taught. Cunda, whatever should be done by a Teacher for his disciples, who seeks their welfare, who is compassionate, out of compassion—that has been done for you by me. Here, Cunda, are the roots of trees, here are empty dwellings. Meditate, Cunda, do not be heedless, do not be remorseful later. This is our instruction to you.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mahācundo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. The Venerable Mahācunda, pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Catuttālīsapadā vuttā, sandhayo pañca desitā;

Sallekho nāma suttanto, gambhīro sāgarūpamoti.

Forty-four points were spoken, five connections explained; the Suttanta named 'Effacement,' profound, like the ocean.

Sallekhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Sallekha Sutta, the eighth, is finished.

9. Sammādiṭṭhisuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Right View

89. Evaṃ [T 1.0085][M 1.0057][V 1.0059] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

89. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend!” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta then said this:

“‘Sammādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhī (sī. syā.) sammādiṭṭhī’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhamma”nti?

“‘Right view, right view,’ friends, it is said. To what extent, friends, is a noble disciple one of right view, whose view is straight, who is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this Good Dhamma?”

“Dūratopi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āgaccheyyāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṃ. Sādhu vatāyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Āyasmato sāriputtassa sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Tena hi, āvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

“Friends, we would come even from afar to the Venerable Sāriputta to learn the meaning of this statement. It would be good if the Venerable Sāriputta himself would clarify the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Venerable Sāriputta, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.” “Then, friends, listen and attend closely. I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta then said this:

“Yato kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako akusalañca pajānāti, akusalamūlañca pajānāti, kusalañca pajānāti, kusalamūlañca pajānāti [P 1.0047] – ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena [T 1.0086] samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhammaṃ. Katamaṃ panāvuso, akusalaṃ, katamaṃ akusalamūlaṃ, katamaṃ kusalaṃ, katamaṃ kusalamūlaṃ? Pāṇātipāto kho, āvuso, akusalaṃ, adinnādānaṃ akusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro akusalaṃ, musāvādo akusalaṃ, pisuṇā vācā pisuṇavācā (ka.) akusalaṃ, pharusā vācā pharusavācā (ka.) akusalaṃ, samphappalāpo akusalaṃ, abhijjhā akusalaṃ, byāpādo akusalaṃ, micchādiṭṭhi akusalaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso akusalaṃ. Katamañcāvuso, akusalamūlaṃ? Lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, akusalamūlaṃ.

“Friends, when a noble disciple understands the unwholesome and the root of the unwholesome, and understands the wholesome and the root of the wholesome, to that extent a noble disciple is one of right view, whose view is straight, who is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this Good Dhamma. And what, friends, is the unwholesome? What is the root of the unwholesome? What is the wholesome? What is the root of the wholesome? Taking life, friends, is unwholesome; taking what is not given is unwholesome; misconduct in sensual pleasures is unwholesome; false speech is unwholesome; slanderous speech is unwholesome; harsh speech is unwholesome; idle chatter is unwholesome; covetousness is unwholesome; ill will is unwholesome; wrong view is unwholesome—this, friends, is called the unwholesome. And what, friends, is the root of the unwholesome? Greed is a root of the unwholesome, hatred is a root of the unwholesome, delusion is a root of the unwholesome. This, friends, is called the root of the unwholesome.

“Katamañcāvuso[M 1.0058][V 1.0060], kusalaṃ? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, anabhijjhā kusalaṃ, abyāpādo kusalaṃ, sammādiṭṭhi kusalaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, kusalaṃ. Katamañcāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ? Alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ.

“And what, friends, is the wholesome? Abstinence from taking life is wholesome; abstinence from taking what is not given is wholesome; abstinence from misconduct in sensual pleasures is wholesome; abstinence from false speech is wholesome; abstinence from slanderous speech is wholesome; abstinence from harsh speech is wholesome; abstinence from idle chatter is wholesome; non-covetousness is wholesome; non-ill will is wholesome; right view is wholesome. This, friends, is called the wholesome. And what, friends, is the root of the wholesome? Non-greed is a root of the wholesome, non-hatred is a root of the wholesome, non-delusion is a root of the wholesome. This, friends, is called the root of the wholesome.”

“Yato kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako evaṃ akusalaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ akusalamūlaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ kusalaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ kusalamūlaṃ pajānāti, so sabbaso rāgānusayaṃ pahāya, paṭighānusayaṃ paṭivinodetvā, ‘asmī’ti diṭṭhimānānusayaṃ samūhanitvā, avijjaṃ pahāya vijjaṃ uppādetvā, diṭṭhevadhamme dukkhassantakaro hoti – ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena [T 1.0087] samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhamma”nti.

“Friends, when a noble disciple thus understands the unwholesome, thus understands the root of the unwholesome, thus understands the wholesome, and thus understands the root of the wholesome, he, having entirely abandoned the underlying tendency to lust, having dispelled the underlying tendency to aversion, having uprooted the underlying tendency of the view and conceit ‘I am,’ having abandoned ignorance and aroused true knowledge, makes an end of suffering in this very life. To that extent also, friends, a noble disciple is one of right view, whose view is straight, who is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this Good Dhamma.”

90. “Sādhāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ uttari uttariṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pañhaṃ apucchuṃ apucchiṃsu (syā.) – “siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo yathā ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhamma”nti?
