182. “No [M 1.0135] cepi, āvuso, bhikkhu pavāreti – ‘vadantu maṃ āyasmanto, vacanīyomhi āyasmantehī’ti, so ca hoti suvaco, sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī vattabbañceva maññanti, anusāsitabbañca maññanti, tasmiñca puggale vissāsaṃ āpajjitabbaṃ maññanti.

182. Friends, even if a bhikkhu does not invite correction, saying, ‘May the venerable ones correct me; I am to be corrected by the venerable ones,’ yet he is easy to correct, possesses qualities that make him easy to correct, is tolerant, and accepts instruction respectfully, then his companions in the holy life consider him fit to be spoken to, fit to be instructed, and they think it fit to place trust in that person.

“Katame cāvuso, sovacassakaraṇā dhammā? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu na pāpiccho hoti, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na pāpiccho hoti na [T 1.0192] pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

And what, friends, are the qualities that make one easy to correct? Here, friends, a bhikkhu does not have evil desires; he has not fallen under the sway of evil desires. Friends, that a bhikkhu does not have evil desires and has not fallen under the sway of evil desires—this, too, is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu anattukkaṃsako hoti aparavambhī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu anattukkaṃsako hoti aparavambhī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu does not exalt himself or disparage others. Friends, that a bhikkhu does not exalt himself or disparage others—this, too, is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhābhibhūto. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhābhibhūto – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor overcome by anger. That a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor overcome by anger—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu upanāhī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu upanāhī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor, due to anger, harbors resentment. That a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor, due to anger, harbors resentment—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor, due to anger, clings to it. That a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor, due to anger, clings to it—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā. Yampāvuso[V 1.0136], bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor does he utter speech bordering on anger. That a bhikkhu is not prone to anger, nor does he utter speech bordering on anger—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharati. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharati – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo[T 1.0193].

Furthermore, friends, when a bhikkhu is admonished by an admonisher, he does not admonish in return. That a bhikkhu, when admonished by an admonisher, does not admonish in return—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna [M 1.0136] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādeti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādeti – ayampi dhammo [P 1.0097] sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, when a bhikkhu is admonished by an admonisher, he does not disparage the admonisher. That a bhikkhu, when admonished by an admonisher, does not disparage the admonisher—this too is a quality that makes one easy to correct.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakassa na paccāropeti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakassa na paccāropeti – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, when a bhikkhu is admonished by an admonisher, he does not accuse the admonisher in return. That a bhikkhu, when admonished by an admonisher, does not accuse the admonisher in return—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, when a bhikkhu is admonished by an admonisher, he does not evade the issue by raising another, nor does he lead the discussion astray, nor does he manifest anger, greater anger, and displeasure. That a bhikkhu, when admonished by an admonisher, does not evade the issue by raising another, nor does he lead the discussion astray, nor does he manifest anger, greater anger, and displeasure—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena apadāne sampāyati. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena apadāne sampāyati – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, when a bhikkhu is admonished by an admonisher, he can give a satisfactory account of his conduct. That a bhikkhu, when admonished by an admonisher, can give a satisfactory account of his conduct—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not contemptuous nor contentious. That a bhikkhu is not contemptuous nor contentious—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu anissukī hoti amaccharī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu anissukī hoti amaccharī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not envious and not stingy. That a bhikkhu is not envious and not stingy—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna [V 1.0137] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti amāyāvī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti amāyāvī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not deceitful and not crafty. That a bhikkhu is not deceitful and not crafty—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu atthaddho hoti anatimānī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu atthaddho hoti anatimānī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not stubborn and not excessively conceited. That a bhikkhu is not stubborn and not excessively conceited—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti, anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī [M 1.0137] – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo. Ime vuccantāvuso, sovacassakaraṇā dhammā.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is not one who clings to his own views, is not one who holds on stubbornly, and is one who relinquishes easily. That a bhikkhu is not one who clings to his own views, is not one who holds on stubbornly, and is one who relinquishes easily—this too is a quality that makes one easy to admonish. These, friends, are called the qualities that make one easy to admonish.

183. “Tatrāvuso[T 1.0194], bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ anuminitabbaṃ anumānitabbaṃ (sī.) – ‘yo khvāyaṃ puggalo pāpiccho, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ pāpiccho pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na pāpiccho bhavissāmi, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

183. In this regard, friends, a bhikkhu should infer about himself by himself thus: ‘Whatever person has evil wishes and has come under the sway of evil wishes, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to have evil wishes and come under the sway of evil wishes, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not have evil wishes, nor will I come under the sway of evil wishes.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo attukkaṃsako paravambhī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ attukkaṃsako paravambhī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘anattukkaṃsako bhavissāmi aparavambhī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person exalts himself and disparages others, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to exalt myself and disparage others, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be one who exalts himself or disparages others.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhābhibhūto, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo. Ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhābhibhūto, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhābhibhūto’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person is prone to anger and is overcome by anger, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to be prone to anger and be overcome by anger, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be prone to anger, nor will I be overcome by anger.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhahetu upanāhī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person is prone to anger and, due to anger, harbors resentment, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to be prone to anger and, due to anger, harbor resentment, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be prone to anger, nor will I, due to anger, harbor resentment.’

“‘Yo [V 1.0138] khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva [T 1.0195] kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person is prone to anger and, due to anger, clings to it, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to be prone to anger and, due to anger, cling to it, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be prone to anger, nor will I, due to anger, cling to it.’

“‘Yo [M 1.0138] khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāressāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person is prone to anger and utters speech connected with anger, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself were to be prone to anger and utter speech connected with anger, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be prone to anger, nor will I utter speech connected with anger.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakaṃ paṭippharati, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakaṃ paṭipphareyyaṃ[P 1.0098], ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person, when admonished by an admonisher, retorts, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself, when admonished by an admonisher, were to retort, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘When admonished by an admonisher, I will not retort.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakaṃ apasādeti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakaṃ apasādeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādessāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person, when admonished by an admonisher, disparages the admonisher, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself, when admonished by an admonisher, were to disparage the admonisher, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘When admonished by an admonisher, I will not disparage the admonisher.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakassa paccāropeti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakassa paccāropeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ [T 1.0196] jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakassa na paccāropessāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘Whatever person, when admonished by an admonisher, accuses the admonisher in return, that person is unloved and disagreeable to me. If I myself, when admonished by an admonisher, were to accuse the admonisher in return, I too would be unloved and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a bhikkhu should arouse the thought: ‘When admonished by an admonisher, I will not accuse the admonisher in return.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicareyyaṃ, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeyyaṃ[V 1.0139], kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukareyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissāmi, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmessāmi, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukarissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who, when admonished by an admonisher, retorts evasively, deflects the discussion, and displays anger, ill will, and displeasure is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too, when admonished by an admonisher, were to retort evasively, deflect the discussion, and display anger, ill will, and displeasure, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘When admonished by an admonisher, I will not retort evasively, nor will I deflect the discussion, nor will I display anger, ill will, or displeasure.’

“‘Yo [M 1.0139] khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena apadāne na sampāyati, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena apadāne na sampāyeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena apadāne sampāyissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who, when admonished by an admonisher, is unable to give a satisfactory account of his conduct is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too, when admonished by an admonisher, were unable to give a satisfactory account of my conduct, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘When admonished by an admonisher, I will give a satisfactory account of my conduct.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo makkhī paḷāsī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ makkhī paḷāsī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘amakkhī bhavissāmi apaḷāsī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who is contemptuous and contentious is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too were to be contemptuous and contentious, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be contemptuous and I will not be contentious.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo issukī maccharī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ [T 1.0197] issukī maccharī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘anissukī bhavissāmi amaccharī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who is envious and stingy is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too were to be envious and stingy, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be envious and I will not be stingy.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo saṭho māyāvī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ saṭho māyāvī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘asaṭho bhavissāmi amāyāvī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who is deceitful and crafty is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too were to be deceitful and crafty, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘I will not be deceitful and I will not be crafty.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo thaddho atimānī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ thaddho atimānī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘atthaddho bhavissāmi anatimānī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who is stubborn and conceited is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too were to be stubborn and conceited, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘I will be neither stubborn nor conceited.’

“‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī bhavissāmi anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘That person who clings to his own views, holds to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty, is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I too were to cling to my own views, hold to them tenaciously, and relinquish them with difficulty, I too would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ Knowing this, friends, a monk should arouse the thought: ‘I will not cling to my own views, I will not hold to them tenaciously, and I will relinquish them with ease.’

184. “Tatrāvuso[V 1.0140], bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi pāpiccho, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti? Sace, āvuso[M 1.0140], bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘pāpiccho khomhi, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno [T 1.0198] evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi pāpiccho, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

184. ‘Therein, friends, a monk should reflect on himself by himself thus: “Am I of evil desires? Have I come under the sway of evil desires?” If, friends, a monk, while reflecting, knows thus: “I am of evil desires; I have come under the sway of evil desires,” then, friends, that monk should strive for the abandoning of those same evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a monk, while reflecting, knows thus: “I am not of evil desires; I have not come under the sway of evil desires,” then, friends, that monk should dwell with that same joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.’

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi attukkaṃsako paravambhī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘attukkaṃsako khomhi paravambhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anattukkaṃsako [P 1.0099] khomhi aparavambhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a monk should reflect on himself thus: ‘Am I one who exalts myself and belittles others?’ If, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am one who exalts myself and belittles others,’ then, friends, that monk should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am not one who exalts myself or belittles others,’ then, friends, that monk should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhābhibhūto’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhābhibhūto’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhābhibhūto’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a monk should reflect on himself thus: ‘Am I prone to anger, overcome by anger?’ If, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am prone to anger, overcome by anger,’ then, friends, that monk should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am not prone to anger, not overcome by anger,’ then, friends, that monk should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘kodhano khomhi kodhahetu upanāhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva [T 1.0199] pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a monk should reflect on himself thus: ‘Am I prone to anger and, on account of anger, given to resentment?’ If, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am prone to anger and, on account of anger, given to resentment,’ then, friends, that monk should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon reflecting, a monk knows: ‘I am not prone to anger and, on account of anger, not given to resentment,’ then, friends, that monk should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna [M 1.0141][V 1.0141] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘Am I prone to anger and, on account of anger, given to hostility?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘I am prone to anger and, on account of anger, given to hostility,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘I am not prone to anger and, on account of anger, not given to hostility,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘Am I prone to anger and one who utters speech bordering on anger?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘I am prone to anger and one who utters speech bordering on anger,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘I am not prone to anger, nor one who utters speech bordering on anger,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakaṃ [T 1.0200] paṭippharāmī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ paṭippharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘When censured by a critic, do I retaliate against the critic?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I retaliate against the critic,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I do not retaliate against the critic,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakaṃ apasādemī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ apasādemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ [M 1.0142] na apasādemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘When censured by a critic, do I disparage the critic?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I disparage the critic,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I do not disparage the critic,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakassa paccāropemī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno [V 1.0142] evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakassa paccāropemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakassa na paccāropemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena [T 1.0201] vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘When censured by a critic, do I accuse the critic in turn?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I accuse the critic in turn,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I do not accuse the critic in turn,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘When censured by a critic, do I answer beside the point, turn the talk aside, and manifest anger, ill will, and displeasure?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I answer beside the point, turn the talk aside, and manifest anger, ill will, and displeasure,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I do not answer beside the point, do not turn the talk aside, and do not manifest anger, ill will, and displeasure,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena apadāne na sampāyāmī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena apadāne na sampāyāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena apadāne sampāyāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should examine himself thus: ‘When censured by a critic, am I unable to give a satisfactory account of my conduct?’ If, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I am unable to give a satisfactory account of my conduct,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, upon examination, a bhikkhu knows: ‘When censured by a critic, I am able to give a satisfactory account of my conduct,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

“Puna [M 1.0143] caparaṃ[T 1.0202], āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi makkhī paḷāsī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘makkhī khomhi paḷāsī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘amakkhī khomhi apaḷāsī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should reflect upon himself thus: ‘Am I denigrating and rivalrous?’ If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am denigrating and rivalrous,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am not denigrating and not rivalrous,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Puna [V 1.0143] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi issukī maccharī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘issukī khomhi maccharī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anissukī khomhi amaccharī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should reflect upon himself thus: ‘Am I envious and stingy?’ If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am envious and stingy,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am not envious and not stingy,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi saṭho māyāvī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘saṭho khomhi māyāvī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘asaṭho khomhi amāyāvī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should reflect upon himself thus: ‘Am I fraudulent and deceptive?’ If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am fraudulent and deceptive,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am not fraudulent and not deceptive,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ [T 1.0203] – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi thaddho atimānī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘thaddho khomhi atimānī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘atthaddho khomhi anatimānī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should reflect upon himself thus: ‘Am I stubborn and conceited?’ If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am stubborn and conceited,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am not stubborn and not conceited,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī’ti? Sace, āvuso[M 1.0144], bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī khomhi ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā [P 1.0100] tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī khomhi anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should reflect upon himself thus: ‘Am I one who clings to my own views, is obstinate, and relinquishes them with difficulty?’ If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am one who clings to my own views, is obstinate, and relinquishes them with difficulty,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I am not one who clings to my own views, am not obstinate, and relinquish them with ease,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Sace[V 1.0144], āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ, ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

If, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, sees all these evil, unwholesome states as unabandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of all these very evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, sees all these evil, unwholesome states as abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, itthī [T 1.0204] vā puriso vā, daharo yuvā maṇḍanajātiko, ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte, acche vā udakapatte, sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno, sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati; no ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, teneva attamano hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evameva kho, āvuso, sace bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ, ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesū”ti.

Just as, friends, a woman or a man, young, youthful, and fond of adornment, while examining their own facial image in a pure, bright mirror or in a bowl of clear water, if they see any dust or blemish there, they strive for the abandoning of that very dust or blemish. But if they do not see any dust or blemish there, for that very reason they are glad, thinking: ‘It is a gain for me! I am indeed pure!’ In this very way, friends, if a bhikkhu, upon examination, sees all these evil, unwholesome states as not abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive for the abandoning of all these evil, unwholesome states. But if, friends, a bhikkhu, upon examination, sees all these evil, unwholesome states as abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should dwell with that very joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

Idamavocāyasmā mahāmoggallāno. Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this. Those bhikkhus, being pleased, greatly rejoiced in the words of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna.

Anumānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Discourse on Inference, the fifth, is concluded.

6. Cetokhilasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Mental Barrenness

185. Evaṃ [T 1.0205][M 1.0145][V 1.0145][P 1.0101] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

185. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this:

“Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañca cetokhilā appahīnā, pañca cetasovinibandhā cetasovinibaddhā (sī.), cetovinibaddhā (sāratthadīpanīṭīkā) asamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

Bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu whatsoever for whom the five mental barrennesses are not abandoned and the five bonds of the mind are not severed, that he will attain growth, increase, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“Katamāssa pañca cetokhilā appahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

What are the five mental spikes that have not been abandoned by him? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the Teacher, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who doubts the Teacher, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence, his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, this is the first mental spike that has not been abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the Dhamma, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence... Thus, this is the second mental spike that has not been abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the Saṅgha, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence... Thus, this is the third mental spike that has not been abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ na namati [T 1.0206] ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ [V 1.0146] na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the training, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence. For that bhikkhu who doubts the training, is uncertain, is not resolved, and does not gain confidence, his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this is the fourth mental spike that has not been abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati [M 1.0146] ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetokhilā appahīnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is angry and displeased with his companions in the holy life, with a resentful mind, and has become barren-minded. For that bhikkhu who is angry and displeased with his companions in the holy life, with a resentful mind, and has become barren-minded, his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this is the fifth mental spike that has not been abandoned by him. These are the five mental spikes that have not been abandoned by him.

186. “Katamāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme avītarāgo avigatarāgo (katthaci) hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

186. What are the five bonds of the mind that have not been severed by him? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not rid of passion for sensual pleasures; he is not free from desire, not free from affection, not free from thirst, not free from fever, and not free from craving for them. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who is not rid of passion for sensual pleasures, who is not free from desire, not free from affection, not free from thirst, not free from fever, and not free from craving for them, his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this is the first bond of the mind that has not been severed by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not rid of passion for the body... Thus, this is the second bond of the mind that has not been severed by him.

“Puna [P 1.0102] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpe avītarāgo hoti…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno [T 1.0207] hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not rid of passion for form... Thus, this is the third bond of the mind that has not been severed by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having eaten his fill, dwells devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lying on his side, and the pleasure of sleep. For that bhikkhu who, having eaten his fill, dwells devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lying on his side, and the pleasure of sleep, his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this is the fourth bond of the mind that has not been severed by him.

“Puna [V 1.0147] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya[M 1.0147]. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu practices the holy life aspiring to a certain celestial realm, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or by this observance, or by this austerity, or by this holy life, I shall become a deva or a deva of some other kind.’ Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who practices the holy life aspiring to a certain celestial realm, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or by this observance, or by this austerity, or by this holy life, I shall become a deva or a deva of some other kind,’ his mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this is the fifth bond of the mind that has not been severed by him. These are the five bonds of the mind that have not been severed by him.

“Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ime pañca cetokhilā appahīnā, ime pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

Bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu by whom these five mental spikes have not been abandoned and these five bonds of the mind have not been severed, that he will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

187. “Yassa [T 1.0208] kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañca cetokhilā pahīnā, pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

187. Bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu by whom these five mental spikes have been abandoned and these five bonds of the mind have been well severed, that he will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“Katamāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

What are the five mental spikes that have been abandoned by him? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the Teacher, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is serene. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who does not doubt the Teacher, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is serene, his mind inclines towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind inclines towards ardour, application, perseverance, and striving, thus, this first mental spike has been abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the Dhamma, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is serene... Thus, this second spike of the mind is abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghe na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the Sangha, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is serene... Thus, this third spike of the mind is abandoned by him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the training, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is serene... Thus, this fourth spike of the mind is abandoned by him.

“Puna [V 1.0148] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti na anattamano attamano (sī. pī.) anāhatacitto akhilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti na anattamano anāhatacitto akhilajāto, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya [P 1.0103] anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ [T 1.0209] pañcamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not angry with his companions in the holy life, is not displeased, has a mind not struck by anger, and has not become obstinate. Bhikkhus, for whichever bhikkhu is not angry with his companions in the holy life, is not displeased, has a mind not struck by anger, and has not become obstinate, his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For whomsoever the mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, thus this fifth spike of the mind is abandoned by him. These five spikes of the mind are abandoned by him.

188. “Katamāssa [M 1.0148] pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti.

188. What are the five bondages of the mind that are well cut off by him? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is without lust for sensual pleasures, without desire, without affection, without thirst, without burning, and without craving. Bhikkhus, for whichever bhikkhu is without lust for sensual pleasures, without desire, without affection, without thirst, without burning, and without craving, his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For whomsoever the mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, thus this first bondage of the mind is well cut off for him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye vītarāgo hoti…pe… rūpe vītarāgo hoti…pe… na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is without lust for the body... is without lust for form... does not, having eaten as much as he desires to fill his belly, dwell devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of reclining, and the pleasure of sleep. Bhikkhus, for whichever bhikkhu does not, having eaten as much as he desires to fill his belly, dwell devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of reclining, and the pleasure of sleep, his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For whomsoever the mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, thus this fourth bondage of the mind is well cut off for him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro [T 1.0210] vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not practice the holy life aspiring to a certain celestial realm, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or by this observance, or by this austerity, or by this celibacy, I shall become a powerful deva or one of the lesser devas.’ Bhikkhus, for whichever bhikkhu does not practice the holy life aspiring to a certain celestial realm, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or by this observance, or by this austerity, or by this celibacy, I shall become a powerful deva or one of the lesser devas,’ his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For whomsoever the mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, thus this fifth bondage of the mind is well cut off for him. These five bondages of the mind are well cut off for him.

“Yassa [V 1.0149] kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ime pañca cetokhilā pahīnā, ime pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

Bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu for whom these five spikes of the mind are abandoned and these five bondages of the mind are well cut off, that this bhikkhu will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

189. “So chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [M 1.0149] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, ussoḷhīyeva pañcamī. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, evaṃ ussoḷhīpannarasaṅgasamannāgato [P 1.0104] bhikkhu bhabbo abhinibbidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā. Tānassu kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitāni sammā pariseditāni sammā paribhāvitāni. Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vatime kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ [T 1.0211] padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyu’nti. Atha kho bhabbāva te kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, evaṃ ussoḷhipannarasaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo abhinibbidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti.

189. He develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration of desire, accompanied by the formations of striving. He develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration of energy, accompanied by the formations of striving. He develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration of mind, accompanied by the formations of striving. He develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration of investigation, accompanied by the formations of striving, with exertion as the fifth. Indeed, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu thus endowed with these fifteen factors including exertion is capable of penetration, capable of full enlightenment, capable of attaining the unsurpassed security from bondage. Suppose, bhikkhus, a hen has eight, ten, or twelve eggs. They are properly brooded over by the hen and properly warmed. Even if that hen does not have such a wish as: 'Oh, may these chicks pierce the eggshell with their claw-tips or beak-tips and hatch safely!' Still, those chicks are capable of piercing the eggshell with their claw-tips or beak-tips and hatching safely. In the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu thus endowed with these fifteen factors including exertion is capable of penetration, capable of full enlightenment, capable of attaining the unsurpassed security from bondage.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

This is what the Blessed One said. The bhikkhus, being pleased, greatly rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Cetokhilasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Discourse on Mental Barrenness, the Sixth, is finished.

7. Vanapatthasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Forest Wilderness

190. Evaṃ [V 1.0150][T 1.0212] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “vanapatthapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

190. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Monks, I shall teach you the discourse on the forest thicket. Listen to it and pay close attention. I shall speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

191. “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca [M 1.0150] cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ [P 1.0105] – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi, tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā [T 1.0213] samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vā tamhā vanapatthā pakkamitabbaṃ, na vatthabbaṃ.

191. “Here, monks, a monk dwells depending on a certain forest thicket. For him, while dwelling depending on that forest thicket, unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, and he does not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that he has not yet attained. And these requisites of life that should be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty. Monks, that monk should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling depending on this forest thicket. For me, while dwelling depending on this forest thicket, unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, and I do not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that I have not yet attained. And these requisites of life that should be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.’ Monks, that monk should depart from that forest thicket, whether by night or by day; he should not dwell there.

192. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena[V 1.0151], bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Atha ca pana me imaṃ [T 1.0214] vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi tamhā vanapatthā pakkamitabbaṃ, na vatthabbaṃ.

192. “But here, monks, a monk dwells depending on a certain forest thicket. For him, while dwelling depending on that forest thicket, unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, and he does not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that he has not yet attained. And these requisites of life that should be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty. Monks, that monk should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling depending on this forest thicket. For me, while dwelling depending on this forest thicket, unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, and I do not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that I have not yet attained. And these requisites of life that should be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty. But I did not go forth from the household life into homelessness for the sake of robes, nor for almsfood, nor for lodging, nor for medicinal supplies for the sick. And yet, for me, while dwelling depending on this forest thicket, unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, and I do not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that I have not yet attained.’ Monks, that monk, after reflecting, should depart from that forest thicket; he should not dwell there.

193. “Idha [M 1.0151] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā, te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ [P 1.0106] – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito[T 1.0215]. Atha ca pana me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi tasmiṃ vanapatthe vatthabbaṃ, na pakkamitabbaṃ.

193. Here, monks, a bhikkhu dwells depending on a certain forest grove. While he is dwelling depending on that forest grove, mindfulness that was previously unestablished becomes established, his mind that was previously unconcentrated becomes concentrated, his taints that were previously unexhausted go to exhaustion, and he attains the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise with difficulty. Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling depending on this forest grove. While I am dwelling depending on this forest grove, mindfulness that was previously unestablished becomes established, my mind that was previously unconcentrated becomes concentrated, my taints that were previously unexhausted go to exhaustion, and I attain the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise with difficulty. Indeed, I did not go forth from the household life into the homeless life for the sake of robes, nor for the sake of alms-food, nor for the sake of lodging, nor for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick. And yet, while I am dwelling depending on this forest grove, mindfulness that was previously unestablished becomes established, my mind that was previously unconcentrated becomes concentrated, my taints that were previously unexhausted go to exhaustion, and I attain the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained.’ Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu, having considered thus, should dwell in that very forest grove; he should not depart.

194. “Idha [V 1.0152] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchantī’ti[M 1.0152]. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yāvajīvampi tasmiṃ vanapatthe vatthabbaṃ, na pakkamitabbaṃ.

194. Here, monks, a bhikkhu dwells depending on a certain forest grove. While he is dwelling depending on that forest grove, mindfulness that was previously unestablished becomes established, his mind that was previously unconcentrated becomes concentrated, his taints that were previously unexhausted go to exhaustion, and he attains the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise without difficulty. Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling depending on this forest grove. While I am dwelling depending on this forest grove, mindfulness that was previously unestablished becomes established, my mind that was previously unconcentrated becomes concentrated, my taints that were previously unexhausted go to exhaustion, and I attain the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise without difficulty.’ Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should dwell in that very forest grove for his entire life; he should not depart.

195. “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upanissāya viharati [T 1.0216] …pe… aññataraṃ nigamaṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ nagaraṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ janapadaṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vā so puggalo anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṃ, nānubandhitabbo.

195. Here, monks, a bhikkhu dwells depending on a certain village... or on a certain town... or on a certain city... or on a certain district... or on a certain person. While he is dwelling depending on that person, mindfulness that was previously unestablished does not become established, his mind that was previously unconcentrated does not become concentrated, his taints that were previously unexhausted do not go to exhaustion, and he does not attain the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise with difficulty. Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling depending on this person. While I am dwelling depending on this person, mindfulness that was previously unestablished does not become established, my mind that was previously unconcentrated does not become concentrated, my taints that were previously unexhausted do not go to exhaustion, and I do not attain the supreme security from bondage which had not been attained. And those requisites of life which are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—arise with difficulty.’ Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should depart from that person without taking leave, either by night or by day; he should not continue to associate with him.

196. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ [V 1.0153] puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā [P 1.0107] ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca [T 1.0217] āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā, te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā [M 1.0153] – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Atha ca pana me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi so puggalo āpucchā pakkamitabbaṃ, nānubandhitabbo.

196. Here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence on a certain person. For him, dwelling in dependence on that person, unarisen mindfulness does not arise, an unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, unexhausted taints do not reach exhaustion, and he does not attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty. Then, monks, that monk should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling in dependence on this person. For me, dwelling in dependence on this person, unarisen mindfulness does not arise, an unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, unexhausted taints do not reach exhaustion, and I do not attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty. But I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, nor for the sake of almsfood, nor for the sake of lodging, nor for the sake of medicinal supplies for the sick. And yet, for me, dwelling in dependence on this person, unarisen mindfulness does not arise, an unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, unexhausted taints do not reach exhaustion, and I do not attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage.’ Then, monks, that monk, having reflected thus, should take leave of that person and depart; he should not continue to associate with him.

197. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca [T 1.0218] cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā [V 1.0154] anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Atha ca pana me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi so puggalo anubandhitabbo, na pakkamitabbaṃ.

197. Here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence on a certain person. For him, dwelling in dependence on that person, unarisen mindfulness arises, an unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, unexhausted taints reach exhaustion, and he attains the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty. Then, monks, that monk should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling in dependence on this person. For me, dwelling in dependence on this person, unarisen mindfulness arises, an unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, unexhausted taints reach exhaustion, and I attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty. But I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, nor for the sake of almsfood, nor for the sake of lodging, nor for the sake of medicinal supplies for the sick. And yet, for me, dwelling in dependence on this person, unarisen mindfulness arises, an unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, unexhausted taints reach exhaustion, and I attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage.’ Then, monks, that monk, having reflected thus, should continue to associate with that person; he should not depart.

198. “Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati [T 1.0219] upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti[M 1.0154], ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi[P 1.0108]. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yāvajīvampi so puggalo anubandhitabbo, na pakkamitabbaṃ, api panujjamānenapī”ti api paṇujjamānenāti (?).

198. Here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence on a certain person. For him, dwelling in dependence on that person, unarisen mindfulness arises, an unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, unexhausted taints reach exhaustion, and he attains the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty. Then, monks, that monk should reflect thus: ‘I am dwelling in dependence on this person. For me, dwelling in dependence on this person, unarisen mindfulness arises, an unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, unexhausted taints reach exhaustion, and I attain the unattained, supreme security from bondage. And those requisites of life that are to be acquired by one who has gone forth—robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.’ Then, monks, that monk should associate with that person for his entire life; he should not depart, even if being driven away.
