Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho itipi, saṃkiṇṇaparikkho itipi, abbūḷhesiko itipi, niraggaḷo itipi, ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto itipi.

245. “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with formations, disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ This, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who has lifted the cross-bar, who has filled in the moat, who has uprooted the pillar, who is unbolted; a noble one with banner lowered, burden dropped, unfettered.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjā pahīnā hoti, ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā, āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one who has lifted the cross-bar? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s ignorance is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, of a nature not to arise again in the future. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has lifted the cross-bar.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṃkiṇṇaparikkho hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ponobbhaviko [V 1.0194] jātisaṃsāro pahīno hoti, ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato, āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṃkiṇṇaparikkho hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one who has filled in the moat? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s round of births that leads to renewed existence is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, of a nature not to arise again in the future. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has filled in the moat.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbūḷhesiko hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti, ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā, āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbūḷhesiko hoti.

And how, monks, is a monk one who has uprooted the stake? Here, monks, a monk has abandoned craving, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, brought it to a state of non-existence, so that it is of a nature not to arise again in the future. Thus, monks, a monk is one who has uprooted the stake.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niraggaḷo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañca orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni honti, ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṃkatāni, āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni[M 1.0193]. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niraggaḷo hoti.

And how, monks, is a monk one who is without a bolt? Here, monks, a monk has abandoned the five lower fetters, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, brought them to a state of non-existence, so that they are of a nature not to arise again in the future. Thus, monks, a monk is one who is without a bolt.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno asmimāno pahīno hoti, ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato[T 1.0278], āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo[P 1.0140]. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hoti.

And how, monks, is a monk a noble one with lowered banner, with burden laid down, and unfettered? Here, monks, a monk has abandoned the conceit 'I am,' cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, brought it to a state of non-existence, so that it is of a nature not to arise again in the future. Thus, monks, a monk is a noble one with lowered banner, with burden laid down, and unfettered.

246. “Evaṃ vimuttacittaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saindā devā sabrahmakā sapajāpatikā anvesaṃ nādhigacchanti – ‘idaṃ nissitaṃ tathāgatassa viññāṇa’nti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Diṭṭhevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dhamme tathāgataṃ ananuvijjoti vadāmi. Evaṃvādiṃ kho maṃ, bhikkhave, evamakkhāyiṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññāpetī’ti. Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhave bhikkhave na (sī. syā. pī.), yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmi, tathā maṃ te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññāpetī’ti. Pubbe cāhaṃ bhikkhave, etarahi ca dukkhañceva paññāpemi, dukkhassa ca nirodhaṃ. Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṃ akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa na hoti āghāto na appaccayo na cetaso anabhiraddhi.

246. Monks, when a monk's mind is thus liberated, the devas with Inda, with Brahmā, and with Pajāpati, do not find him when searching, thinking: 'The consciousness of the Tathāgata is dependent on this.' For what reason? I declare, monks, that a Tathāgata is untraceable even in this present life. Monks, though I speak thus and declare thus, some ascetics and brahmins misrepresent me with what is non-existent, empty, false, and untrue, saying: 'The ascetic Gotama is a destructionist; he teaches the cutting off, destruction, and perishing of an existing being.' In that I am not so, monks, and in that I do not declare so, those venerable ascetics and brahmins misrepresent me with what is non-existent, empty, false, and untrue, saying: 'The ascetic Gotama is a destructionist; he teaches the cutting off, destruction, and perishing of an existing being.' Both formerly and now, monks, I teach only suffering and the cessation of suffering. In that regard, monks, if others were to revile, abuse, scold, or harass the Tathāgata, on that account, monks, the Tathāgata has no anger, no displeasure, and no dissatisfaction of mind.

“Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṃ sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa na hoti ānando na somanassaṃ na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ. Tatra ce, bhikkhave[V 1.0195], pare [T 1.0279] vā tathāgataṃ sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ tattha me evarūpā kārā sakkārā (ka.) karīyantī’ti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare akkoseyyuṃ paribhāseyyuṃ roseyyuṃ viheseyyuṃ, tatra tumhe hi na āghāto na appaccayo na cetaso anabhiraddhi karaṇīyā. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyuṃ, tatra tumhehi na ānando na somanassaṃ na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ karaṇīyaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ [M 1.0194] kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyuṃ, tatra tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ, tattha me tattha no (ka.) tattha + imeti padacchedo evarūpā kārā karīyantī’ti.

In that regard, monks, if others were to honor, respect, revere, or venerate the Tathāgata, on that account, monks, the Tathāgata has no joy, no gladness, and no elation of mind. In that regard, monks, if others were to honor, respect, revere, or venerate the Tathāgata, on that account, monks, it occurs to the Tathāgata thus: 'In regard to that which was previously fully understood, such honors are being done to me.' Therefore, monks, if others were to revile, abuse, scold, or harass you, on that account you should not have anger, displeasure, or dissatisfaction of mind. Therefore, monks, if others were to honor, respect, revere, or venerate you, on that account you should not have joy, gladness, or elation of mind. Therefore, monks, if others were to honor, respect, revere, or venerate you, on that account it should occur to you thus: 'In regard to that which was previously fully understood, such honors are being done to us.'

247. “Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ [P 1.0141] pajahatha; sā vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saññā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; sā vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saṅkhārā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, te pajahatha; te vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissanti. Viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, yaṃ [T 1.0280] imasmiṃ jetavane tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ, taṃ jano hareyya vā daheyya vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā kareyya. Api nu tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘amhe jano harati vā dahati vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā karotī’ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Na hi no etaṃ, bhante, attā vā attaniyaṃ vā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā, bhikkhave…pe… saññā, bhikkhave… saṅkhārā, bhikkhave…pe… viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.

247. Therefore, monks, abandon what is not yours. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. Feeling, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. Perception, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. Formations, monks, are not yours; abandon them. Their abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. Consciousness, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. What do you think, monks? If people were to carry away, burn, or do as they please with the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves in this Jeta's Grove, would it occur to you: 'People are carrying us away, burning us, or doing as they please with us'?' 'No, venerable sir.' 'For what reason?' 'Because, venerable sir, that is not our self nor what belongs to our self.' Even so, monks, abandon what is not yours. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time. Feeling, monks... Perception, monks... Formations, monks... Consciousness, monks, is not yours; abandon it. Its abandonment will be for your welfare and happiness for a long time.

248. “Evaṃ [V 1.0196] svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike ye te bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni [M 1.0195] pahīnāni, sabbe te opapātikā, tattha [T 1.0281] parinibbāyino, anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, rāgadosamohā tanubhūtā, sabbe te sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, sabbe te sotāpannā, avinipātadhammā[P 1.0142], niyatā sambodhiparāyanā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike ye te bhikkhū dhammānusārino saddhānusārino sabbe te sambodhiparāyanā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamattaṃ sabbe te saggaparāyanā”ti.

248. “Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, for those monks who are arahants—whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and are liberated through right knowledge—there is no round of existence to be designated for them. Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, for those monks whose five lower fetters have been abandoned—all are of spontaneous birth, due to attain final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world. Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, for those monks whose three fetters have been abandoned and for whom greed, hatred, and delusion are attenuated—all are once-returners who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering. Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, for those monks whose three fetters have been abandoned—all are stream-enterers, not liable to states of deprivation, certain, and destined for enlightenment. Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, those monks who are Dhamma-followers or faith-followers—all are destined for enlightenment. Thus, monks, the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by me—made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork. In this Dhamma so well-proclaimed by me, monks, made plain, laid open, revealed, and stripped of patchwork, those for whom there is mere faith in me, mere affection for me—all are destined for heaven.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Being pleased, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

Alagaddūpamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second, the Discourse on the Simile of the Water Snake, is concluded.

3. Vammikasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Anthill

249. Evaṃ [T 1.0282][V 1.0197] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā kumārakassapo andhavane viharati. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ andhavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāyasmā kumārakassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā āyasmantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ etadavoca –

249. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the Venerable Kumārakassapa was dwelling in the Andha Grove. Then, when the night was far advanced, a certain deity of surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Andha Grove, approached the Venerable Kumārakassapa. Having approached, that deity stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity said this to the Venerable Kumārakassapa:

“Bhikkhu [M 1.0196] bhikkhu, ayaṃ vammiko vammīko (katthaci) sakkatānurūpaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa laṅgiṃ ‘laṅgī, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa laṅgiṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa uddhumāyikaṃ. ‘Uddhumāyikā, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa uddhumāyikaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa dvidhāpathaṃ. ‘Dvidhāpatho, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa dvidhāpathaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa caṅgavāraṃ paṅkavāraṃ (syā.), caṅkavāraṃ (ka.). ‘Caṅgavāro, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa [P 1.0143] caṅgavāraṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa kummaṃ. ‘Kummo[T 1.0283], bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa kummaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa asisūnaṃ. ‘Asisūnā, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa asisūnaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa maṃsapesiṃ. ‘Maṃsapesi, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa maṃsapesiṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa nāgaṃ. ‘Nāgo, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘tiṭṭhatu nāgo, mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesi; namo karohi nāgassā’”ti.

“Monk, monk, this anthill smokes by night and blazes by day. A brahmin said: ‘Take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a bar. ‘A bar, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the bar; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a toad. ‘A toad, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the toad; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a forked path. ‘A forked path, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the forked path; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a sieve. ‘A sieve, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the sieve; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a tortoise. ‘A tortoise, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the tortoise; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a butcher’s knife and block. ‘A butcher’s knife and block, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the butcher’s knife and block; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a lump of meat. ‘A lump of meat, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Lift up the lump of meat; take up the knife and dig, wise one!’ The wise one took up the knife and, digging, saw a serpent. ‘A serpent, venerable sir.’ The brahmin said: ‘Let the serpent be; do not harm the serpent. Pay homage to the serpent.’”

“Ime [V 1.0198] kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pañhe bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyāsi, yathā ca te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāsi. Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhu, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya aññatra tathāgatena vā, tathāgatasāvakena vā, ito vā pana sutvā”ti – idamavoca sā devatā. Idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi.

“You, monk, should approach the Blessed One and ask about these questions. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should bear it in mind. For I do not see anyone, monk, in this world with its deities, its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its deities and humans, who could satisfy the mind with an explanation of these questions, other than the Tathāgata, or a disciple of the Tathāgata, or one who has heard it from them.” This is what that deity said. Having said this, that deity vanished right there.

250. Atha kho āyasmā kumārakassapo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā kumārakassapo bhagavantaṃ [M 1.0197] etadavoca – “imaṃ, bhante, rattiṃ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ andhavanaṃ obhāsetvā [T 1.0284] yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho, bhante, sā devatā maṃ etadavoca – ‘bhikkhu bhikkhu, ayaṃ vammiko rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati’. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya…pe… ito vā pana sutvāti. Idamavoca, bhante, sā devatā. Idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi. ‘Ko nu kho, bhante, vammiko, kā rattiṃ dhūmāyanā, kā divā pajjalanā, ko brāhmaṇo, ko sumedho, kiṃ satthaṃ, kiṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ, kā laṅgī, kā uddhumāyikā, ko dvidhāpatho, kiṃ caṅgavāraṃ, ko kummo, kā asisūnā[T 1.0285], kā maṃsapesi, ko nāgo’”ti?

250. Then, when that night had passed, the Venerable Kumārakassapa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Kumārakassapa said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, this night a certain deity, when the night was far advanced, of surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Andhavana, approached me; having approached, that deity stood to one side. Standing to one side, venerable sir, that deity said this to me: “Monk, monk, this anthill smokes by night and blazes by day. The brahmin says thus: ‘Dig, O wise one, taking up the sword.’” The wise one, digging, taking up the sword… This, venerable sir, is what that deity said. Having said this, that deity vanished right there. Now, venerable sir, what is the anthill? What is the smoking by night? What is the blazing by day? Who is the brahmin? Who is the wise one? What is the sword? What is the digging? What is the bar? What is the frog? What is the forked path? What is the strainer? What is the tortoise? What is the butcher’s knife and block? What is the lump of meat? What is the nāga?'

251. “‘Vammiko’ti [P 1.0144] kho, bhikkhu, imassetaṃ cātumahābhūtikassa cātummahābhūtikassa (sī. syā. pī.) kāyassa adhivacanaṃ, mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādana-parimaddanabhedana-viddhaṃsana-dhammassa.

251. 'Anthill,' monk, is a designation for this body composed of the four great elements, born of mother and father, nourished by rice and gruel, subject to impermanence, to anointing, to massaging, to breaking up, and to disintegration.

“Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, divā kammante kammantaṃ (ka.) ārabbha rattiṃ anuvitakketi anuvicāreti – ayaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyanā. Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, rattiṃ anuvitakketvā anuvicāretvā divā kammante payojeti kāyena vācāya ‘manasā’ ( ) natthi (sī. syā.) – ayaṃ divā pajjalanā.

That which, monk, one ponders and reflects upon by night concerning the day’s work—this is the smoking by night. That which, monk, one puts into practice by day with body, speech, and mind after having pondered and reflected upon it by night—this is the blazing by day.

“‘Brāhmaṇo’ti [V 1.0199] kho, bhikkhu, tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. ‘Sumedho’ti kho bhikkhu sekkhassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacanaṃ.

'Brahmin,' monk, is a designation for the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. 'Wise one,' monk, is a designation for a monk in training.

“‘Sattha’nti kho, bhikkhu, ariyāyetaṃ paññāya adhivacanaṃ. ‘Abhikkhaṇa’nti kho, bhikkhu, vīriyārambhassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

'Sword,' monk, is a designation for noble wisdom. 'Digging,' monk, is a designation for the arousing of energy.

“‘Laṅgī’ti kho, bhikkhu, avijjāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa laṅgiṃ, pajaha avijjaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Bar,' monk, is a designation for ignorance. Remove the bar, abandon ignorance; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Uddhumāyikā’ti kho, bhikkhu, kodhūpāyāsassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa uddhumāyikaṃ, pajaha kodhūpāyāsaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Frog,' monk, is a designation for anger and vexation. Remove the frog, abandon anger and vexation; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Dvidhāpatho’ti [M 1.0198] kho, bhikkhu, vicikicchāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa dvidhāpathaṃ, pajaha vicikicchaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Forked path,' monk, is a designation for doubt. Remove the forked path, abandon doubt; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Caṅgavāra’nti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kāmacchandanīvaraṇassa, byāpādanīvaraṇassa, thīnamiddhanīvaraṇassa, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇassa, vicikicchānīvaraṇassa. Ukkhipa caṅgavāraṃ, pajaha pañca nīvaraṇe[T 1.0286]; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Strainer,' monk, is a designation for these five hindrances, namely: the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, and the hindrance of doubt. Remove the strainer, abandon the five hindrances; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Kummo’ti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ adhivacanaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandhassa, vedanupādānakkhandhassa, saññupādānakkhandhassa, saṅkhārupādānakkhandhassa, viññāṇupādānakkhandhassa. Ukkhipa kummaṃ, pajaha pañcupādānakkhandhe; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Tortoise,' monk, is a designation for these five aggregates subject to clinging, namely: the form aggregate subject to clinging, the feeling aggregate subject to clinging, the perception aggregate subject to clinging, the formations aggregate subject to clinging, and the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. Remove the tortoise, abandon the five aggregates subject to clinging; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Asisūnā’ti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ – cakkhuviññeyyānaṃ rūpānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ piyarūpānaṃ kāmūpasaṃhitānaṃ rajanīyānaṃ, sotaviññeyyānaṃ saddānaṃ…pe… ghānaviññeyyānaṃ gandhānaṃ…pe… jivhāviññeyyānaṃ rasānaṃ…pe… kāyaviññeyyānaṃ [V 1.0200] phoṭṭhabbānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ piyarūpānaṃ kāmūpasaṃhitānaṃ [P 1.0145] rajanīyānaṃ. Ukkhipa asisūnaṃ, pajaha pañca kāmaguṇe; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Butcher’s knife and block,' monk, is a designation for these five cords of sensual pleasure: forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, and arousing passion; sounds cognizable by the ear... smells cognizable by the nose... tastes cognizable by the tongue... tactile objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, and arousing passion. Remove the butcher’s knife and block, abandon the five cords of sensual pleasure; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Maṃsapesī’ti kho, bhikkhu, nandīrāgassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa maṃsapesiṃ, pajaha nandīrāgaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

'Lump of meat,' monk, is a designation for delight and lust. Remove the lump of meat, abandon delight and lust; dig, O wise one, taking up the sword—this is its meaning.

“‘Nāgo’ti kho, bhikkhu, khīṇāsavassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacanaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu nāgo, mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesi; namo karohi nāgassāti ayametassa attho”ti.

'Nāga,' monk, is a designation for a monk whose taints are destroyed. Let the nāga be, do not harm the nāga; pay homage to the nāga—this is its meaning.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā kumārakassapo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

This the Blessed One said. The Venerable Kumārakassapa was gratified and delighted with the Blessed One's words.

Vammikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Anthill Sutta, the third, is finished.

4. Rathavinītasuttaṃ

4. The Relay Chariots Sutta

252. Evaṃ [T 1.0287][M 1.0199][V 1.0201] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho sambahulā jātibhūmakā bhikkhū jātibhūmiyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca –

252. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Sanctuary. Then a number of bhikkhus from Jātibhūmi, having completed the rains residence in Jātibhūmi, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then addressed those bhikkhus who were sitting to one side:

“Ko nu kho, bhikkhave, jātibhūmiyaṃ jātibhūmakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ evaṃ sambhāvito – ‘attanā ca appiccho appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca santuṭṭho santuṭṭhikathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca pavivitto pavivekakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho asaṃsaggakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo vīriyārambhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca sīlasampanno sīlasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca samādhisampanno samādhisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca paññāsampanno paññāsampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca vimuttisampanno vimuttisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, ovādako viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako [P 1.0146] sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīna’”nti? “Puṇṇo nāma, bhante, āyasmā mantāṇiputto [T 1.0288] jātibhūmiyaṃ jātibhūmakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ evaṃ sambhāvito – ‘attanā ca appiccho appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca santuṭṭho…pe… ovādako viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīna’”nti.

“Bhikkhus, who in his native land is thus esteemed by the monks of his native land, his fellow practitioners of the holy life: ‘He himself has few desires and speaks to the bhikkhus about having few desires; he himself is content and speaks to the bhikkhus about contentment; he himself is secluded and speaks to the bhikkhus about seclusion; he himself is unentangled and speaks to the bhikkhus about being unentangled; he himself has aroused energy and speaks to the bhikkhus about arousing energy; he himself is accomplished in virtue and speaks to the bhikkhus about accomplishment in virtue; he himself is accomplished in concentration and speaks to the bhikkhus about accomplishment in concentration; he himself is accomplished in wisdom and speaks to the bhikkhus about accomplishment in wisdom; he himself is accomplished in liberation and speaks to the bhikkhus about accomplishment in liberation; he himself is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks to the bhikkhus about accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of liberation; he is an instructor, one who explains, one who demonstrates, one who incites, one who rouses, and one who gladdens his fellow practitioners of the holy life’?” “Venerable sir, it is the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta who is thus esteemed in his native land by the monks of his native land, his fellow practitioners of the holy life: ‘He himself has few desires… he is an instructor, one who explains, one who demonstrates, one who incites, one who rouses, and one who gladdens his fellow practitioners of the holy life.’”

253. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti. Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi – “lābhā āyasmato puṇṇassa mantāṇiputtassa, suladdhalābhā āyasmato puṇṇassa mantāṇiputtassa, yassa viññū sabrahmacārī satthu sammukhā anumassa anumassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, tañca satthā abbhanumodati. Appeva nāma mayampi kadāci [V 1.0202] karahaci āyasmatā puṇṇena mantāṇiputtena saddhiṃ samāgaccheyyāma samāgamaṃ gaccheyya (ka.), appeva nāma siyā kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti.

253. At that time, the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Blessed One. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Sāriputta: “It is a gain for the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, a great gain for the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, that his wise fellow practitioners of the holy life praise him point by point in the presence of the Teacher, and the Teacher approves of it. Perhaps I too might sometime meet with the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta; perhaps there might be some conversation.”

254. Atha [M 1.0200] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 1.0289] ārāme. Assosi kho āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto – “bhagavā kira sāvatthiṃ anuppatto; sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme”ti.

254. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Rājagaha for as long as he wished, set out on a journey towards Sāvatthī. Journeying by stages, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. The Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, has arrived at Sāvatthī and is dwelling there in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.”

255. Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya.

255. Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having put his lodging in order and taken his bowl and robe, set out on a journey towards Sāvatthī. Journeying by stages, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī, at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta with a Dhamma talk as he sat to one side. Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words. He rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and went to the Andhavana for his day’s abiding.

256. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “yassa kho tvaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, puṇṇassa nāma bhikkhuno mantāṇiputtassa abhiṇhaṃ kittayamāno ahosi, so bhagavatā [P 1.0147] dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena andhavanaṃ tena pakkanto divāvihārāyā”ti.

256. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Venerable Sāriputta and said to him: “Friend Sāriputta, that bhikkhu named Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, whom you were constantly praising—he has been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk. Having rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed for the Andhavana for his day’s abiding.”

Atha [T 1.0290] kho āyasmā sāriputto taramānarūpo nisīdanaṃ ādāya āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi sīsānulokī. Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Āyasmāpi [V 1.0203] kho sāriputto andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta, in a hurry, took his sitting cloth and followed closely behind the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, keeping his head in sight. Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta entered the Andhavana and sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his day’s abiding. The Venerable Sāriputta also entered the Andhavana and sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his day’s abiding.

Atha [M 1.0201] kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā puṇṇena mantāṇiputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ etadavoca –

Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, and when they had concluded their courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta:

257. “Bhagavati no, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

257. “Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?”

“Evamāvuso”ti.

“Yes, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“But friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of view?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“But friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path?”

“No [V 1.0204] hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“But friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ [T 1.0291] bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti?

“Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhatthaṃ…pe… kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ āvuso’ti vadesi. Kimatthaṃ carahāvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ [P 1.0148] vussatī”ti? “Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti.

“When you were asked, ‘Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue?’ you replied, ‘No, friend.’ When you were asked, ‘But friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind?’ you replied, ‘No, friend.’ When you were asked, ‘Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of view?’… ‘for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt?’… ‘for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path?’… ‘for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way?’… ‘Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision?’ you replied, ‘No, friend.’ For what purpose, then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?” “Friend, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“Friend, is purification of virtue final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“But friend, is purification of mind final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“Friend, is purification of view final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No [V 1.0205] hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti[M 1.0202]?

“But friend, is purification by overcoming doubt final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“Friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“But friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of the way final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“Friend, is purification of knowledge and vision final Nibbāna without clinging?”

“No hidaṃ[T 1.0292], āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“Kiṃ panāvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbāna”nti?

“But friend, is final Nibbāna without clinging apart from these states?”

“No hidaṃ, āvuso”.

“No, friend.”

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti…pe… kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi… maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi… paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi… ‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. Yathākathaṃ panāvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?

“When asked, ‘Friend, is purification of virtue final Nibbāna without clinging?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’ When asked, ‘But friend, is purification of mind final Nibbāna without clinging?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’ When asked, ‘Friend, is purification of view final Nibbāna without clinging?’ … purification by overcoming doubt … purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path … purification by knowledge and vision of the way … When asked, ‘Friend, is purification of knowledge and vision final Nibbāna without clinging?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’ When asked, ‘But friend, is final Nibbāna without clinging apart from these states?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’ But how, friend, is the meaning of this statement to be understood?”

258. “Sīlavisuddhiṃ [V 1.0206] ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya paññāpessa (sī. syā.) evamaññatthapi. Cittavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Diṭṭhivisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya[T 1.0293]. Maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva [M 1.0203] samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Aññatra ce, āvuso, imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbānaṃ abhavissa, puthujjano parinibbāyeyya. Puthujjano hi, āvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi. Tena hāvuso, upamaṃ te karissāmi; upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

258. “Friend, if the Blessed One were to declare purification of virtue to be final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be declaring that which itself has clinging to be final Nibbāna without clinging. If the Blessed One were to declare purification of mind… purification of view… purification by overcoming doubt… purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path… purification by knowledge and vision of the way… or purification of knowledge and vision to be final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be declaring that which itself has clinging to be final Nibbāna without clinging. Furthermore, friend, if final Nibbāna without clinging were to exist apart from these states, an ordinary person would attain Parinibbāna. For an ordinary person, friend, is apart from these states. Therefore, friend, I shall make a simile for you, for by means of a simile some wise persons here understand the meaning of what is said.”

259. “Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasantassa [P 1.0149] sākete kiñcideva accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ uppajjeyya. Tassa antarā ca sāvatthiṃ antarā ca sāketaṃ satta rathavinītāni upaṭṭhapeyyuṃ. Atha kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sāvatthiyā nikkhamitvā antepuradvārā paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya, paṭhamena rathavinītena dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Dutiyena rathavinītena tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ [T 1.0294] abhiruheyya. Tatiyena rathavinītena catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Catutthena rathavinītena pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Pañcamena rathavinītena chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Chaṭṭhena rathavinītena sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Sattamena rathavinītena sāketaṃ anupāpuṇeyya antepuradvāraṃ. Tamenaṃ antepuradvāragataṃ samānaṃ mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘iminā tvaṃ, mahārāja, rathavinītena sāvatthiyā sāketaṃ anuppatto antepuradvāra’nti[V 1.0207]? Kathaṃ byākaramāno nu kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā”ti?

259. “Just as, friend, if King Pasenadi of Kosala, while residing in Sāvatthī, were to have some urgent business arise in Sāketa, seven relay chariots would be stationed for him between Sāvatthī and Sāketa. Then, friend, King Pasenadi of Kosala, having departed from Sāvatthī, would mount the first relay chariot at the palace gate. By means of the first relay chariot, he would reach the second relay chariot, then dismiss the first and mount the second. By means of the second relay chariot, he would reach the third relay chariot, then dismiss the second and mount the third. By means of the third relay chariot, he would reach the fourth relay chariot, then dismiss the third and mount the fourth. By means of the fourth relay chariot, he would reach the fifth relay chariot, then dismiss the fourth and mount the fifth. By means of the fifth relay chariot, he would reach the sixth relay chariot, then dismiss the fifth and mount the sixth. By means of the sixth relay chariot, he would reach the seventh relay chariot, then dismiss the sixth and mount the seventh. By means of the seventh relay chariot, he would arrive at Sāketa, at the palace gate. When he had arrived at the palace gate, his friends, ministers, kinsmen, and relatives would ask him: ‘Great king, did you arrive from Sāvatthī to the palace gate of Sāketa by means of this relay chariot?’ How, friend, should King Pasenadi of Kosala answer in order to answer rightly?”

“Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyya – ‘idha me sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasantassa sākete kiñcideva accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ uppajji uppajjati (ka.). Tassa me antarā ca sāvatthiṃ antarā ca sāketaṃ satta rathavinītāni upaṭṭhapesuṃ. Atha khvāhaṃ sāvatthiyā [M 1.0204] nikkhamitvā antepuradvārā paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Paṭhamena rathavinītena dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Dutiyena rathavinītena tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Tatiyena rathavinītena catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Catutthena rathavinītena pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, pañcamaṃ [T 1.0295] rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Pañcamena rathavinītena chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Chaṭṭhena rathavinītena sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Sattamena rathavinītena sāketaṃ anuppatto antepuradvāra’nti. Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā”ti.

“Friend, if King Pasenadi of Kosala were to answer in this way, he would be answering correctly: ‘While I was residing here in Sāvatthī, some urgent business arose for me in Sāketa. Then, between Sāvatthī and Sāketa, seven relay chariots were prepared for me. Then, having departed from Sāvatthī from the palace gate, I mounted the first relay chariot. By the first relay chariot, I reached the second relay chariot; I dismissed the first relay chariot and mounted the second relay chariot. By the second relay chariot, I reached the third relay chariot; I dismissed the second relay chariot and mounted the third relay chariot. By the third relay chariot, I reached the fourth relay chariot; I dismissed the third relay chariot and mounted the fourth relay chariot. By the fourth relay chariot, I reached the fifth relay chariot; I dismissed the fourth relay chariot and mounted the fifth relay chariot. By the fifth relay chariot, I reached the sixth relay chariot; I dismissed the fifth relay chariot and mounted the sixth relay chariot. By the sixth relay chariot, I reached the seventh relay chariot; I dismissed the sixth relay chariot and mounted the seventh relay chariot. By the seventh relay chariot, I arrived at the palace gate of Sāketa.’ Friend, if King Pasenadi of Kosala were to answer in this way, he would be answering correctly.”

“Evameva kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi yāvadeva cittavisuddhatthā, cittavisuddhi yāvadeva diṭṭhivisuddhatthā, diṭṭhivisuddhi yāvadeva kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthā, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi [P 1.0150] yāvadeva maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva anupādāparinibbānatthā. Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti.

“In the same way, friend, purification of virtue is for the sake of purification of mind; purification of mind is for the sake of purification of view; purification of view is for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt; purification by overcoming doubt is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is path and what is not path; purification by knowledge and vision of what is path and what is not path is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way; purification by knowledge and vision of the way is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision; purification by knowledge and vision is for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging. It is for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging, friend, that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”

260. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ etadavoca – “konāmo āyasmā, kathañca panāyasmantaṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī”ti? “Puṇṇoti kho me, āvuso, nāmaṃ; mantāṇiputtoti ca pana maṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī”ti. “Acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso! Yathā taṃ sutavatā sāvakena sammadeva satthusāsanaṃ ājānantena, evameva āyasmatā [V 1.0208] puṇṇena mantāṇiputtena gambhīrā [T 1.0296] gambhīrapañhā anumassa anumassa byākatā. Lābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, ye āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ labhanti dassanāya, labhanti payirūpāsanāya. Celaṇḍukena celaṇḍakena (ka.), celaṇḍupekena (?) cepi sabrahmacārī āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ [M 1.0205] muddhanā pariharantā labheyyuṃ dassanāya, labheyyuṃ payirūpāsanāya, tesampi lābhā tesampi suladdhaṃ, amhākampi lābhā amhākampi suladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ labhāma dassanāya, labhāma payirūpāsanāyā”ti.

260. When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta: “What is the venerable one’s name, and how do your companions in the holy life know you?” “Friend, my name is Puṇṇa, and my companions in the holy life know me as Mantāṇiputta.” “It is wonderful, friend! It is marvelous, friend! Just as a learned disciple who rightly knows the Teacher’s Dispensation should answer, so has the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having penetrated each point, answered these deep, deep questions. It is a gain for his companions in the holy life, a great gain for his companions in the holy life, who get to see and attend upon the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta. Even if his companions in the holy life were to carry the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta on their heads with a cloth cushion to get to see and attend upon him, it would be a gain for them, a great gain for them. It is a gain for us, a great gain for us, that we get to see and attend upon the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta.”

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “ko nāmo āyasmā, kathañca panāyasmantaṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī”ti? “Upatissoti kho me, āvuso, nāmaṃ; sāriputtoti ca pana maṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī”ti. “Satthukappena vata kira, bho kho (ka.), sāvakena saddhiṃ mantayamānā na jānimha – ‘āyasmā sāriputto’ti. Sace hi mayaṃ jāneyyāma ‘āyasmā sāriputto’ti, ettakampi no nappaṭibhāseyya nappaṭibheyya (?). Acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso! Yathā taṃ sutavatā sāvakena sammadeva satthusāsanaṃ ājānantena, evameva āyasmatā sāriputtena gambhīrā gambhīrapañhā anumassa anumassa pucchitā. Lābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ suladdhalābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, ye āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ labhanti dassanāya, labhanti payirūpāsanāya. Celaṇḍukena cepi sabrahmacārī āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ muddhanā pariharantā [T 1.0297] labheyyuṃ dassanāya, labheyyuṃ payirūpāsanāya, tesampi [P 1.0151] lābhā tesampi suladdhaṃ, amhākampi lābhā amhākampi suladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ labhāma dassanāya, labhāma payirūpāsanāyā”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “What is the venerable one’s name, and how do your companions in the holy life know you?” “Friend, my name is Upatissa, and my companions in the holy life know me as Sāriputta.” “Indeed, sir, while conversing with a disciple comparable to the Teacher, we did not know it was ‘the Venerable Sāriputta.’ For if we had known it was ‘the Venerable Sāriputta,’ even this much would not have occurred to us. It is wonderful, friend! It is marvelous, friend! Just as a learned disciple who rightly knows the Teacher’s Dispensation should ask, so has the Venerable Sāriputta, having penetrated each point, asked these deep, deep questions. It is a gain for his companions in the holy life, a great gain for his companions in the holy life, who get to see and attend upon the Venerable Sāriputta. Even if his companions in the holy life were to carry the Venerable Sāriputta on their heads with a cloth cushion to get to see and attend upon him, it would be a gain for them, a great gain for them. It is a gain for us, a great gain for us, that we get to see and attend upon the Venerable Sāriputta.”

Itiha te ubhopi mahānāgā aññamaññassa subhāsitaṃ samanumodiṃsūti.

Thus, both of those great beings rejoiced in each other’s well-spoken words.

Rathavinītasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Discourse on the Relay of Chariots, the fourth, is concluded.

5. Nivāpasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Bait

261. Evaṃ [T 1.0298][V 1.0209] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

261. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” they replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Na[M 1.0206], bhikkhave, nevāpiko nivāpaṃ nivapati migajātānaṃ – ‘imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ migajātā paribhuñjantā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ yāpentū’ti. Evañca kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko nivāpaṃ nivapati migajātānaṃ – ‘imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ migajātā anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissanti, anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjissanti, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjissanti, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissanti imasmiṃ nivāpe’ti.

“Bhikkhus, a hunter does not set out bait for the deer thinking, ‘May the deer who feed on this bait I have set out live long, be beautiful, and endure for a long time.’ Rather, bhikkhus, a hunter sets out bait for the deer thinking, ‘The deer, approaching and becoming infatuated with this bait I have set out, will eat the food. While eating the food, approaching and becoming infatuated, they will become intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they will become negligent. Being negligent, they will be at my disposal in this bait.’”

262. “Tatra, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

262. “There, bhikkhus, the first group of deer, approaching and becoming infatuated with that bait laid out by the hunter, ate the food. While eating the food, approaching and becoming infatuated, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became negligent. Being negligent, they were at the disposal of the hunter in that bait. In this way, bhikkhus, the first group of deer did not escape from the hunter’s power.

263. “Tatra, bhikkhave, dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho [T 1.0299] te paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā [P 1.0152] ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni [V 1.0210] ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse, tiṇodakasaṅkhaye, adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa paccāgamiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

263. “There, bhikkhus, the second group of deer reflected thus: ‘The first group of deer, approaching and becoming infatuated with that bait laid out by the hunter, ate the food. While eating the food, approaching and becoming infatuated, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became negligent. Being negligent, they were at the disposal of the hunter in that bait. In this way, the first group of deer did not escape from the hunter’s power. What if we were to completely abstain from eating the bait, abstain from food involving danger, and dwell having plunged into the wilderness?’ They completely abstained from eating the bait, abstained from food involving danger, and dwelled having plunged into the wilderness. But when the last month of the hot season arrived, when grass and water were scarce, their bodies became extremely emaciated. With their bodies extremely emaciated, their strength and vigor waned. With their strength and vigor waned, they returned to that very bait laid out by the hunter. There, approaching and becoming infatuated, they ate the food. While eating the food, approaching and becoming infatuated, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became negligent. Being negligent, they were at the disposal of the hunter in that bait. In this way, bhikkhus, the second group of deer also did not escape from the hunter’s power.

264. “Tatra[M 1.0207], bhikkhave, tatiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā [T 1.0300] amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmāti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse tiṇodakasaṅkhaye adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa paccāgamiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya [P 1.0153] āsayaṃ kappeyyāma. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja [T 1.0301] amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā [V 1.0211] na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

264. “Bhikkhus, the third group of deer reflected thus: ‘Those first deer who approached the bait laid out by the hunter… and so on… thus, that first group of deer did not escape from the hunter’s power. And the second group of deer also reflected thus: “Those first deer who approached the bait laid out by the hunter… and so on… thus, that first group of deer did not escape from the hunter’s power. What if we were to abstain completely from eating the bait? Having abstained from eating out of fear, we could enter the forest wilderness and dwell there.” They abstained completely from eating the bait. Having abstained from eating out of fear, they entered the forest wilderness and dwelt there. In the last month of the hot season, when grass and water were scarce, their bodies became extremely emaciated. Their bodies having become extremely emaciated, their strength and energy waned. When their strength and energy had waned, they returned to that very bait laid out by the hunter. There, they approached and ate the food with infatuation. Approaching it and eating the food with infatuation, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became negligent. Being negligent, they were at the disposal of the hunter in that bait. Thus, that second group of deer also did not escape from the hunter’s power. What if we were to make our dwelling depending on this bait laid out by the hunter? Having made our dwelling there, we will eat the food—that bait laid out by the hunter—without approaching it and without becoming infatuated. Eating the food without approaching it and without becoming infatuated, we will not become intoxicated. Not being intoxicated, we will not become negligent. Not being negligent, we will not be at the disposal of the hunter in that bait.’ They made their dwelling depending on that bait laid out by the hunter. Having made their dwelling there, they ate the food—that bait laid out by the hunter—without approaching it and without becoming infatuated. Eating the food there without approaching it and without becoming infatuated, they did not become intoxicated. Not being intoxicated, they did not become negligent. Not being negligent, they were not at the disposal of the hunter in that bait.”

“Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā parajanā; imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti, na ca nesaṃ [M 1.0208] jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi daṇḍavāgurāhi (syā.) samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma – appeva nāma tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Addasaṃsu kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ agamaṃsu. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, tatiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

“Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the hunter and his company: ‘Indeed, this third group of deer is cunning and skilled in deception. Indeed, this third group of deer has psychic power; they are non-human beings. They consume this sown pasture, yet we do not know their coming or their going. What if we were to surround this sown pasture on all sides with great nets propped on stakes, covering the entire area? Perhaps then we might see the dwelling place of the third group of deer, the haunt to which they go.’ So they surrounded that sown pasture on all sides with great nets propped on stakes, covering the entire area. And indeed, Bhikkhus, the hunter and his company saw the dwelling place of the third group of deer, the haunt to which they came. Thus, Bhikkhus, even that third group of deer did not escape from the hunter's power.”

265. “Tatra, bhikkhave, catutthā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ [T 1.0302] sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu…pe… evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te tatiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā [P 1.0154] migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu…pe… evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā [V 1.0212] samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa [M 1.0209] amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

265. “Therein, monks, the fourth group of deer deliberated together thus: ‘Those first deer… thus, those first deer did not escape from the hunter's power. And those second deer… thus, those second deer also did not escape from the hunter's power. And those third deer… thus, those third deer also did not escape from the hunter's power. What if we were to make our dwelling place near that sown pasture of the hunter? Having made our dwelling place there, we would eat the food without entering that sown pasture of the hunter and without greed. Eating the food without entering and without greed, we would not become intoxicated. Being unintoxicated, we would not become heedless. Being heedful, we would not be subject to the hunter's will in that pasture.’ They made their dwelling place near that sown pasture of the hunter. Having made their dwelling place there, they ate the food without entering that sown pasture of the hunter and without greed. Eating there without entering and without greed, they did not become intoxicated; being unintoxicated, they did not become heedless; being heedful, they were not subject to the hunter's will in that pasture.”

“Tatra nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime tatiyā [T 1.0303] migajātā parajanā, imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti. Na ca nesaṃ jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīti [M 1.0210] daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma, appeva nāma tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīti daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Addasaṃsu kho nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ agamaṃsu. Evañhi te tatiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yattha agati nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca tatrāsayaṃ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā [P 1.0155] bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te yattha agati nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca tatrāsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

“Then this thought occurred to the hunter and his company: ‘Indeed, this third group of deer is cunning and deceitful. Indeed, this third group of deer has psychic power; they are non-human beings. They consume this sown pasture, yet we do not know their coming or their going. What if we were to surround this sown pasture on all sides with great nets propped on stakes, covering the entire area? Perhaps then we might see the dwelling place of the third group of deer, the haunt they frequent.’ So they surrounded that sown pasture on all sides with great nets propped on stakes, covering the entire area. And indeed, the hunter and his company saw the dwelling place of the third group of deer, the haunt they frequented. Thus, even that third group of deer did not escape from the hunter's power. What if we were to make our dwelling place in a location that is beyond the reach of the hunter and his company? Having made our dwelling place there, we would eat the food without entering that sown pasture of the hunter and without greed. Eating the food without entering and without greed, we would not become intoxicated; being unintoxicated, we would not become heedless; being heedful, we would not be subject to the hunter's will in that pasture.’ So they made their dwelling place where it was beyond the reach of the hunter and his company. Having made their dwelling place there, they ate the food without entering that sown pasture of the hunter and without greed. Eating there without entering and without greed, they did not become intoxicated; being unintoxicated, they did not become heedless; being heedful, they were not subject to the hunter's will in that pasture.”

“Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime catutthā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime catutthā migajātā parajanā. Imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti, na ca nesaṃ jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ [V 1.0213] nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma, appeva nāma catutthānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te [T 1.0304] amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Neva kho, bhikkhave, addasaṃsu nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca catutthānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyuṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘sace kho mayaṃ catutthe migajāte ghaṭṭessāma, te ghaṭṭitā aññe ghaṭṭissanti te ghaṭṭitā aññe ghaṭṭissanti. Evaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ sabbaso migajātā parimuñcissanti. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ catutthe migajāte ajjhupekkheyyāmā’ti. Ajjhupekkhiṃsu kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca catutthe migajāte. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, catutthā migajātā parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the hunter and his company: ‘Indeed, this fourth group of deer is deceitful and skilled in trickery! Indeed, this fourth group of deer has power; they are non-human beings! They consume this sown pasture, yet we do not know their coming or their going. What if we were to completely surround this sown pasture on all sides with large nets propped on poles? Perhaps we might then see the dwelling place of the fourth group of deer, where they resort.’ So they completely surrounded that sown pasture on all sides with large nets propped on poles. However, Bhikkhus, the hunter and his company did not see the dwelling place of the fourth group of deer, where they resort. Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the hunter and his company: ‘If we were to startle the fourth group of deer, they, being startled, will startle others, and those, being startled, will in turn startle still others. In this way, all the deer will completely abandon this sown pasture. What if we were to disregard the fourth group of deer?’ So, Bhikkhus, the hunter and his company disregarded the fourth group of deer. Thus, Bhikkhus, that fourth group of deer escaped from the hunter's power.

266. “Upamā kho me ayaṃ, bhikkhave, katā atthassa viññāpanāya. Ayaṃ cevettha attho – nivāpoti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Nevāpikoti kho, bhikkhave, mārassetaṃ pāpimato adhivacanaṃ. Nevāpikaparisāti kho, bhikkhave, māraparisāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Migajātāti kho, bhikkhave, samaṇabrāhmaṇānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

266. Bhikkhus, this simile has been given by me to make the meaning known. And this, herein, is the meaning: ‘The pasture,’ Bhikkhus, is a designation for the five strands of sensual pleasure. ‘The hunter,’ Bhikkhus, is a designation for Māra, the Evil One. ‘The hunter’s company,’ Bhikkhus, is a designation for Māra’s company. ‘The groups of deer,’ Bhikkhus, is a designation for ascetics and brahmins.

267. “Tatra, bhikkhave, paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni anupakhajja mucchitā [P 1.0156] bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise[T 1.0305]. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā tathūpame ahaṃ ime paṭhame samaṇabrāhmaṇe vadāmi.

267. In this case, Bhikkhus, the first ascetics and brahmins, having approached Māra's sown pasture and those worldly allurements, became infatuated and consumed those nutriments. Consuming those nutriments there with infatuation, they fell into intoxication. Being intoxicated, they fell into heedlessness. Being heedless, they became subject to Māra's will with regard to that pasture and those worldly allurements. Thus, Bhikkhus, those first ascetics and brahmins were not freed from Māra's domain. Just as that first group of deer, Bhikkhus, so do I declare these first ascetics and brahmins to be comparable.

268. “Tatra, bhikkhave, dutiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ [M 1.0211] āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise. Evañhi te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu [V 1.0214] mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmāti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Te tattha sākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, sāmākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, nīvārabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, daddulabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, haṭabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, kaṇabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, ācāmabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, piññākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, tiṇabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, gomayabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpesuṃ pavattaphalabhojī.

268. In this case, Bhikkhus, the second ascetics and brahmins considered thus: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins, having approached Māra's sown pasture and those worldly allurements, became infatuated and consumed those nutriments. Consuming those nutriments there with infatuation, they fell into intoxication. Being intoxicated, they fell into heedlessness. Being heedless, they became subject to Māra's will with regard to that pasture and those worldly allurements. Thus, those first ascetics and brahmins were not freed from Māra's domain. What if we were to abstain completely from the consumption of the pasture and from worldly allurements? Having abstained from fearful consumption, let us enter into forest abodes and dwell there.’ They abstained completely from the consumption of the pasture and from worldly allurements; having abstained from fearful consumption, they entered into forest abodes and dwelt there. There, they were eaters of greens, eaters of millet, eaters of wild rice, eaters of leather scraps, eaters of moss, eaters of broken rice, eaters of rice-scum, eaters of oil-cake, eaters of grass, and eaters of cow-dung. They sustained themselves on the roots and fruits of the forest, eating what had fallen.

“Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse, tiṇodakasaṅkhaye, adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ [T 1.0306] pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne cetovimutti parihāyi. Cetovimuttiyā parihīnāya tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa paccāgamiṃsu tāni ca lokāmisāni. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu.
