One took the Blessed One’s bowl and robe, one prepared a seat, and one set out water for the feet. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One washed his feet. Those venerable ones, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Anuruddha, who was sitting to one side:

326. “Kacci vo, anuruddhā, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci piṇḍakena na kilamathā”ti[V 1.0270]? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; na ca mayaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamāmā”ti. “Kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā”ti? “Taggha mayaṃ[M 1.0267], bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā”ti? “Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā [T 1.0388] imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe citta”nti.

326. “Anuruddhas, are you keeping well? Are you getting by? Are you not weary on account of alms-food?” “We are keeping well, Blessed One. We are getting by, Blessed One. And we are not weary, venerable sir, on account of alms-food.” “But, Anuruddhas, do you dwell in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blended like milk and water, regarding one another with loving eyes?” “Indeed, venerable sir, we dwell in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blended like milk and water, regarding one another with loving eyes.” “And how is it, Anuruddhas, that you dwell in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blended like milk and water, regarding one another with loving eyes?” “Here, venerable sir, it occurs to me: ‘It is a gain for me, it is truly well-gained by me, that I dwell together with such companions in the holy life.’ Venerable sir, in regard to these venerable ones, bodily action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private; verbal action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private; mental action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private. It occurs to me, venerable sir: ‘What if I were to set aside my own mind and conduct myself according to the will of these venerable ones’ minds?’ So, venerable sir, I set aside my own mind and conduct myself according to the will of these venerable ones’ minds. Venerable sir, our bodies are indeed diverse, but our mind, I believe, is one.”

Āyasmāpi kho nandiyo…pe… āyasmāpi kho kimilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mayhampi, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ [P 1.0207] cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe cittanti.

The Venerable Nandiya... and the Venerable Kimila also said this to the Blessed One: “For me too, Venerable Sir, it occurs thus: ‘It is a gain for me, indeed, it is well-gained for me, that I dwell together with such companions in the holy life.’ For me, Venerable Sir, towards these venerable ones, bodily action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private; verbal action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private; and mental action of loving-kindness is established, both openly and in private. To me, Venerable Sir, it occurs thus: ‘It would be good if I, having set aside my own mind, were to act according to the will of these venerable ones’ minds.’ Indeed, Venerable Sir, I, having set aside my own mind, act according to the will of these venerable ones’ minds. For, Venerable Sir, our bodies are different, but I think our mind is but one.”

“Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā”ti.

“Thus, Venerable Sir, we dwell united, rejoicing together, without dispute, having become like milk and water, looking upon one another with loving eyes.”

327. “Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharathā”ti? “Taggha mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā”ti. “Yathā [V 1.0271] kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharathā”ti? “Idha, bhante, amhākaṃ yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati so āsanāni [T 1.0389] paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, avakkārapātiṃ upaṭṭhāpeti. Yo pacchā gāmato [M 1.0268] piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso sace ākaṅkhati bhuñjati, no ce ākaṅkhati appaharite vā chaḍḍeti, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeti. So āsanāni paṭisāmeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeti, avakkārapātiṃ paṭisāmeti, bhattaggaṃ sammajjati. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeti. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpema, na tveva mayaṃ, bhante, tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindāma. Pañcāhikaṃ kho pana mayaṃ, bhante, sabbarattikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sannisīdāma. Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā”ti.

327. “Good, good, Anuruddhas! But do you, Anuruddhas, dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute?” “Indeed, Venerable Sir, we dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute.” “And how is it, Anuruddhas, that you dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute?” “Here, Venerable Sir, whoever among us returns first from the village for alms-food prepares the seats, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sets out the waste-bowl. Whoever returns last from the village for alms-food, if there are leftovers from the meal and if he wishes, he eats. If he does not wish, he either discards it where there is little green, or immerses it in water that is without living beings. He puts away the seats, puts away the drinking water and water for use, washes and puts away the waste-bowl, and sweeps the dining hall. Whoever sees the pot for drinking water, or the pot for water for use, or the pot for the privy is empty and void, he sets it up. If it is beyond his strength, having summoned a second person with a hand gesture, we set it up by linking hands. But, Venerable Sir, we certainly do not break into speech for that reason. Furthermore, Venerable Sir, every five days we sit together for the entire night for a talk on the Dhamma. It is in this way, Venerable Sir, that we dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute.”

328. “Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Atthi pana vo, anuruddhā, evaṃ appamattānaṃ ātāpīnaṃ pahitattānaṃ viharantānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, amhākaṃ appamattānaṃ ātāpīnaṃ pahitattānaṃ viharantānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

328. “Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, dwelling thus heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute, has a state superior to human states, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable dwelling, been attained?” “And why should it not be, Venerable Sir? Here, Venerable Sir, whenever we wish, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, we enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. This indeed, Venerable Sir, is the state superior to human states, the distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, the comfortable dwelling, that has been attained by us who dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds resolute.”

“Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa [T 1.0390] pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa [P 1.0208] paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

“Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this dwelling, for the calming of this dwelling, is there another state superior to human states, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable dwelling, that has been attained?” “And why should it not be, Venerable Sir? Here, Venerable Sir, whenever we wish, with the calming of applied thought and sustained thought, with internal confidence and unification of mind, without applied thought and without sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of concentration, we enter and dwell in the second jhāna. For the transcending of this dwelling, Venerable Sir, for the calming of this dwelling, this other state superior to human states, this distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, this comfortable dwelling, has indeed been attained.”

“Sādhu [V 1.0272] sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi [M 1.0269] no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhakā ca viharāma, satā ca sampajānā, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedema, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

“Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this dwelling, for the calming of this dwelling, is there another state superior to human states, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable dwelling, that has been attained?” “And why should it not be, Venerable Sir? Here, Venerable Sir, whenever we wish, with the fading away of rapture, we dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and we experience happiness with the body; we enter and dwell in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one dwells happily.’ For the transcending of this dwelling, Venerable Sir, for the calming of this dwelling, this other state superior to human states, this distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, this comfortable dwelling, has indeed been attained.”

“Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti[T 1.0391]? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

“Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this comfortable abiding, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, has another comfortable abiding been attained, a state superior to that of humans, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” “Why should it not be for us, Bhante? Here, Bhante, whenever we wish, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow, we enter and dwell in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. For the transcending of this comfortable abiding, Bhante, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, this other comfortable abiding has been attained—a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a state superior to that of humans.”

“Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [P 1.0209] upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

“Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this comfortable abiding, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, has another comfortable abiding been attained, a state superior to that of humans, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” “Why should it not be for us, Bhante? Here, Bhante, whenever we wish, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and through non-attention to perceptions of diversity, thinking, ‘Space is infinite,’ we enter and dwell in the base of the infinity of space. For the transcending of this comfortable abiding, Bhante, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, this other comfortable abiding has been attained—a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a state superior to that of humans.”

“Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma [V 1.0273] sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma…pe… sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ [T 1.0392] samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma…pe… sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma [M 1.0270] nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti.

“Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this comfortable abiding, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, has another comfortable abiding been attained, a state superior to that of humans, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” “Why should it not be for us, Bhante? Here, Bhante, whenever we wish, having completely transcended the base of the infinity of space, thinking, ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ we enter and dwell in the base of the infinity of consciousness; … having completely transcended the base of the infinity of consciousness, thinking, ‘There is nothing,’ we enter and dwell in the base of nothingness; … having completely transcended the base of nothingness, we enter and dwell in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. For the transcending of this comfortable abiding, Bhante, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, this other comfortable abiding has been attained—a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a state superior to that of humans.”

329. “Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharāma, paññāya ca no disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro. Imamhā ca mayaṃ, bhante, phāsuvihārā aññaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ uttaritaraṃ vā paṇītataraṃ vā na samanupassāmā”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Imamhā phāsuvihārā uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā phāsuvihāro natthī”ti.

329. “Good, good, Anuruddhas! But for you, Anuruddhas, for the transcending of this comfortable abiding, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, has another comfortable abiding been attained, a state superior to that of humans, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” “Why should it not be for us, Bhante? Here, Bhante, whenever we wish, having completely transcended the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, we enter and dwell in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, our taints are destroyed. For the transcending of this comfortable abiding, Bhante, for the calming of this comfortable abiding, this other comfortable abiding has been attained—a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a state superior to that of humans. And, Bhante, we do not see any other comfortable abiding higher or more sublime than this.” “Good, good, Anuruddhas! There is no comfortable abiding higher or more sublime than this.”

330. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantañca anuruddhaṃ āyasmantañca nandiyaṃ āyasmantañca kimilaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā [T 1.0393] samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo bhagavantaṃ anusaṃyāyitvā anusaṃsāvetvā (sī.), anusāvetvā (ṭīkā) tato paṭinivattitvā āyasmā ca nandiyo [P 1.0210] āyasmā ca kimilo āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ āyasmato anuruddhassa evamārocimha – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ mayaṃ lābhino’ti, yaṃ no āyasmā anuruddho bhagavato sammukhā yāva āsavānaṃ khayā pakāsetī”ti? “Na kho me āyasmanto evamārocesuṃ – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ mayaṃ lābhino’ti, api ca me āyasmantānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ ime āyasmanto lābhino’ti. Devatāpi me [M 1.0271] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ ime āyasmanto lābhino’ti. Tamenaṃ bhagavatā pañhābhipuṭṭhena byākata”nti.

330. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimila with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and departed. Then the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimila, having followed the Blessed One for a while, turned back. Then the Venerable Nandiya and the Venerable Kimila said to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Did we inform the Venerable Anuruddha thus: ‘We are attainers of these and these abiding-attainments,’ that the Venerable Anuruddha then declared this on our behalf in the presence of the Blessed One, even up to the destruction of the taints?” “The venerable ones did not inform me thus: ‘We are attainers of these and these abiding-attainments.’ Rather, it was known to me by encompassing the minds of the venerable ones with my own mind: ‘These venerable ones are attainers of these and these abiding-attainments.’ Devas also informed me of this matter: ‘These venerable ones are attainers of these and these abiding-attainments.’ That is what was answered when I was questioned by the Blessed One.”

331. Atha [V 1.0274] kho dīgho parajano yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dīgho parajano yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “lābhā vata, bhante, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo”ti. Dīghassa parajanassa yakkhassa saddaṃ sutvā bhummā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘lābhā [T 1.0394] vata, bho, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo’ti. Bhummānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā cātumahārājikā devā…pe… tāvatiṃsā devā…pe… yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā…pe… nimmānaratī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā…pe… brahmakāyikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “lābhā vata, bho, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo”ti. Itiha te āyasmanto tena khaṇena (tena layena) ( ) sī. syā. pī. potthakesu natthi tena muhuttena yāvabrahmalokā viditā saṃviditā (ka.) ahesuṃ.

331. Then the yakkha Dīgha Parajana approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the yakkha Dīgha Parajana said this to the Blessed One: “It is a gain, venerable sir, for the Vajjis, a well-gained gain for the Vajjian people, that the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells there, and also these three clansmen—the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimila.” Hearing the sound of the yakkha Dīgha Parajana, the earth devas proclaimed: “It is a gain, sirs, for the Vajjis, a well-gained gain for the Vajjian people, that the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells there, and also these three clansmen—the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimila.” Hearing the sound of the earth devas, the devas of the Four Great Kings… the devas of the Thirty-Three… the Yāma devas… the Tusita devas… the Nimmānaratī devas… the Paranimmitavasavattī devas… the devas of Brahmā’s retinue proclaimed: “It is a gain, sirs, for the Vajjis, a well-gained gain for the Vajjian people, that the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells there, and also these three clansmen—the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimila.” Thus, in that moment, in that instant, those venerable ones became known as far as the Brahmā world.

“Evametaṃ, dīgha, evametaṃ, dīgha! Yasmāpi, dīgha, kulā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, tañcepi kulaṃ ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittaṃ anussareyya, tassapāssa kulassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, kulaparivaṭṭā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ [P 1.0211] pabbajitā, so cepi kulaparivaṭṭo ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa kulaparivaṭṭassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, gāmā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi gāmo ete tayo kulaputte [M 1.0272] pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa gāmassa [T 1.0395] dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, nigamā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi nigamo ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa nigamassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, nagarā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, tañcepi nagaraṃ ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittaṃ anussareyya, tassapāssa nagarassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, janapadā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi janapado ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa janapadassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, dīgha, khattiyā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā [V 1.0275] anussareyyuṃ, sabbesānaṃpāssa khattiyānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, dīgha, brāhmaṇā…pe… sabbe cepi, dīgha, vessā…pe… sabbe cepi, dīgha, suddā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā anussareyyuṃ, sabbesānaṃpāssa suddānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sadevako cepi, dīgha, loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī pajā sadevamanussā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā anussareyya, sadevakassapāssa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Passa, dīgha, yāva ete tayo kulaputtā bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya, atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti.

“It is so, Dīgha, it is so! Dīgha, from whichever family these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that family were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that family. Dīgha, from whichever circle of relatives these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that circle of relatives were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that circle of relatives. Dīgha, from whichever village these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that village were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that village. Dīgha, from whichever market town these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that market town were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that market town. Dīgha, from whichever city these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that city were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that city. Dīgha, from whichever country these three clansmen have gone forth from the household life into homelessness, if that country were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of that country. Dīgha, if all the nobles were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of all those nobles. Dīgha, if all the brahmins… if all the merchants… Dīgha, if all the commoners were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of all those commoners. Dīgha, if this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, were to recollect these three clansmen with a confident mind, it would be for the long-term welfare and happiness of this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. See, Dīgha, how these three clansmen have undertaken the practice for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans.”

Idamavoca [T 1.0396] bhagavā. Attamano dīgho parajano yakkho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, the yakkha Dīgha Parajana rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

Cūḷagosiṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Cūḷagosiṅga Sutta, the first, is concluded.

2. Mahāgosiṅgasuttaṃ

2. The Great Gosiṅga Sutta

332. Evaṃ [T 1.0397][V 1.0276][P 1.0212] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā gosiṅgasālavanadāye viharati sambahulehi abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ – āyasmatā ca sāriputtena āyasmatā ca mahāmoggallānena āyasmatā [M 1.0273] ca mahākassapena āyasmatā ca anuruddhena āyasmatā ca revatena āyasmatā ca ānandena, aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “āyāmāvuso, kassapa, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamissāma dhammassavanāyā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca anuruddho yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāya. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantañca mahāmoggallānaṃ āyasmantañca mahākassapaṃ āyasmantañca anuruddhaṃ yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamante dhammassavanāya. Disvāna yenāyasmā revato tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – “upasaṅkamantā kho amū, āvuso āyasmantāvuso (ka.) revata, sappurisā yenāyasmā sāriputto [T 1.0398] tena dhammassavanāya. Āyāmāvuso revata, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamissāma dhammassavanāyā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā revato āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā ca revato āyasmā ca ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāya.

332. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood, together with many well-known and eminent senior disciples: the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Ānanda, and other well-known and eminent senior disciples. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna rose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached, he said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Come, friend Kassapa, let us approach the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma.” “Very well, friend,” replied the Venerable Mahākassapa to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, and the Venerable Anuruddha approached the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma. The Venerable Ānanda saw the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, and the Venerable Anuruddha approaching the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma. Having seen this, he approached the Venerable Revata. Having approached, he said to the Venerable Revata: “These good men are approaching the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma, friend Revata. Come, friend Revata, let us approach the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma.” “Very well, friend,” replied the Venerable Revata to the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda approached the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma.

333. Addasā kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantañca revataṃ āyasmantañca ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho āyasmā ānando! Svāgataṃ āyasmato ānandassa bhagavato upaṭṭhākassa bhagavato santikāvacarassa! Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso ānanda, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sabbapāliphullā (sī.) sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso ānanda, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti? “Idhāvuso sāriputta[P 1.0213], bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā [M 1.0274] sātthā sabyañjanā; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ [V 1.0277] parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti, dhātā dhatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. So catassannaṃ parisānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi appabaddhehi (sī. pī.) anusayasamugghātāya. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

333. The Venerable Sāriputta saw the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda approaching from afar. Upon seeing them, he said to the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Venerable Ānanda! Welcome, Venerable Ānanda, attendant of the Blessed One, who stays close to the Blessed One! Delightful, friend Ānanda, is the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood. The night is clear, all the sāla trees are in full bloom, and heavenly fragrances, it seems, waft around. By what kind of monk, friend Ānanda, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified?” “Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk is very learned, a repository of what has been heard, an accumulator of what has been heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and phrasing, proclaiming a holy life that is perfectly complete and pure—such teachings he has heard much, retained, recited, considered in mind, and penetrated well by view. He teaches the Dhamma to the four assemblies with well-rounded words and phrases, in a continuous flow, for the uprooting of underlying tendencies. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified.”

334. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca [T 1.0399] – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso revata, āyasmatā ānandena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso revata, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso revata, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti? “Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato, ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato, brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

334. When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Revata: “The Venerable Ānanda has explained according to his own inspiration, friend Revata. Now we ask the Venerable Revata about this matter: ‘Delightful, friend Revata, is the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood; the night is clear; the sāla trees are all in full bloom; divine scents, it seems, are wafting around. By what kind of monk, friend Revata, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified?’” “Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk delights in seclusion, is devoted to seclusion, is dedicated to internal tranquility of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a developer of empty dwellings. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified.”

335. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso anuruddha, āyasmatā revatena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso anuruddha, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso anuruddha, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti? “Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhumā puriso uparipāsādavaragato sahassaṃ nemimaṇḍalānaṃ volokeyya; evameva kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

335. When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Anuruddha: “The Venerable Revata has explained according to his own inspiration, friend Anuruddha. Now we ask the Venerable Anuruddha about this matter: ‘Delightful, friend Anuruddha, is the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood; the night is clear; the sāla trees are all in full bloom; divine scents, it seems, are wafting around. By what kind of monk, friend Anuruddha, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified?’” “Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk surveys a thousand worlds with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human. Just as, friend Sāriputta, a man with good eyesight, having gone to the top of a fine palace, could survey a thousand wheel-rims; even so, friend Sāriputta, a monk surveys a thousand worlds with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood be beautified.”

336. Evaṃ [T 1.0400][M 1.0275] vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso kassapa, āyasmatā anuruddhena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso kassapa, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso kassapa, bhikkhunā [P 1.0214] gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti? “Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca āraññiko [V 1.0278] hoti āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko hoti piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paṃsukūliko hoti paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca tecīvariko hoti tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca appiccho hoti appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca santuṭṭho hoti santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca pavivitto hoti pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho hoti asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo hoti vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti sīlasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti samādhisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti paññāsampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti vimuttisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta[T 1.0401], bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

336. When this was said, Venerable Sāriputta said to Venerable Mahākassapa: “Friend Kassapa, Venerable Anuruddha has answered according to his own inspiration. Now we ask Venerable Mahākassapa: ‘Delightful, friend Kassapa, is the Gosiṅga Sāla forest, the night is clear, all the sāla trees are in full bloom, and what seem to be divine fragrances are wafting about. What kind of monk, friend Kassapa, would adorn the Gosiṅga Sāla forest?’”

“Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk is a forest dweller himself and speaks in praise of being a forest dweller; he is an alms-goer himself and speaks in praise of being an alms-goer; he is a rag-robe wearer himself and speaks in praise of being a rag-robe wearer; he is a triple-robe wearer himself and speaks in praise of being a triple-robe wearer; he has few wishes himself and speaks in praise of having few wishes; he is content himself and speaks in praise of contentment; he is secluded himself and speaks in praise of seclusion; he is aloof from company himself and speaks in praise of aloofness from company; he is energetic himself and speaks in praise of arousing energy; he is accomplished in virtue himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in virtue; he is accomplished in concentration himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in concentration; he is accomplished in wisdom himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in wisdom; he is accomplished in liberation himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in liberation; he is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of liberation. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, the Gosiṅga Sāla forest would be adorned.”

337. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso moggallāna, āyasmatā mahākassapena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso moggallāna, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti? “Idhāvuso sāriputta, dve bhikkhū abhidhammakathaṃ kathenti, te aññamaññaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, aññamaññassa pañhaṃ puṭṭhā vissajjenti, no ca saṃsādenti saṃsārenti (ka.), dhammī ca nesaṃ kathā pavattinī hoti. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

337. When this was said, Venerable Sāriputta said to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: “Friend Moggallāna, Venerable Mahākassapa has answered according to his own inspiration. Now we ask Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: ‘Delightful, friend Moggallāna, is the Gosiṅga Sāla forest, the night is clear, all the sāla trees are in full bloom, and what seem to be divine fragrances are wafting about. What kind of monk, friend Moggallāna, would adorn the Gosiṅga Sāla forest?’”

“Here, friend Sāriputta, two monks discuss the higher Dhamma. They question one another, and in answering they enlighten one another; they do not falter, and their discussion on the Dhamma flows on. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, the Gosiṅga Sāla forest would be adorned.”

338. Atha [M 1.0276] kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso sāriputta, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti? “Idhāvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati [P 1.0215] pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā [T 1.0402] ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ majjhantikasamayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ [V 1.0279] viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Seyyathāpi, āvuso moggallāna, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṃ dussānaṃ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa. So yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupeyya. Evameva kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Evarūpena kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

338. Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, we have all answered according to our own inspiration. Now we ask Venerable Sāriputta: ‘Delightful, friend Sāriputta, is the Gosiṅga Sāla forest, the night is clear, all the sāla trees are in full bloom, and what seem to be divine fragrances are wafting about. What kind of monk, friend Sāriputta, would adorn the Gosiṅga Sāla forest?’”

“Here, friend Moggallāna, a monk has his mind under his control; he is not under the control of his mind. In the morning, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. At midday, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. In the evening, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. Suppose, friend Moggallāna, a king or a royal minister had a chest full of clothes of various colors. In the morning, whatever pair of garments he wished to wear, that he would wear. At midday, whatever pair of garments he wished to wear, that he would wear. In the evening, whatever pair of garments he wished to wear, that he would wear. So too, friend Moggallāna, a monk has his mind under his control; he is not under the control of his mind. In the morning, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. At midday, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. In the evening, whatever meditative dwelling he wishes to attain, that he attains. By such a monk, friend Moggallāna, the Gosiṅga Sāla forest would be adorned.”

339. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto te āyasmante etadavoca – “byākataṃ kho, āvuso, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Āyāmāvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ [M 1.0277] bhagavato [T 1.0403] ārocessāma. Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te āyasmanto āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho te āyasmanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantañca revataṃ āyasmantañca ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ [P 1.0216] ānandaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘etu kho āyasmā ānando! Svāgataṃ āyasmato ānandassa bhagavato upaṭṭhākassa bhagavato santikāvacarassa! Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso ānanda, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso ānanda, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā ānando maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso, sāriputta, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo…pe… anusayasamugghātāya. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ [V 1.0280] sobheyyā’”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ ānandova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Ānando hi, sāriputta, bahussuto sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ [T 1.0404] brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti, dhātā, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. So catassannaṃ parisānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi anusayasamugghātāyā”ti.

339. Then the Venerable Sāriputta said this to those venerable ones: “Friends, we have all answered according to our own understanding. Come, friends, let us approach the Blessed One. Having approached, we shall report this matter to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so shall we remember it.” “Yes, friend,” those venerable ones replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. Then those venerable ones approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I saw the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda coming from a distance. Having seen them, I said this to the Venerable Ānanda: ‘Come, Venerable Ānanda! Welcome to the Venerable Ānanda, the Blessed One’s attendant who dwells near the Blessed One! The Gosiṅga Sāla forest is delightful, friend Ānanda, the night is clear, the sāla trees are all in full bloom, and it seems that divine fragrances are wafting. By what kind of monk, friend Ānanda, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Ānanda said this to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk is very learned, a bearer of what has been heard... for the uprooting of underlying tendencies. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned.’ ” “Good, good, Sāriputta! Just as Ānanda, answering correctly, would answer, so has he answered. For Ānanda, Sāriputta, is very learned, a bearer of what has been heard, an accumulator of what has been heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure—such teachings have been much heard by him, retained, recited verbally, examined with the mind, and well penetrated by view. He teaches the Dhamma to the four assemblies with well-rounded words and phrases, uninterrupted, for the uprooting of underlying tendencies.”

340. “Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso revata āyasmatā ānandena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pucchāma – ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso revata, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā maññe gandhā sampavanti. Kathaṃrūpena, āvuso revata, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā revato maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta bhikkhu paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato[M 1.0278], ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto, anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato, brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ revatova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Revato hi, sāriputta, paṭisallānārāmo paṭisallānarato, ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārāna”nti.

340. “When this was said, venerable sir, I said this to the Venerable Revata: ‘Friend Revata, the Venerable Ānanda has answered according to his own understanding. Now we ask the Venerable Revata: The Gosiṅga Sāla forest is delightful, friend Revata, the night is clear, the sāla trees are all in full bloom, and it seems that divine fragrances are wafting. By what kind of monk, friend Revata, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Revata said this to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk delights in seclusion, is devoted to seclusion, is committed to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a cultivator of empty dwellings. By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned.’ ” “Good, good, Sāriputta! Just as Revata, answering correctly, would answer, so has he answered. For Revata, Sāriputta, delights in seclusion, is devoted to seclusion, is committed to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is a cultivator of empty dwellings.”

341. “Evaṃ [P 1.0217] vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho āvuso anuruddha āyasmatā revatena…pe… kathaṃrūpena, āvuso [T 1.0405] anuruddha, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā anuruddho maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhumā puriso…pe… evarūpena kho āvuso sāriputta bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, yathā taṃ anuruddhova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Anuruddho hi, sāriputta, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketī”ti.

341. “When this was said, venerable sir, I said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: ‘Friend Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata has answered... By what kind of monk, friend Anuruddha, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Anuruddha said this to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, surveys a thousand worlds. Just as, friend Sāriputta, a man with good sight... By such a monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned.’ ” “Good, good, Sāriputta! Just as Anuruddha, answering correctly, would answer, so has he answered. For Anuruddha, Sāriputta, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, surveys a thousand worlds.”

342. “Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso [V 1.0281] kassapa āyasmatā anuruddhena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ pucchāma…pe… kathaṃ rūpena kho, āvuso kassapa, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte bhante, āyasmā mahākassapo maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca āraññiko hoti āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko hoti…pe… attanā ca paṃsukūliko hoti…pe… attanā ca tecīvariko hoti…pe… attanā ca appiccho hoti…pe… attanā ca santuṭṭho hoti…pe… attanā ca pavivitto hoti…pe… attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho hoti…pe… attanā ca āraddhavīriyo hoti…pe… attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti…pe… attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti…pe… attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti… attanā ca vimuttisampanno [T 1.0406] hoti… [M 1.0279] attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti[P 1.0218]. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ kassapova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Kassapo hi, sāriputta, attanā ca āraññiko āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paṃsukūliko paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca tecīvariko tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca appiccho appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca santuṭṭho santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca pavivitto pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca sīlasampanno sīlasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca samādhisampanno samādhisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paññāsampanno paññāsampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttisampanno vimuttisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

342. When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: ‘Indeed, friend Kassapa, the Venerable Anuruddha has answered according to his own wisdom. Now we ask the Venerable Mahākassapa… By what kind of monk, friend Kassapa, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be beautified?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Mahākassapa said to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a monk is himself a forest-dweller and speaks in praise of being a forest-dweller; he is himself an alms-goer… a rag-robe wearer… a wearer of three robes… one of few wishes… content… secluded… unassociated… one with aroused energy… accomplished in virtue… accomplished in concentration… accomplished in wisdom… accomplished in liberation… he is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation. By such a kind of monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be beautified.’ “Good, good, Sāriputta! It is just as Kassapa, answering rightly, would answer. For Kassapa, Sāriputta, is himself a forest-dweller and speaks in praise of being a forest-dweller; he is himself an alms-goer and speaks in praise of alms-going; he is himself a rag-robe wearer and speaks in praise of wearing rag-robes; he is himself a wearer of three robes and speaks in praise of wearing three robes; he is himself one of few wishes and speaks in praise of having few wishes; he is himself content and speaks in praise of contentment; he is himself secluded and speaks in praise of seclusion; he is himself unassociated and speaks in praise of non-association; he is himself one with aroused energy and speaks in praise of the arousal of energy; he is himself accomplished in virtue and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of virtue; he is himself accomplished in concentration and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of concentration; he is himself accomplished in wisdom and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of wisdom; he is himself accomplished in liberation and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of liberation; he is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation.”

343. “Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ bhante āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso moggallāna, āyasmatā mahākassapena [T 1.0407] yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ pucchāma…pe… kathaṃrūpena, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā mahāmoggallāno maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, dve bhikkhū abhidhammakathaṃ kathenti. Te aññamaññaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, aññamaññassa [V 1.0282] pañhaṃ puṭṭhā vissajjenti, no ca saṃsādenti, dhammī ca nesaṃ kathā pavattinī hoti. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, yathā taṃ moggallānova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Moggallāno hi, sāriputta, dhammakathiko”ti.

343. When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: ‘Indeed, friend Moggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa has answered according to his own wisdom. Now we ask the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna… By what kind of monk, friend Moggallāna, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be beautified?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, two monks engage in a discussion on the Abhidhamma. They ask each other questions, and having been asked, they answer each other without getting bogged down, and their talk on the Dhamma proceeds. By such a kind of monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be beautified.’ “Good, good, Sāriputta! It is just as Moggallāna, answering rightly, would answer. For Moggallāna, Sāriputta, is a speaker on the Dhamma.”

344. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atha khvāhaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso sāriputta, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni [M 1.0280] mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ pucchāma – ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti. Kathaṃrūpena, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso, moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ [T 1.0408] viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Seyyathāpi, āvuso moggallāna, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṃ dussānaṃ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa. So yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ[P 1.0219], taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupeyya. Evameva kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Evarūpena kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, moggallāna! Yathā taṃ sāriputtova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Sāriputto hi, moggallāna, cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti no ca sāriputto cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā [T 1.0409][V 1.0283] ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharatī”ti.

344. When this was said, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to the Blessed One: “Then, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Sāriputta: ‘Friend Sāriputta, we have all explained according to our own understanding. Now we ask the Venerable Sāriputta: The Gosiṅga Sāla forest is delightful, friend Sāriputta, the night is clear, the sāla trees are in full bloom, and divine fragrances, I think, are wafting. By what kind of monk, friend Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Sāriputta said to me: ‘Here, friend Moggallāna, a monk has his mind under his control and is not under the control of his mind. Whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the morning, he abides in that abiding during the morning; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the midday, he abides in that abiding during the midday; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the evening, he abides in that abiding during the evening. Just as, friend Moggallāna, a king or a royal minister might have a chest full of garments of various hues. Whatever pair of garments he wishes to put on in the morning, he puts on that very pair in the morning; whatever pair he wishes to put on at midday, he puts on that very pair at midday; whatever pair he wishes to put on in the evening, he puts on that very pair in the evening. In the same way, friend Moggallāna, a monk has his mind under his control and is not under the control of his mind. Whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the morning, he abides in that abiding during the morning; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the midday, he abides in that abiding during the midday; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the evening, he abides in that abiding during the evening. By a monk of such a kind, friend Moggallāna, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned.’” “Good, good, Moggallāna! Sāriputta has answered just as he would when answering correctly. For Sāriputta, Moggallāna, has his mind under his control and is not under the control of his mind. Whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the morning, he abides in that abiding during the morning; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the midday, he abides in that abiding during the midday; whatever abiding he wishes to abide in during the evening, he abides in that abiding during the evening.”

345. Evaṃ [M 1.0281] vutte, āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kassa nu kho, bhante, subhāsita”nti? “Sabbesaṃ vo, sāriputta, subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena. Api ca mamapi suṇātha yathārūpena bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyya. Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ pallaṅkaṃ bhindissāmi yāva me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccissatī’ti. Evarūpena kho, sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā”ti.

345. When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Whose words, venerable sir, were well spoken?” “All of your words, Sāriputta, were well spoken, each in its own way. Nevertheless, listen to me as well as to the kind of monk by whom the Gosiṅga Sāla forest would be adorned. Here, Sāriputta, a monk, after his meal, on his return from the alms round, sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him, making the resolve: ‘I shall not break this cross-legged posture until my mind is liberated from the taints without clinging.’ By a monk of such a kind, Sāriputta, would the Gosiṅga Sāla forest be adorned.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te āyasmanto te bhikkhū (ka.) bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Those venerable ones, delighted, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Mahāgosiṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Great Gosiṅga Sutta, the second, is concluded.

3. Mahāgopālakasuttaṃ

3. The Great Cowherd Sutta

346. Evaṃ [T 1.0410][V 1.0284][P 1.0220] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

346. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. There, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks.” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Ekādasahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako abhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ phātikattuṃ (sī. pī.), phātikātuṃ (syā. kaṃ.). Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, gopālako na rūpaññū hoti, na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā sāṭetā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) hoti, na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, na titthaṃ jānāti, na pītaṃ jānāti, na vīthiṃ jānāti, na gocarakusalo hoti anavasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako abhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye [M 1.0282] vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti, na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, na titthaṃ jānāti, na pītaṃ jānāti, na vīthiṃ jānāti, na gocarakusalo hoti, anavasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te [T 1.0411] bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

“Bhikkhus, a cowherd endowed with eleven factors is incapable of tending to a herd of cattle and causing it to prosper. With which eleven? Here, bhikkhus, a cowherd is not one who knows forms, is not skilled in characteristics, is not one who removes fly-eggs, is not one who covers wounds, is not one who makes smoke, does not know the ford, does not know what has been drunk, does not know the path, is not skilled in grazing grounds, and is one who milks dry. He is not one who honors with extra veneration those bulls who are the fathers and leaders of the herd. Bhikkhus, a cowherd endowed with these eleven factors is incapable of tending to a herd of cattle and causing it to prosper. In the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with eleven qualities is incapable of attaining growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline. With which eleven? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who knows form, is not skilled in characteristics, is not one who removes unwholesome thoughts, is not one who covers wounds, is not one who makes smoke, does not know the ford, does not know what has been drunk, does not know the path, is not skilled in the grazing ground, and is one who milks dry. He is not one who honors with extra veneration those bhikkhus who are elders, of long standing, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha.”

347. “Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘cattāri mahābhūtāni, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti.

347. “And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not one who knows form? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not understand as it really is whatever form there is, all form, as: ‘The four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements.’ In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who knows form.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘kammalakkhaṇo [V 1.0285] bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍito’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not skilled in characteristics? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not understand as it really is: ‘A fool is characterized by his kamma, a wise person is characterized by his kamma.’ In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not skilled in characteristics.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ adhivāseti, nappajahati na vinodeti na byantī karoti na anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme adhivāseti, nappajahati [P 1.0221] na vinodeti na byantī karoti na anabhāvaṃ gameti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not one who removes unwholesome thoughts? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endures an arisen thought of sensuality; he does not abandon it, does not dispel it, does not bring it to an end, and does not cause it to go to non-existence. He endures an arisen thought of ill will… he endures an arisen thought of cruelty… he endures arisen evil, unwholesome states; he does not abandon them, does not dispel them, does not bring them to an end, and does not cause them to go to non-existence. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who removes unwholesome thoughts.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati [T 1.0412] cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na [M 1.0283] rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not one who covers wounds? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, grasps its signs and features. Inasmuch as evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow into him who dwells with the eye faculty unrestrained, he does not practice for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… Having smelled an odor with the nose… Having tasted a flavor with the tongue… Having touched a tangible with the body… Having cognized a mental object with the mind, he grasps its signs and features. Inasmuch as evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow into him who dwells with the mind faculty unrestrained, he does not practice for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who covers wounds.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ na vitthārena paresaṃ desetā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not one who makes smoke? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who teaches the Dhamma in detail to others as he has heard it and as he has learned it. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not one who makes smoke.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na titthaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā na paripucchati, na paripañhati – ‘idaṃ, bhante, kathaṃ? Imassa ko attho’ti? Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva na vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca na uttānī karonti, anekavihitesu [V 1.0286] ca kaṅkhāṭhānīyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṃ na paṭivinodenti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na titthaṃ jānāti.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu not know the ford? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not from time to time approach those bhikkhus who are of great learning, versed in the scriptures, upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, and upholders of the Mātikās, and question them and inquire: ‘How is this, venerable sirs? What is its meaning?’ To him, those venerable ones do not reveal what has not been revealed, do not make plain what has not been made plain, and do not dispel doubt concerning many doubtful points in the teachings. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not know the ford.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na pītaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne na labhati atthavedaṃ, na labhati dhammavedaṃ, na labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na pītaṃ jānāti.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu not know what has been drunk? Here, bhikkhus, when the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata is being taught, a bhikkhu does not gain inspiration from the meaning, does not gain inspiration from the Dhamma, and does not gain the gladness connected with the Dhamma. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not know what has been drunk.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na [T 1.0413] vīthiṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vīthiṃ jānāti.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu not know the path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not understand the Noble Eightfold Path as it really is. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not know the path.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na gocarakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave[P 1.0222], bhikkhu na gocarakusalo hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu not skilled in the grazing ground? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not understand the four establishments of mindfulness as they really are. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not skilled in the grazing ground.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anavasesadohī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saddhā gahapatikā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārenti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi, tatra bhikkhu mattaṃ na jānāti paṭiggahaṇāya. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anavasesadohī hoti.

“And how, monks, is a bhikkhu one who milks without remainder? Here, monks, faithful householders invite a bhikkhu to accept robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. But in that, the bhikkhu does not know the proper measure in accepting them. Thus, monks, a bhikkhu is one who milks without remainder.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti[M 1.0284]? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā, tesu na mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; na mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; na mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

“And how, monks, is a bhikkhu not one who honors with extra veneration those bhikkhus who are elders, of long standing, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, leaders of the Saṅgha? Here, monks, a bhikkhu does not establish bodily acts of loving-kindness towards those bhikkhus who are elders, of long standing, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha, both openly and in private; does not establish verbal acts of loving-kindness towards them, both openly and in private; does not establish mental acts of loving-kindness towards them, both openly and in private. Thus, monks, a bhikkhu is not one who honors with extra veneration those bhikkhus who are elders, of long standing, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha.”

“Imehi kho bhikkhave ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ.

“Monks, a bhikkhu endowed with these eleven qualities is incapable of attaining growth, progress, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

348. “Ekādasahi[V 1.0287], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako bhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave[T 1.0414], gopālako rūpaññū hoti, lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, titthaṃ jānāti, pītaṃ jānāti, vīthiṃ jānāti, gocarakusalo hoti, sāvasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako bhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti, lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, titthaṃ jānāti, pītaṃ jānāti, vīthiṃ jānāti, gocarakusalo hoti, sāvasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

348. “Monks, a cowherd endowed with eleven factors is capable of tending a herd of cattle and causing it to prosper. What are the eleven? Here, monks, a cowherd is one who knows forms, is skilled in characteristics, is one who removes fly-eggs, is one who covers wounds, is one who makes smoke, knows the watering place, knows what has been drunk, knows the path, is skilled in pasturage, and is one who milks leaving some behind. He is one who honors with extra veneration those bulls who are fathers and leaders of the herd. Monks, a cowherd endowed with these eleven factors is capable of tending a herd of cattle and causing it to prosper. In the same way, monks, a bhikkhu endowed with eleven qualities is capable of attaining growth, progress, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline. What are the eleven? Here, monks, a bhikkhu is one who knows forms, is skilled in characteristics, is one who removes fly-eggs, is one who covers wounds, is one who makes smoke, knows the watering place, knows what has been drunk, knows the path, is skilled in pasturage, and is one who milks leaving some behind. He is one who honors with extra veneration those bhikkhus who are elders, of long standing, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha.”

349. “Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘cattāri mahābhūtāni[P 1.0223], catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti.

349. “And how, monks, is a bhikkhu one who knows form? Here, monks, a bhikkhu understands as it really is, regarding whatever form there is, all form: ‘The four great elements, and form derived from the four great elements.’ Thus, monks, a bhikkhu is one who knows form.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lakkhaṇakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kammalakkhaṇo bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍitoti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lakkhaṇakusalo hoti.

“And how, monks, is a bhikkhu skilled in characteristics? Here, monks, a bhikkhu understands as it really is: ‘A fool is characterized by his actions, a wise person is characterized by his actions.’ Thus, monks, a bhikkhu is skilled in characteristics.”

“Kathañca[M 1.0285], bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ [T 1.0415] kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti byantī karoti anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti byantī karoti anabhāvaṃ gameti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti.

“And how, monks, is a bhikkhu one who removes fly-eggs? Here, monks, a bhikkhu does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire; he abandons it, dispels it, brings it to an end, and causes it to disappear. He does not tolerate an arisen thought of ill will... an arisen thought of cruelty... He does not tolerate any evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he abandons them, dispels them, brings them to an end, and causes them to disappear. In this way, monks, a bhikkhu is one who removes fly-eggs.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā [V 1.0288] rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti.

“And how, monks, is a bhikkhu one who covers a wound? Here, monks, when a bhikkhu sees a form with the eye, he does not grasp at its signs or its secondary features. Inasmuch as, if he were to dwell with the eye faculty unguarded, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might assail him, he practices for its restraint, he guards the eye faculty, he undertakes the restraint of the eye faculty.
