Householders, if one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously should wish: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the Tāvatiṃsa devas… the Yāma devas… the Tusita devas… the Nimmānaratī devas… the Paranimmitavasavattī devas… or the Brahmakāyika devas!’—this possibility exists, that with the breakup of the body, after death, he might be reborn into companionship with the Brahmakāyika devas. For what reason? Because he is one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ābhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ābhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

Householders, if one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously should wish: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the Ābhā devas!’—this possibility exists, that with the breakup of the body, after death, he might be reborn into companionship with the Ābhā devas. For what reason? Because he is one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parittābhānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… appamāṇābhānaṃ devānaṃ… ābhassarānaṃ devānaṃ… parittasubhānaṃ [V 1.0364] devānaṃ… appamāṇasubhānaṃ devānaṃ… subhakiṇhānaṃ devānaṃ… vehapphalānaṃ devānaṃ… avihānaṃ [M 1.0360] devānaṃ… atappānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassīnaṃ devānaṃ… akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ [T 1.0527]… ākiñcaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

Householders, if one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously should wish: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the devas of limited radiance… the devas of boundless radiance… the devas of streaming radiance… the devas of limited glory… the devas of boundless glory… the devas of refulgent glory… the devas of great fruit… the Aviha devas… the Atappa devas… the Sudassa devas… the Sudassī devas… the Akaniṭṭha devas… the devas gone to the base of the infinity of space… the devas gone to the base of the infinity of consciousness… the devas gone to the base of nothingness… or the devas gone to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception!’—this possibility exists, that with the breakup of the body, after death, he might be reborn into companionship with the devas gone to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. For what reason? Because he is one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī”ti.

Householders, if one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously should wish: ‘Oh, that through the destruction of the taints, I might in this very life realize for myself with direct knowledge, enter upon, and dwell in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom!’—this possibility exists, that through the destruction of the taints, he might in this very life realize for himself with direct knowledge, enter upon, and dwell in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. For what reason? Because he is one who practices the Dhamma and lives harmoniously.

443. Evaṃ [P 1.0290] vutte, sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti. Evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete pāṇupetaṃ (ka.) saraṇaṃ gate”ti.

443. When this was said, the brahmin householders of Sālā said to the Blessed One: "Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with sight might see forms—so too has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by the Venerable Gotama. We go for refuge to the Venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. From this day forward, may the Venerable Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life."

Sāleyyakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Sāleyyaka Sutta, the first, is concluded.

2. Verañjakasuttaṃ

2. The Verañjaka Sutta

444. Evaṃ [T 1.0528][V 1.0365] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosuṃ [M 1.0361] kho verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti’. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti.

444. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the brahmin householders of Verañjā were residing in Sāvatthī for some business. The brahmin householders of Verañjā heard: "The recluse Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, is dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. And of that Venerable Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-farer, knower of the world, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Having realized it himself through direct knowledge, he makes known this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its recluses and brahmins, with its gods and humans. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; he reveals the completely perfect and pure holy life. It is indeed good to see such Arahants."

Atha kho verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ [P 1.0291] sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavato santike [T 1.0529] nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti?

Then the brahmin householders of Verañjā approached the Blessed One. Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One and, after concluding the courteous and memorable talk, sat down to one side; some raised their joined hands in salutation towards the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some announced their name and clan in the Blessed One's presence and sat down to one side; some sat down to one side in silence. Sitting to one side, the brahmin householders of Verañjā said this to the Blessed One: "What, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, on the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a lower world, in hell? And what, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, on the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world?"

“Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti. Dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo[V 1.0366], evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

"Householders, it is because of unrighteous and uneven conduct that some beings here, on the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a lower world, in hell. It is because of righteous and even conduct that some beings here, on the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world."

“Na kho mayaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa, vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa, vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāma. Sādhu no bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā mayaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa, vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa, vitthārena atthaṃ [M 1.0362] ājāneyyāmā”ti. “Tena hi, gahapatayo, suṇātha sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ bho”ti kho verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

"We do not understand in detail the meaning of this statement spoken in brief by the Venerable Gotama, of which the meaning has not been analyzed in detail. It would be good, Venerable Gotama, if you would teach us the Dhamma in such a way that we might understand in detail the meaning of this statement spoken in brief by the Venerable Gotama, of which the meaning has not been analyzed in detail." "In that case, householders, listen and apply your minds well; I will speak." "Yes, venerable sir," the brahmin householders of Verañjā replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

445. “Tividhaṃ kho, gahapatayo, kāyena adhammacārī visamacārī hoti, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacārī visamacārī hoti, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacārī visamacārī hoti.

445. "Householders, a person is unrighteous and uneven in conduct in three ways by body, in four ways by speech, and in three ways by mind.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo[T 1.0530], tividhaṃ kāyena adhammacārī visamacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti. Luddo lohitapāṇi hatappahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu. Adinnādāyī kho pana hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ… taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti. Kāmesumicchācārī kho pana hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā… tathārūpāsu cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ kāyena adhammacārī visamacārī hoti.

"And how, householders, is a person unrighteous and uneven in conduct in three ways by body? Here, householders, a certain person is a destroyer of living beings; he is cruel, with blood-stained hands, intent on striking and killing, without compassion for all living beings. He is one who takes what is not given; he takes the wealth and property of another... that which is not given, with thievish intent. He is one who engages in sexual misconduct; he engages in intercourse with such women as are protected by their mother... Thus, householders, a person is unrighteous and uneven in conduct in three ways by body.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacārī visamacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhāgato vā… sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti. Pisuṇavāco kho pana hoti. Ito sutvā amutra akkhātā… vaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Pharusavāco kho pana hoti. Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā… tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Samphappalāpī kho pana hoti. Akālavādī… apariyantavatiṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacārī visamacārī hoti.

"And how, householders, is a person unrighteous and uneven in conduct in four ways by speech? Here, householders, a certain person is a liar. When in an assembly... he is one who speaks a deliberate lie. He is a slanderous speaker. Having heard here, he tells it elsewhere for the division of these people... he is one who speaks words that create factions. He is a harsh speaker. That speech which is thorny, rough... he is one who speaks such speech. He is an idle chatterer. He speaks at the wrong time... speaks speech that is without limit and unbeneficial. Thus, householders, a person is unrighteous and uneven in conduct in four ways by speech.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacārī visamacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti…pe… taṃ mamassā’ti. Byāpannacitto kho pana hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ime sattā haññantu vā… mā vā ahesu’nti. Micchādiṭṭhiko kho pana [V 1.0367] hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ… sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ [T 1.0531] kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacārī visamacārī hoti.

"And how, householders, is a person unrighteous and uneven in conduct in three ways by mind? Here, householders, a certain person is covetous... he covets, thinking: 'Oh, that what belongs to another would be mine!' Furthermore, he has a mind of ill will and a mental resolve corrupted by malice: 'Let these beings be killed... or let them not exist!' Furthermore, he has wrong view and a distorted perception: 'There is no result of what is given, no result of what is offered... there are no ascetics and brahmins in the world who, having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, proclaim it.' Thus, householders, a person is unrighteous and uneven in conduct in three ways by mind.

“Evaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.

"Thus, householders, on account of unrighteous and uneven conduct, some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell.

446. “Tividhaṃ [M 1.0363] kho, gahapatayo, kāyena dhammacārī samacārī hoti, catubbidhaṃ vācāya dhammacārī samacārī hoti, tividhaṃ manasā dhammacārī samacārī hoti.

446. Indeed, householders, a person is righteous and even in conduct by body in three ways, righteous and even in conduct by speech in four ways, and righteous and even in conduct by mind in three ways.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ kāyena dhammacārī samacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati. Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, yaṃ taṃ parassa… taṃ nādinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti. Kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya… tathārūpāsu na cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ kāyena dhammacārī samacārī hoti.

And how, householders, is a person righteous and even in conduct by body in three ways? Here, householders, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from taking life. With rod laid down, with weapon laid down, conscientious, endowed with mercy, he dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings. Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given... he is not one who takes what is not given with thievish intent. Having abandoned misconduct in sensual pleasures... he does not engage in such conduct. Thus indeed, householders, a person is righteous and even in conduct by body in three ways.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya dhammacārī samacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhāgato vā…pe… na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti. Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya… samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya… tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya… kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ[T 1.0532]. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya dhammacārī samacārī hoti.

And how, householders, is a person righteous and even in conduct by speech in four ways? Here, householders, a certain person, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech... he is not one who knowingly speaks falsehood. Having abandoned divisive speech... he speaks words that create harmony. Having abandoned harsh speech... he speaks such words. Having abandoned frivolous talk... he speaks at the proper time, with reason, with limits, and connected with benefit. Thus indeed, householders, a person is righteous and even in conduct by speech in four ways.

“Kathañca, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā dhammacārī samacārī hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ nābhijjhātā hoti ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa, taṃ mamassā’ti. Abyāpannacitto kho pana hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā averā abyābajjhā anīghā sukhī attānaṃ pariharantū’ti. Sammādiṭṭhiko kho pana hoti aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā dhammacārī samacārī hoti.

And how, householders, is a person righteous and even in conduct by mind in three ways? Here, householders, a certain person is not covetous. He does not covet the property of another, thinking: 'Oh, that what belongs to another would be mine!' Furthermore, he has a mind free from ill will and a mental resolve that is not corrupted: 'May these beings be free from enmity, free from ill will, free from distress! May they maintain themselves in happiness!' Furthermore, he has right view and an undistorted perception: 'There is a result of what is given, there is a result of what is offered... there are ascetics and brahmins in the world who, having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, proclaim it.' Thus indeed, householders, a person is righteous and even in conduct by mind in three ways.

“Evaṃ [V 1.0368] dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

Thus indeed, householders, on account of righteous and even conduct, some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

447. “Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti[M 1.0364]; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

447. If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: 'Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with khattiyas of great wealth!'; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with khattiyas of great wealth. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṃ gahapatimahāsālānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gahapatimahāsālānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu[T 1.0533]? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: 'Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with brahmins of great wealth... or with householders of great wealth!'; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with householders of great wealth. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkeyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: 'Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the devas of the Four Great Kings!'; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with the devas of the Four Great Kings. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ… yāmānaṃ devānaṃ… tusitānaṃ devānaṃ… nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ… paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ… brahmakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā brahmakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: 'Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the Tāvatiṃsa devas... the Yāma devas... the Tusita devas... the Nimmānaratī devas... the Paranimmitavasavattī devas... or the Brahmakāyika devas!'; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with the Brahmakāyika devas. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ābhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ābhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: 'Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the Ābhā devas!'; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with the Ābhā devas. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkheyya [V 1.0369] ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parittābhānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… appamāṇābhānaṃ devānaṃ… ābhassarānaṃ devānaṃ… parittasubhānaṃ devānaṃ… appamāṇasubhānaṃ devānaṃ… subhakiṇhānaṃ devānaṃ [T 1.0534]… vehapphalānaṃ devānaṃ… avihānaṃ devānaṃ… atappānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassīnaṃ devānaṃ… akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanūpagānaṃ [M 1.0365] devānaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

If, householders, one who is righteous and even in conduct should wish: ‘Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into companionship with the devas of Limited Radiance... the devas of Boundless Radiance... the devas of Refulgent Glory... the devas of Limited Glory... the devas of Boundless Glory... the devas of Lustrous Glory... the devas of Great Fruit... the devas of Aviha... the devas of Atappa... the devas of Sudassa... the devas of Sudassī... the devas of Akaniṭṭha... the devas who have reached the sphere of infinite space... the devas who have reached the sphere of infinite consciousness... the devas who have reached the sphere of nothingness... or the devas who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception!’; it is possible that he might be reborn into companionship with the devas who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. For what reason? Because he is one who is righteous and even in conduct.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce gahapatayo dhammacārī samacārī – ‘aho vatāhaṃ āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti; ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, ‘yaṃ so āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī’”ti.

If, householders, one who practices the Dhamma, who practices evenly, should wish: ‘Oh, that by the destruction of the taints I might, in this very life, having realized for myself with higher knowledge, attain and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom!’—that condition exists whereby by the destruction of the taints he might, in this very life, having realized for himself with higher knowledge, attain and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. For what reason? Because that person practices the Dhamma, practices evenly.

448. Evaṃ vutte, verañjakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma [T 1.0535] dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ gate”ti.

448. When this was said, the brahmin householders of Verañjā said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was covered, or point out the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with sight might see forms—in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by Master Gotama in many ways. We go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May Master Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

Verañjakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Verañjaka Sutta, the second, is concluded.

3. Mahāvedallasuttaṃ

3. The Great Discourse of Questions and Answers

449. Evaṃ [T 1.0536][V 1.0370][P 1.0292] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca [M 1.0366] –

449. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. After concluding their courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“‘Duppañño duppañño’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, duppaññoti vuccatī”ti?

“Friend, it is said, ‘one of little wisdom, one of little wisdom.’ To what extent, friend, is one said to be ‘one of little wisdom’?”

“‘Nappajānāti nappajānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā duppaññoti vuccati.

“Friend, because ‘one does not discern, one does not discern,’ for that reason one is called ‘one of little wisdom.’”

“Kiñca nappajānāti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti nappajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti nappajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti nappajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti nappajānāti. ‘Nappajānāti nappajānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā duppaññoti vuccatī”ti.

“And what does one not discern? One does not discern: ‘This is suffering.’ One does not discern: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ One does not discern: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ One does not discern: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ Because ‘one does not discern, one does not discern,’ friend, for that reason one is called ‘one of little wisdom.’”

“‘Sādhāvuso’ti kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi –

“Good, friend.” The Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika, having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the Venerable Sāriputta, asked the Venerable Sāriputta a further question:

“‘Paññavā paññavā’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, paññavāti vuccatī”ti?

“Friend, it is said, ‘a wise person, a wise person.’ To what extent, friend, is one said to be ‘a wise person’?”

“‘Pajānāti pajānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā paññavāti vuccati.

“Friend, because ‘one discerns, one discerns,’ for that reason one is called ‘a wise person.’”

“Kiñca pajānāti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti [T 1.0537][V 1.0371] pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti pajānāti. ‘Pajānāti pajānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā paññavāti vuccatī”ti.

“And what does one discern? One discerns: ‘This is suffering.’ One discerns: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ One discerns: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ One discerns: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ Because ‘one discerns, one discerns,’ friend, for that reason one is called ‘a wise person.’”

“‘Viññāṇaṃ viññāṇa’nti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, viññāṇanti vuccatī”ti?

“Friend, it is said, ‘consciousness, consciousness.’ To what extent, friend, is it called ‘consciousness’?”

“‘Vijānāti vijānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā viññāṇanti vuccati.

“Friend, because ‘it cognizes, it cognizes,’ for that reason it is called ‘consciousness.’”

“Kiñca vijānāti? Sukhantipi vijānāti, dukkhantipi vijānāti, adukkhamasukhantipi vijānāti. ‘Vijānāti vijānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā viññāṇanti vuccatī”ti.

“And what does it cognize? It cognizes what is pleasant, it cognizes what is painful, and it cognizes what is neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Because ‘it cognizes, it cognizes,’ friend, for that reason it is called ‘consciousness.’”

“Yā cāvuso, paññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā udāhu visaṃsaṭṭhā? Labbhā ca panimesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujjitvā vinibbhujjitvā (ka.) vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetu”nti? “Yā cāvuso, paññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā, no visaṃsaṭṭhā. Na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetuṃ. Yaṃ hāvuso yañcāvuso (syā. kaṃ. ka.), pajānāti taṃ vijānāti, yaṃ vijānāti taṃ pajānāti. Tasmā [P 1.0293] ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā, no visaṃsaṭṭhā. Na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetu”nti.

“Friend, as to this wisdom and this consciousness—are these phenomena conjoined or disjoined? And is it possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them?” “Friend, as to this wisdom and this consciousness—these phenomena are conjoined, not disjoined. And it is not possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them. For, friend, what one discerns, that one cognizes; and what one cognizes, that one discerns. Therefore, these phenomena are conjoined, not disjoined. And it is not possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them.”

“Yā cāvuso, paññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – imesaṃ dhammānaṃ saṃsaṭṭhānaṃ no visaṃsaṭṭhānaṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇa”nti? “Yā cāvuso, paññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – imesaṃ [M 1.0367] dhammānaṃ saṃsaṭṭhānaṃ no visaṃsaṭṭhānaṃ paññā bhāvetabbā, viññāṇaṃ pariññeyyaṃ. Idaṃ nesaṃ nānākaraṇa”nti.

“Friend, as to this wisdom and this consciousness—these phenomena being conjoined, not disjoined—what is the difference between them?” “Friend, as to this wisdom and this consciousness—these phenomena being conjoined, not disjoined—wisdom is to be developed, and consciousness is to be fully understood. This is the difference between them.”

450. “‘Vedanā vedanā’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso[T 1.0538], vedanāti vuccatī”ti?

450. “Friend, it is said, ‘feeling, feeling.’ To what extent, friend, is it called ‘feeling’?”

“‘Vedeti vedetī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā vedanāti vuccati.

“Friend, because ‘it feels, it feels,’ for that reason it is called ‘feeling.’”

“Kiñca [V 1.0372] vedeti? Sukhampi vedeti, dukkhampi vedeti, adukkhamasukhampi vedeti. ‘Vedeti vedetī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā vedanāti vuccatī”ti.

“And what does it feel? It feels what is pleasant, it feels what is painful, and it feels what is neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Because ‘it feels, it feels,’ friend, for that reason it is called ‘feeling.’”

“‘Saññā saññā’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, saññāti vuccatī”ti?

“Friend, it is said, ‘perception, perception.’ To what extent, friend, is it called ‘perception’?”

“‘Sañjānāti sañjānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā saññāti vuccati.

“Friend, because ‘it perceives, it perceives,’ for that reason it is called ‘perception.’”

“Kiñca sañjānāti? Nīlakampi sañjānāti, pītakampi sañjānāti, lohitakampi sañjānāti, odātampi sañjānāti. ‘Sañjānāti sañjānātī’ti kho, āvuso, tasmā saññāti vuccatī”ti.

“And what does it perceive? It perceives blue, it perceives yellow, it perceives red, and it perceives white. Because ‘it perceives, it perceives,’ friend, for that reason it is called ‘perception.’”

“Yā cāvuso, vedanā yā ca saññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā udāhu visaṃsaṭṭhā? Labbhā ca panimesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetu”nti? “Yā cāvuso, vedanā yā ca saññā yañca viññāṇaṃ – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā, no visaṃsaṭṭhā. Na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetuṃ. Yaṃ hāvuso yañcāvuso (syā. kaṃ. ka.), vedeti taṃ sañjānāti, yaṃ sañjānāti taṃ vijānāti. Tasmā ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā no visaṃsaṭṭhā. Na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetu”nti.

‘Friend, as to this feeling, this perception, and this consciousness—are these phenomena conjoined or disjoined? And is it possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them?’ ‘Friend, as to this feeling, this perception, and this consciousness—these phenomena are conjoined, not disjoined. And it is not possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them. For, friend, what one feels, that one perceives; and what one perceives, that one cognizes. Therefore, these phenomena are conjoined, not disjoined. And it is not possible, having separated them again and again, to make known the difference between them.’

451. “Nissaṭṭhena hāvuso nissaṭṭhena panāvuso (?), pañcahi indriyehi parisuddhena manoviññāṇena kiṃ neyya”nti?

451. ‘Friend, by the purified mind-consciousness that is divested of the five faculties, what is to be known?’

“Nissaṭṭhena āvuso, pañcahi indriyehi parisuddhena manoviññāṇena ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [T 1.0539] neyyaṃ, ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ neyyaṃ, ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ neyya”nti.

‘Friend, by the purified mind-consciousness that is divested of the five faculties, the base of the infinity of space is to be known as “infinite space”; the base of the infinity of consciousness is to be known as “infinite consciousness”; and the base of nothingness is to be known as “there is nothing.”’

“Neyyaṃ panāvuso, dhammaṃ kena pajānātī”ti?

‘But, friend, by what does one discern the phenomenon that is to be known?’

“Neyyaṃ [V 1.0373] kho, āvuso, dhammaṃ paññācakkhunā pajānātī”ti.

‘Friend, one discerns the phenomenon that is to be known with the eye of wisdom.’

“Paññā panāvuso, kimatthiyā”ti?

‘But, friend, for what purpose is wisdom?’

“Paññā kho, āvuso, abhiññatthā pariññatthā pahānatthā”ti.

‘Wisdom, friend, is for direct knowledge, for full understanding, and for abandoning.’

452. “Kati [M 1.0368][P 1.0294] panāvuso, paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāyā”ti?

452. “But how many, friend, are the conditions for the arising of right view?”

“Dve kho, āvuso, paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāya – parato ca ghoso, yoniso ca manasikāro. Ime kho, āvuso, dve paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāyā”ti.

“Friend, there are two conditions for the arising of right view: the voice of another and wise attention. These, friend, are the two conditions for the arising of right view.”

“Katihi panāvuso, aṅgehi anuggahitā sammādiṭṭhi cetovimuttiphalā ca hoti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca hoti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā cā”ti?

“But, friend, supported by how many factors does right view have liberation of mind as its fruit and benefit, and liberation by wisdom as its fruit and benefit?”

“Pañcahi kho, āvuso, aṅgehi anuggahitā sammādiṭṭhi cetovimuttiphalā ca hoti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca hoti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca. Idhāvuso, sammādiṭṭhi sīlānuggahitā ca hoti, sutānuggahitā ca hoti, sākacchānuggahitā ca hoti, samathānuggahitā ca hoti, vipassanānuggahitā ca hoti. Imehi kho, āvuso, pañcahaṅgehi anuggahitā sammādiṭṭhi cetovimuttiphalā ca hoti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca hoti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā cā”ti.

“Friend, right view supported by five factors has liberation of mind as its fruit and benefit, and liberation by wisdom as its fruit and benefit. Here, friend, right view is supported by virtue, supported by learning, supported by discussion, supported by tranquility, and supported by insight. Friend, right view supported by these five factors has liberation of mind as its fruit and benefit, and liberation by wisdom as its fruit and benefit.”

453. “Kati panāvuso, bhavā”ti?

453. “But how many kinds of existence are there, friend?”

“Tayome, āvuso, bhavā – kāmabhavo[T 1.0540], rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo”ti.

“Friend, there are these three kinds of existence: the sensual existence, the form existence, and the formless existence.”

“Kathaṃ panāvuso, āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti hotī”ti?

“But how, friend, does the production of renewed existence in the future come to be?”

“Avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ [V 1.0374] kho, āvuso, sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ tatratatrābhinandanā – evaṃ āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti hotī”ti.

“Friend, for beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, delighting in this and that—thus the production of renewed existence in the future comes to be.”

“Kathaṃ panāvuso, āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti na hotī”ti?

“But, friend, how is it that the production of renewed existence in the future does not come to be?”

“Avijjāvirāgā kho, āvuso, vijjuppādā taṇhānirodhā – evaṃ āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti na hotī”ti.

“Friend, with the fading away of ignorance, with the arising of true knowledge, and with the cessation of craving—thus the production of renewed existence in the future does not come to be.”

454. “Katamaṃ panāvuso, paṭhamaṃ jhāna”nti?

454. “But what, friend, is the first jhāna?”

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – idaṃ vuccati, āvuso, paṭhamaṃ jhāna”nti.

“Here, friend, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This, friend, is called the first jhāna.”

“Paṭhamaṃ panāvuso, jhānaṃ katiaṅgika”nti?

“But, friend, how many factors does the first jhāna have?”

“Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ pañcaṅgikaṃ. Idhāvuso, paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno vitakko ca vattati, vicāro ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca. Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ evaṃ pañcaṅgika”nti.

“The first jhāna, friend, has five factors. Here, friend, for a monk who has attained the first jhāna, applied thought occurs, sustained thought occurs, rapture occurs, pleasure occurs, and one-pointedness of mind occurs. Thus, friend, the first jhāna has five factors.”

“Paṭhamaṃ panāvuso, jhānaṃ kataṅgavippahīnaṃ kataṅgasamannāgata”nti?

“But, friend, how many factors are abandoned in the first jhāna, and with how many factors is it endowed?”

“Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ pañcaṅgavippahīnaṃ, pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ. Idhāvuso, paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno [M 1.0369] hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thīnamiddhaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīnaṃ [P 1.0295] hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti; vitakko ca vattati, vicāro ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca. Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ evaṃ pañcaṅgavippahīnaṃ pañcaṅgasamannāgata”nti.

“The first jhāna, friend, has five factors abandoned and is endowed with five factors. Here, friend, for a monk who has attained the first jhāna, sensual desire is abandoned, ill will is abandoned, sloth and torpor are abandoned, restlessness and remorse are abandoned, and doubt is abandoned; and applied thought occurs, sustained thought occurs, rapture occurs, pleasure occurs, and one-pointedness of mind occurs. Thus, friend, the first jhāna has five factors abandoned and is endowed with five factors.”

455. “Pañcimāni[T 1.0541], āvuso, indriyāni nānāvisayāni nānāgocarāni, na aññamaññassa [V 1.0375] gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ nānāvisayānaṃ nānāgocarānaṃ, na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ, kiṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ, ko ca nesaṃ gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhotī”ti?

455. “Friend, these five faculties have different ranges and different pastures, and they do not experience the range and pasture of one another. That is, the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty. Of these five faculties, friend, with their different ranges and different pastures, not experiencing the range and pasture of one another, what is their resort, and what experiences their range and pasture?”

“Pañcimāni, āvuso, indriyāni nānāvisayāni nānāgocarāni, na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ nānāvisayānaṃ nānāgocarānaṃ, na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ, mano paṭisaraṇaṃ, mano ca nesaṃ gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhotī”ti.

“Friend, these five faculties have different ranges and different pastures, and they do not experience the range and pasture of one another. That is, the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty. Of these five faculties, friend, with their different ranges and different pastures, not experiencing the range and pasture of one another, the mind is their resort, and it is the mind that experiences their range and pasture.”

456. “Pañcimāni, āvuso, indriyāni, seyyathidaṃ – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ. Imāni kho, āvuso, pañcindriyāni kiṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhantī”ti?

456. “Friend, there are these five faculties: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty. Upon what, friend, do these five faculties depend?”

“Pañcimāni, āvuso, indriyāni, seyyathidaṃ – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ. Imāni kho, āvuso, pañcindriyāni āyuṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhantī”ti.

“Friend, there are these five faculties: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty. These five faculties, friend, depend on vitality.”

“Āyu panāvuso, kiṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī”ti?

“But upon what, friend, does vitality depend?”

“Āyu usmaṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī”ti.

“Vitality depends on heat.”

“Usmā panāvuso, kiṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī”ti?

“But upon what, friend, does heat depend?”

“Usmā āyuṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī”ti.

“Heat depends on vitality.”

“Idāneva kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ evaṃ ājānāma – ‘āyu [V 1.0376] usmaṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī’ti. Idāneva pana mayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmato [T 1.0542] sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ evaṃ ājānāma – ‘usmā āyuṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Just now, friend, we understood the Venerable Sāriputta’s statement thus: ‘Vitality depends on heat.’ And just now, friend, we understood the Venerable Sāriputta’s statement thus: ‘Heat depends on vitality.’”

“Yathā kathaṃ panāvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?

“But how, friend, is the meaning of this statement to be understood?”

“Tena hāvuso, upamaṃ te karissāmi; upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, telappadīpassa jhāyato acciṃ paṭicca ābhā paññāyati, ābhaṃ paṭicca acci paññāyati; evameva kho, āvuso, āyu usmaṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, usmā āyuṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhatī”ti.

“In that case, friend, I shall give you a simile; for by means of a simile, some wise people here understand the meaning of what is said. Just as, friend, when an oil lamp is burning, radiance is discerned in dependence on the flame, and the flame is discerned in dependence on the radiance; even so, friend, vitality persists in dependence on heat, and heat persists in dependence on vitality.”

457. “Teva [M 1.0370] nu kho, āvuso, āyusaṅkhārā, te vedaniyā dhammā udāhu aññe āyusaṅkhārā aññe vedaniyā dhammā”ti? “Na kho[P 1.0296], āvuso, teva āyusaṅkhārā te vedaniyā dhammā. Te ca hāvuso, āyusaṅkhārā abhaviṃsu te vedaniyā dhammā, na yidaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyetha. Yasmā ca kho, āvuso, aññe āyusaṅkhārā aññe vedaniyā dhammā, tasmā saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyatī”ti.

457. “Friend, are those life-formations the same as the phenomena of feeling, or are the life-formations one thing and the phenomena of feeling another?” “No, friend, the life-formations are not the same as the phenomena of feeling. If, friend, those life-formations were the same as the phenomena of feeling, then the emergence of a bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling would not be discerned. But because, friend, the life-formations are one thing and the phenomena of feeling are another, therefore the emergence of a bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling is discerned.”

“Yadā nu kho, āvuso, imaṃ kāyaṃ kati dhammā jahanti; athāyaṃ kāyo ujjhito avakkhitto seti, yathā kaṭṭhaṃ acetana”nti?

“Friend, when how many phenomena abandon this body, does this body then lie discarded, cast aside, like a senseless piece of wood?”

“Yadā kho, āvuso, imaṃ kāyaṃ tayo dhammā jahanti – āyu usmā ca viññāṇaṃ; athāyaṃ kāyo ujjhito avakkhitto seti, yathā kaṭṭhaṃ acetana”nti.

“When, friend, three phenomena abandon this body—vitality, heat, and consciousness—then this body lies discarded, cast aside, like a senseless piece of wood.”

“Yvāyaṃ, āvuso, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṃ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno – imesaṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇa”nti?

“Friend, what is the difference between that being who is dead, who has passed away, and that bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling?”

“Yvāyaṃ, āvuso, mato kālaṅkato tassa kāyasaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā[T 1.0543], vacīsaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā, cittasaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā, āyu parikkhīṇo, usmā vūpasantā, indriyāni paribhinnāni. Yo cāyaṃ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno tassapi kāyasaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā, vacīsaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā, cittasaṅkhārā niruddhā paṭippassaddhā, āyu na parikkhīṇo, usmā avūpasantā, indriyāni vippasannāni. Yvāyaṃ, āvuso, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṃ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno – idaṃ nesaṃ nānākaraṇa”nti.

“Friend, for that being who is dead, who has passed away, the bodily formations have ceased and are stilled, the verbal formations have ceased and are stilled, the mental formations have ceased and are stilled, vitality is exhausted, the heat has been extinguished, and the faculties are destroyed. As for that bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, for him also the bodily formations have ceased and are stilled, the verbal formations have ceased and are stilled, the mental formations have ceased and are stilled, but vitality is not exhausted, the heat has not been extinguished, and the faculties are exceedingly clear. Friend, between that being who is dead, who has passed away, and that bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling—this is the difference between them.”

458. “Kati [V 1.0377] panāvuso, paccayā adukkhamasukhāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā”ti?

458. “Friend, how many conditions are there for the attainment of the liberation of mind that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant?”

“Cattāro kho, āvuso, paccayā adukkhamasukhāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā. Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ime kho, āvuso, cattāro paccayā adukkhamasukhāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā”ti.

“Friend, there are four conditions for the attainment of the liberation of mind that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Here, friend, a bhikkhu, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow, enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. These, friend, are the four conditions for the attainment of the liberation of mind that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant.”

“Kati panāvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā”ti?

“Friend, how many conditions are there for the attainment of the signless liberation of mind?”

“Dve kho, āvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā [M 1.0371] – sabbanimittānañca amanasikāro, animittāya ca dhātuyā manasikāro. Ime kho, āvuso, dve paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā samāpattiyā”ti.

“Friend, there are two conditions for the attainment of the signless liberation of mind: the non-attention to all signs, and the attention to the signless element. These, friend, are the two conditions for the attainment of the signless liberation of mind.”

“Kati panāvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā ṭhitiyā”ti?

“Friend, how many conditions are there for the stability of the signless liberation of mind?”

“Tayo kho, āvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā [T 1.0544] ṭhitiyā [P 1.0297] – sabbanimittānañca amanasikāro, animittāya ca dhātuyā manasikāro, pubbe ca abhisaṅkhāro. Ime kho, āvuso, tayo paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā ṭhitiyā”ti.

“Friend, there are three conditions for the stability of the signless liberation of mind: the non-attention to all signs, the attention to the signless element, and prior determination. These, friend, are the three conditions for the stability of the signless liberation of mind.”

“Kati panāvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā vuṭṭhānāyā”ti?

“Friend, how many conditions are there for emerging from the signless liberation of mind?”

“Dve kho, āvuso, paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā vuṭṭhānāya – sabbanimittānañca manasikāro, animittāya ca dhātuyā amanasikāro. Ime kho, āvuso, dve paccayā animittāya cetovimuttiyā vuṭṭhānāyā”ti.

“Friend, there are two conditions for emerging from the signless liberation of mind: the attention to all signs, and the non-attention to the signless element. These, friend, are the two conditions for emerging from the signless liberation of mind.”

459. “Yā cāyaṃ, āvuso, appamāṇā cetovimutti, yā ca ākiñcaññā cetovimutti, yā ca suññatā cetovimutti, yā ca animittā cetovimutti – ime dhammā nānātthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti?

459. “Friend, this immeasurable liberation of mind, this liberation of mind of nothingness, this liberation of mind of emptiness, and this signless liberation of mind—are these phenomena different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different?”

“Yā cāyaṃ, āvuso, appamāṇā cetovimutti, yā ca ākiñcaññā cetovimutti, yā ca suññatā cetovimutti, yā ca animittā cetovimutti – atthi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānātthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca; atthi ca kho, āvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā, byañjanameva nānaṃ”.

“Friend, regarding this immeasurable liberation of mind, this liberation of mind of nothingness, this liberation of mind of emptiness, and this signless liberation of mind—there is a way, friend, according to which these phenomena are different in meaning and different in phrasing; and there is also a way, friend, according to which these phenomena are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different.”

“Katamo [V 1.0378] cāvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānātthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca”?

“And what, friend, is the way according to which these phenomena are different in meaning and different in phrasing?”

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena [T 1.0545] cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho [M 1.0372] tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatāvuso, appamāṇā cetovimutti”.

“Here, friend, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. With a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by altruistic joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, he dwells pervading one direction, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. This, friend, is called the immeasurable liberation of mind.”

“Katamā cāvuso, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti”?

“And what, friend, is the liberation of mind of nothingness?”

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatāvuso, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti”.

“Here, friend, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of the infinity of consciousness, attending to ‘There is nothing,’ enters and dwells in the base of nothingness. This, friend, is called the liberation of mind of nothingness.”

“Katamā cāvuso, suññatā cetovimutti”?

“And what, friend, is the emptiness liberation of mind?”

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘suññamidaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā’ti. Ayaṃ [P 1.0298] vuccatāvuso, suññatā cetovimutti”.

“Here, friend, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘This is empty of self or of what belongs to self.’ This, friend, is called the emptiness liberation of mind.”

“Katamā cāvuso, animittā cetovimutti”?

“And what, friend, is the signless liberation of mind?”

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatāvuso, animittā cetovimutti. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānātthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca”.

“Here, friend, a bhikkhu, by not attending to all signs, enters and dwells in the signless concentration of mind. This, friend, is called the signless liberation of mind. This, friend, is the way according to which these phenomena are different in meaning and different in phrasing.”

“Katamo cāvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānaṃ”?

“And what, friend, is the way according to which these phenomena are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different?”

“Rāgo kho, āvuso, pamāṇakaraṇo, doso pamāṇakaraṇo, moho pamāṇakaraṇo. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā [T 1.0546] ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho, āvuso, appamāṇā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho panākuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena. Rāgo kho, āvuso, kiñcano, doso kiñcano, moho kiñcano. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho, āvuso, ākiñcaññā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho panākuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena[V 1.0379], suññā mohena. Rāgo kho, āvuso, nimittakaraṇo, doso nimittakaraṇo, moho nimittakaraṇo. Te [M 1.0373] khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho, āvuso, animittā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho panākuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti.

“Friend, lust is a measure-maker, hatred is a measure-maker, delusion is a measure-maker. For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are of a nature not to arise in the future. Insofar as there are immeasurable liberations of mind, friend, the unshakable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. And that unshakable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, and empty of delusion. Friend, lust is an impediment, hatred is an impediment, delusion is an impediment. For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are of a nature not to arise in the future. Insofar as there are liberations of mind of nothingness, friend, the unshakable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. And that unshakable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, and empty of delusion. Friend, lust is a sign-maker, hatred is a sign-maker, delusion is a sign-maker. For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are of a nature not to arise in the future. Insofar as there are signless liberations of mind, friend, the unshakable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. And that unshakable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, and empty of delusion. This, friend, is the way according to which these phenomena are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different.”

Idamavocāyasmā sāriputto. Attamano āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

This is what Venerable Sāriputta said. Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika, being pleased, delighted in the words of Venerable Sāriputta.

Mahāvedallasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Mahāvedalla Sutta, the third, is concluded.

4. Cūḷavedallasuttaṃ

4. The Cūḷavedalla Sutta

460. Evaṃ [T 1.0547][V 1.0380][P 1.0299] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho visākho upāsako yena dhammadinnā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā dhammadinnaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho visākho upāsako dhammadinnaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “‘sakkāyo sakkāyo’ti, ayye, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, ayye, sakkāyo vutto bhagavatā”ti? “Pañca kho ime, āvuso visākha, upādānakkhandhā sakkāyo vutto bhagavatā, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime kho, āvuso visākha, pañcupādānakkhandhā sakkāyo vutto bhagavatā”ti.

460. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Then the lay follower Visākha approached the bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā; having approached, he paid homage to the bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the lay follower Visākha said this to the bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā: “‘Identity, identity,’ venerable lady, it is said. Now what, venerable lady, is the identity declared by the Blessed One?” “These five aggregates of clinging, friend Visākha, are the identity declared by the Blessed One; that is—the form aggregate of clinging, the feeling aggregate of clinging, the perception aggregate of clinging, the volitional formations aggregate of clinging, and the consciousness aggregate of clinging. These, friend Visākha, are the five aggregates of clinging declared as identity by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhayye”ti kho visākho upāsako dhammadinnāya bhikkhuniyā bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā dhammadinnaṃ bhikkhuniṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “‘sakkāyasamudayo sakkāyasamudayo’ti, ayye, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, ayye, sakkāyasamudayo vutto bhagavatā”ti? “Yāyaṃ, āvuso visākha, taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā; ayaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, sakkāyasamudayo vutto bhagavatā”ti.

“Very good, venerable lady,” said the lay follower Visākha, having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā, asked her a further question: “‘The origin of identity, the origin of identity,’ venerable lady, it is said. Now what, venerable lady, is the origin of identity declared by the Blessed One?” “It is this craving, friend Visākha, which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights in this or that, namely: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. This, friend Visākha, is the origin of identity declared by the Blessed One.”

“‘Sakkāyanirodho [M 1.0374] sakkāyanirodho’ti, ayye, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, ayye, sakkāyanirodho vutto bhagavatā”ti?

“‘The cessation of identity, the cessation of identity,’ venerable lady, it is said. Now what, venerable lady, is the cessation of identity declared by the Blessed One?”

“Yo [T 1.0548] kho, āvuso visākha, tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo; ayaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, sakkāyanirodho vutto bhagavatā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, the abandoning, the relinquishing, the release from it, and the non-adherence to it—this, friend Visākha, is the cessation of identity declared by the Blessed One.”

“‘Sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti, ayye, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, ayye, sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā vuttā bhagavatā”ti?

“‘The path leading to the cessation of identity, the path leading to the cessation of identity,’ venerable lady, it is said. Now what, venerable lady, is the path leading to the cessation of identity declared by the Blessed One?”

“Ayameva kho, āvuso visākha, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṃ [V 1.0381] – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhī”ti.

“It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend Visākha, that has been declared by the Blessed One as the path leading to the cessation of identity; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.”

“Taññeva nu kho, ayye, upādānaṃ te teva (sī.) pañcupādānakkhandhā udāhu aññatra pañcahupādānakkhandhehi upādāna”nti? “Na kho, āvuso visākha, taññeva upādānaṃ te pañcupādānakkhandhā, nāpi [P 1.0300] aññatra pañcahupādānakkhandhehi upādānaṃ. Yo kho, āvuso visākha, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu chandarāgo taṃ tattha upādāna”nti.

“Venerable lady, is that clinging the same as the five aggregates of clinging, or is clinging something apart from the five aggregates of clinging?” “Friend Visākha, clinging is not the same as the five aggregates of clinging, nor is clinging something apart from the five aggregates of clinging. But, friend Visākha, whatever desire and lust there is regarding the five aggregates of clinging—that is the clinging in that case.”

461. “Kathaṃ panāyye, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti? “Idhāvuso visākha, assutavā puthujjano, ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto, rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Evaṃ kho[T 1.0549], āvuso visākha, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti.

461. “But how, venerable lady, does identity view come to be?” “Here, friend Visākha, an uninstructed worldling, who does not see the noble ones, is unskilled in the noble Dhamma, and is undisciplined in the noble Dhamma; who does not see true persons, is unskilled in the Dhamma of true persons, and is undisciplined in the Dhamma of true persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He regards feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. This, friend Visākha, is how identity view comes to be.”

“Kathaṃ panāyye, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti?

“And how, venerable lady, does identity view not come to be?”

“Idhāvuso visākha, sutavā ariyasāvako, ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto, na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Na vedanaṃ…pe… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre…pe… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ[M 1.0375], na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti.

“Here, friend Visākha, an instructed noble disciple, who sees the noble ones, is skilled in the noble Dhamma, and is well-disciplined in the noble Dhamma; who sees true persons, is skilled in the Dhamma of true persons, and is well-disciplined in the Dhamma of true persons, does not regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He does not regard feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. This, friend Visākha, is how identity view does not come to be.”

462. “Katamo panāyye, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo”ti?

462. “And what, venerable lady, is the Noble Eightfold Path?”

“Ayameva kho, āvuso visākha, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto [V 1.0382] sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhī”ti. “Ariyo panāyye, aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhato udāhu asaṅkhato”ti?

“It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend Visākha; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. But, venerable lady, is the Noble Eightfold Path conditioned or unconditioned?”

“Ariyo kho, āvuso visākha, aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhato”ti[P 1.0301].

“The Noble Eightfold Path, friend Visākha, is conditioned.”

“Ariyena nu kho, ayye, aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena tayo khandhā saṅgahitā udāhu tīhi khandhehi ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅgahito”ti?

“Venerable lady, are the three aggregates included in the Noble Eightfold Path, or is the Noble Eightfold Path included in the three aggregates?”

“Na kho, āvuso visākha, ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena tayo khandhā saṅgahitā; tīhi ca kho, āvuso visākha, khandhehi ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅgahito. Yā cāvuso visākha, sammāvācā yo ca sammākammanto yo ca sammāājīvo ime dhammā [T 1.0550] sīlakkhandhe saṅgahitā. Yo ca sammāvāyāmo yā ca sammāsati yo ca sammāsamādhi ime dhammā samādhikkhandhe saṅgahitā. Yā ca sammādiṭṭhi yo ca sammāsaṅkappo, ime dhammā paññākkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, the three aggregates are not included in the Noble Eightfold Path; rather, friend Visākha, the Noble Eightfold Path is included in the three aggregates. Whatever is right speech, right action, and right livelihood—these things are included in the aggregate of virtue. Whatever is right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration—these things are included in the aggregate of concentration. Whatever is right view and right intention—these things are included in the aggregate of wisdom.”

“Katamo panāyye, samādhi, katame dhammā samādhinimittā, katame dhammā samādhiparikkhārā, katamā samādhibhāvanā”ti?

“But, venerable lady, what is concentration? What qualities are the signs of concentration? What qualities are the requisites for concentration? What is the development of concentration?”

“Yā kho, āvuso visākha, cittassa ekaggatā ayaṃ samādhi; cattāro satipaṭṭhānā samādhinimittā; cattāro sammappadhānā samādhiparikkhārā. Yā tesaṃyeva dhammānaṃ āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkammaṃ, ayaṃ ettha samādhibhāvanā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, the singleness of mind is concentration; the four foundations of mindfulness are the signs of concentration; the four right exertions are the requisites for concentration. The pursuit, development, and frequent practice of these very qualities is, in this context, the development of concentration.”

463. “Kati panāyye, saṅkhārā”ti?

463. “But, venerable lady, how many formations are there?”

“Tayome, āvuso visākha, saṅkhārā – kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“Friend Visākha, there are these three formations: the bodily formation, the verbal formation, and the mental formation.”

“Katamo panāyye, kāyasaṅkhāro, katamo vacīsaṅkhāro, katamo cittasaṅkhāro”ti?

“But what, venerable lady, is the bodily formation, what is the verbal formation, what is the mental formation?”

“Assāsapassāsā kho, āvuso visākha, kāyasaṅkhāro, vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“In-breaths and out-breaths, friend Visākha, are the bodily formation; applied thought and sustained thought are the verbal formation; perception and feeling are the mental formation.”

“Kasmā panāyye, assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro, kasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, kasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti?

“But why, venerable lady, are in-breaths and out-breaths the bodily formation, why are applied thought and sustained thought the verbal formation, and why are perception and feeling the mental formation?”

“Assāsapassāsā kho, āvuso [M 1.0376] visākha, kāyikā ete dhammā kāyappaṭibaddhā, tasmā assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro. Pubbe kho, āvuso visākha, vitakketvā vicāretvā pacchā vācaṃ bhindati, tasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro. Saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā ete dhammā [T 1.0551] cittappaṭibaddhā, tasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“Friend Visākha, in-breaths and out-breaths are bodily; these phenomena are bound up with the body. Therefore, in-breaths and out-breaths are the bodily formation. First, friend Visākha, one applies thought and sustains thought, and afterwards one utters speech. Therefore, applied thought and sustained thought are the verbal formation. Perception and feeling are mental; these phenomena are bound up with the mind. Therefore, perception and feeling are the mental formation.”

464. “Kathaṃ [V 1.0383] panāyye, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti hotī”ti?

464. “But how, venerable lady, does the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling come to be?”

“Na kho, āvuso visākha, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjissa’nti vā, ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā, ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’ti vā. Atha khvāssa pubbeva tathā cittaṃ bhāvitaṃ hoti yaṃ taṃ tathattāya upanetī”ti.

“Friend Visākha, it is not that when a bhikkhu is attaining the cessation of perception and feeling, it occurs to him: ‘I will attain the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I am attaining the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I have attained the cessation of perception and feeling.’ Rather, his mind has previously been developed in such a way that it leads to such a state.”

“Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa [P 1.0302] panāyye, bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṃ nirujjhanti – yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa kho, āvuso visākha, bhikkhuno paṭhamaṃ nirujjhati vacīsaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“Venerable lady, when a bhikkhu is attaining the cessation of perception and feeling, which phenomena cease first: the bodily formation, or the verbal formation, or the mental formation?” “Friend Visākha, when a bhikkhu is attaining the cessation of perception and feeling, the verbal formation ceases first, then the bodily formation, then the mental formation.”

“Kathaṃ panāyye, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ hotī”ti?

“But how, venerable lady, does emergence from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling come about?”

“Na kho, āvuso visākha, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahissa’nti vā, ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahāmī’ti vā, ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhito’ti vā. Atha khvāssa pubbeva tathā cittaṃ bhāvitaṃ hoti yaṃ taṃ tathattāya upanetī”ti.

“Friend Visākha, it is not that when a bhikkhu is emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, it occurs to him: ‘I will emerge from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I am emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I have emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.’ Rather, his mind has previously been developed in such a way that it leads to such a state.”

“Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa panāyye, bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṃ uppajjanti – yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi [T 1.0552] vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa kho, āvuso visākha, bhikkhuno paṭhamaṃ uppajjati cittasaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato vacīsaṅkhāro”ti.

“Venerable lady, when a bhikkhu is emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, which phenomena arise first: the bodily formation, or the verbal formation, or the mental formation?” “Friend Visākha, when a bhikkhu is emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, the mental formation arises first, then the bodily formation, then the verbal formation.”

“Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṃ panāyye, bhikkhuṃ kati phassā phusantī”ti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṃ kho, āvuso [M 1.0377] visākha, bhikkhuṃ tayo phassā phusanti – suññato phasso, animitto phasso, appaṇihito phasso”ti.

“Venerable lady, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, how many contacts touch him?” “Friend Visākha, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, three contacts touch him: the emptiness contact, the signless contact, and the desireless contact.”

“Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa panāyye, bhikkhuno kiṃninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti kiṃpoṇaṃ kiṃpabbhāra”nti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa kho, āvuso visākha, bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāra”nti.

“Venerable lady, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, to what is his mind inclined, to what does it lean, to what does it tend?” “Friend Visākha, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, his mind is inclined to seclusion, it leans to seclusion, it tends to seclusion.”

465. “Kati [V 1.0384] panāyye, vedanā”ti?

465. “But, venerable lady, how many feelings are there?”

“Tisso kho imā, āvuso visākha, vedanā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.”

“Katamā panāyye, sukhā vedanā, katamā dukkhā vedanā, katamā adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti?

“But, venerable lady, what is pleasant feeling, what is painful feeling, and what is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?”

“Yaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – ayaṃ sukhā vedanā. Yaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – ayaṃ dukkhā vedanā. Yaṃ kho, āvuso visākha, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ vedayitaṃ – ayaṃ adukkhamasukhā [P 1.0303] vedanā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, whatever is felt, whether bodily or mental, that is pleasant and agreeable—this is pleasant feeling. Whatever is felt, whether bodily or mental, that is painful and disagreeable—this is painful feeling. Whatever is felt, whether bodily or mental, that is neither agreeable nor disagreeable—this is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.”

“Sukhā panāyye, vedanā kiṃsukhā kiṃdukkhā, dukkhā vedanā kiṃsukhā kiṃdukkhā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā kiṃsukhā kiṃdukkhā”ti?

“Venerable lady, in what way is pleasant feeling pleasant and in what way painful? In what way is painful feeling pleasant and in what way painful? In what way is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling pleasant and in what way painful?”

“Sukhā kho, āvuso visākha, vedanā ṭhitisukhā vipariṇāmadukkhā; dukkhā vedanā ṭhitidukkhā vipariṇāmasukhā[T 1.0553]; adukkhamasukhā vedanā ñāṇasukhā aññāṇadukkhā”ti.

“Friend Visākha, pleasant feeling is pleasant in its persistence and painful in its change; painful feeling is painful in its persistence and pleasant in its change; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is pleasant when there is knowledge and painful when there is no knowledge.”

“Sukhāya panāyye, vedanāya kiṃ anusayo anuseti, dukkhāya vedanāya kiṃ anusayo anuseti, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya kiṃ anusayo anusetī”ti?

“But, venerable lady, what underlying tendency lies dormant in pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency lies dormant in painful feeling, and what underlying tendency lies dormant in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?”

“Sukhāya kho, āvuso visākha, vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anuseti, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayo anusetī”ti.

“Friend Visākha, the underlying tendency to lust lies dormant in pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion lies dormant in painful feeling, and the underlying tendency to ignorance lies dormant in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.”

“Sabbāya nu kho, ayye, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, sabbāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anuseti, sabbāya adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayo anusetī”ti?

“Venerable lady, does the underlying tendency to lust lie dormant in all pleasant feeling, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie dormant in all painful feeling, and does the underlying tendency to ignorance lie dormant in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?”

“Na kho, āvuso visākha, sabbāya sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, na sabbāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anuseti, na sabbāya adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayo anusetī”ti.

“It is not, friend Visākha, that the underlying tendency to lust lies dormant in all pleasant feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to aversion lies dormant in all painful feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to ignorance lies dormant in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.”

“Sukhāya [M 1.0378] panāyye, vedanāya kiṃ pahātabbaṃ, dukkhāya vedanāya kiṃ pahātabbaṃ, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya kiṃ pahātabba”nti?

“But, venerable lady, what is to be abandoned in pleasant feeling, what is to be abandoned in painful feeling, and what is to be abandoned in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?”
